   of sign each pass a stand-in over as a point another stratum holds,
   the column-wide fill counts the points of its grid less the three,
   and a sign band whose grid holds one is left to the walk (G6.5a). On
   9000 to 9998 beside 10000 and 10001 G6.5a's walk took `9999`, a gap
   between two values the column holds, in one cell at seeds 0, 4 and
   9. **A STAND-IN THE COLUMN HOLDS IS ITS OWN VALUE** (plan P4-D357
   A): G5.4's draw, G6.6's width walk and every value pass above refuse
   only a stand-in the block does not publish as held -- by a
   `kept_as_a_number` decision, as its mode, as a tail block's end, or
   as two adjacent rungs of its value, which type-7 reads only off rows
   holding it (`NumericFacts.kept_stand_ins`, on every numeric block of
   every role) -- so one no published fact shows held is refused, and
   the reader's own end and rows keep the narrower set below. Refusing a held one took the heap away with nothing
   missed: `-999` 44 times beside `9999` 47 times, both published kept,
   came back in no cell; so did a compound column's numeric half
   holding `-999` in 49 rows and a joined position holding `9999` in
   41, each published only as the block's mode, and a half holding
   `-999` in 46 and a position holding `9999` in 46, published only as
   p41 to p43 and p86 to p88. The derived end and the staircase rows are the
   reader's ladder (G5.1a), which the checker's windows read from the
   numeric block alone, so they keep
   only a stand-in the block itself publishes as held -- its mode, a
   tail block's end, two adjacent equal rungs, never a decision -- and
   step off the rest: a count column holding `9999` in 12 rows, its
   mode, beside `9000` to `9990` and `10000` six times, ended its high
   tail at `9998` and the twin held the heap there at seeds 0, 4 and 9
   until they kept it. **A STEP THAT BINARY64 CANNOT TELL FROM THE
   STAND-IN IS NO STEP**: on a grid finer than the format near it -- 14
   figures after the point beside `-999` -- one grid step reads back as
   the stand-in, so the end, the row and G5.4's stratum each take the
   next number binary64 holds that way instead. Measured on 145 four-figure numbers beside five of
   five figures at a floor of eleven, a tail row the walk moved for the
   width census took `9999` and the twin missed seven obligations at
   seeds 0, 4 and 9; three-figure negatives beside five of four figures
   took `-999` at every seed.

**THE STAIRCASE, PUSHED OR SHARED** (stage 4 lane G2T, plan P4-D405).
An unlisted tail read through its shape, on a grid, places its rows on
the grid from the boundary outward, each at its own reading at the share
`(2 i + 1) / (2 m)`, and a row that lands where the row before it stands
takes the next grid point outward, never past the end -- the PUSHED
staircase, one point a row (`contract._tail_steps`). One point a row is
the model of a column whose every number is different. On a column that
repeats its numbers it stretched a tail of `m` rows over at least `m`
points: 100,000 readings of a bell at two places published a low tail
of 1,000 rows at a mean distance of 1.76, the staircase stood at 5.03
and so did the twin, its spread 4.3 per cent above the published one;
on lane B0's table of fifty such columns at 250,000 rows every spread
came back about 12 per cent high and `validate` exited 3 on all fifty;
a count of few values
at 20,000 rows held 194 of its 200 high-tail rows on the derived end `13`,
past the source's own largest. So a side reads the SHARED staircase
(`contract._shared_steps`) where all of these hold: its tail is unlisted,
publishes its pair and is not flat; the block is on a grid (whole
numbers, or the widest width `fraction_widths` names); it repeats its
numbers, at least two cells a number on average (`2 n_distinct_values <=
n_used_in_statistics` -- 128 numbers over 141 cells beside one `99999`
keep the pushed staircase, whose model they are); the pushed staircase's
mean distance stands more than half a grid step FURTHER OUT than the
published one, the test G6.6.8's rule 4 asks of a column whose every
number is different; no row of the shared staircase reaches the one
field width the census names, where it names one (ten to that power, a
figure short where a pad is published: a thousand two-figure readings
beside one `185` read rows at `102` to `172` and lost the width walk's
answer); and G6.6.8's rule 1 moved neither end of the block (rule 3 then
weighs two readings each built on the pushed staircase). Each row of the
shared staircase stands at its own reading on the grid -- on a width,
the grid point nearest the reading's own binary fraction, half to even,
read back as the binary64 nearest it, rounded once (`contract._grid_exact`;
the shortest figures of the reading rounded again to the width moved
four rows of 5,000 readings at 25 places one point, Codex's review of
the repair) --; a row reading
the point of the row before it, or one nearer the boundary, takes that
row's very number; none stands past the end; the outermost row stands
ON the end, and where the end is nought and the column holds zeros,
every one of the outermost `min(n_zero, m)` rows does, the ranks the
zero stratum holds (`contract._end_rows`); a row on a stand-in the block
does not hold steps outward as before. Rounding a row moves its distance
by half a step at the most, so the shared staircase meets the published
mean to within half a step where the shape fits the tail.

**THE SHARED STAIRCASE HOLDS G5.2's SIGN BANDS AT THEIR RANKS** (the
second repair of lane G2T, plan P4-D405; `contract._sign_held`). G5.2
lays the column out negatives first, then the zero stratum, then the
positives, at the published counts, and G5.2a step 1a holds each band's
values to its sign. So, row by row from the outermost inward, a row at a
rank of the zero stratum (the rank of row `i` is `m - 1 - i` on the low
side and `K - m + i` on the high) reads nought and no other row does; a
row at a rank of the negatives reading nought or above stands one grid
step below nought, and a row at a rank of the positives reading nought or
below one grid step above it, never past the row outside it; a row so
moved steps off a stand-in as any row does. Read otherwise the staircase
counted points the twin never holds: 50 less a rounded `lognormal(1.9,
0.6)` at 20,000 rows read `0`, `1` and `2` at three of its six negative
ranks, the twin held them at `-1`, the spread below gained two points
too few, G5.2a divided two runs of the body and G6.5a pushed them down
until the median stood at 41 against a published 43 (lane G2T's combined
verify).

**AND THE SHARED STAIRCASE SPREADS, OR DRAWS TOGETHER, TO THE COUNT THE
TWIN DIVIDES INTO, ITS SUMMED DISTANCE HELD** (`contract._spread_for_the_count`;
the spread of the build, restated by stage 4 lane G2T's repair, plan
P4-D405). Rows sharing points hold fewer different numbers than one
point a row, and G5.2 divides the column into a published count of
strata -- `n_distinct_values`, or, on a plain column of numbers (`count`
or `continuous`), the numbers' share of `n_distinct_folded` under
G6.6's budget split where that is more (`NumericFacts.strata_asked`). Where
the ladder reaches fewer points, G5.2a divides the column's longest run
and G6.5a's walks push its strata apart through the body: counts of
visits 0 to 23 came back with 1,119 ones where the source holds 4,477,
and 500 potassium readings at one place writing both `4` and `4.0`
publish 31 numbers in 33 spellings -- the ladder reached 32 points, the
run of `4.0` was divided, its carriers moved cells across the low tail
and the twin held 29 numbers. The DIFFERENCE is that count (at most
`n_used_in_statistics`) less the points the ladder reaches: one for the
boundary rung `P_lo`, and for each pair of adjacent whole-percent rungs
`p` and `p + 1` from `P_lo` to `P_hi` the fewer of the ranks between
them (`k` with `p K <= 100 k < (p + 1) K`, counted as `ceil((p + 1) K /
100) - ceil(p K / 100)`) and the grid steps between them (their distance
over the step, rounded half up), a null rung taking the nearest held
rung below it; and every point each side's rows or listed values take
past its boundary. Counted in grid steps from the boundary outward on
each shared side, EXACTLY -- a value's own binary fraction times ten to
the grid's figures, rounded half to even, and a point read back as the
binary64 nearest it (`contract._grid_index`, `_grid_value`; a scale
built by multiplying tens is not ten to that power past `1e22`, and
Codex's review measured 5,000 readings at 25 places near `4e-10` whose
point `4000000000000001` read back as `...000`, ten tail readings
crossing their boundary) -- the boundary's own point held by the ladder
inside, a side with a row or an end past `2**52` steps not moved, and
the rows that never move set aside: the rows on the end, and the
outermost rows standing in another sign band than the innermost row
(`contract._sign_frozen`; none moves on a side whose innermost row is the
zero stratum's), whose band's edge, nought, is then the LIMIT a moved row
stays inside in place of the end. A side GAINS a point by moving one row
from a point that keeps a row (a run of two or more, or the boundary's
point) to the nearest grid point no row holds that way, strictly between
the boundary and the limit, and LOSES one by moving the row of a run of
one onto the nearest occupied point that way (the boundary's, never the
end's). Rows are a sorted list, so a move changes one row's value and
the order holds. Each move is the nearest -- the outermost on a tie --
OUTWARD while the side's summed distance stands at or inside the
published `m d1` and INWARD while past it, the other way where none is
left that way. Where a move leaves the sum more than `m / 2` steps from
`m d1` (or further than the unspread staircase stood, if that was
further), the innermost row of a run of one standing at the edge of its
consecutive occupied points with a free point beside it the way the
sum owes moves on through the free points that way -- never onto or past an
occupied point, the boundary, the limit or a refused stand-in -- as far
as the sum owes, rounded down (one step where that is under one and one
step leaves the sum nearer), no point gained or lost, until the sum is
back inside or no such row is left (the second repair: moved one point
at a time, the build's repair took one move a step, 37,424 moves for 235
points on a Pareto column at 100,000 rows). A point that is a stand-in
the block does not hold is no point (step 5). THEN EVERY SHARED SIDE,
whether or not the count moved it, SETTLES ITS SUM TO HALF A STEP: while
it stands more than half a grid step from `m d1`, the innermost row of a
point that keeps a row moves one step the way the sum owes, onto the
occupied point beside it -- no point gained or lost, the least a square
moves (the second repair: within `m / 2` steps is no bound on a coarse
tail, and 20,000 negated rounded `lognormal(2, 0.6)` with one `-0`
published a high tail of 200 rows at 0.5 from `-2`, where the shared
staircase stood 122 rows on `-2` and 77 on `-1`, 21 per cent short, and
the source 101 and 98). The difference is shared between the shared
sides in proportion to the most each can move -- for a gain the fewer of
its spare rows and its free points, for a loss its runs of one row --
the low side's part rounded down and the other taking what the first
cannot. THE MOVES ARE THESE AND THEIR ORDER IS THIS, AND THE PRODUCT
FINDS EACH IN LOGARITHMIC TIME (`contract._Spread`): the occupied points
are kept as blocks of consecutive points, so the free point past a run
is its block's edge, and each kind of move keeps a heap into which every
change pushes the true best move of each block or point it touches,
stale entries dropped when they come to the top. Rescanning every run
for each move, the repair's reading, took one ladder of `pareto(1.1)` at
two places 321.6 s at 250,000 rows and 6,017 s at 500,000 (lane G2T's
combined verify), against 0.05 s on 36ad3061; it takes 0.17 s at
250,000 rows. Measured on a count of Pareto draws at 20,000 rows: spread
outward only, the build's rule, left the high tail's mean distance 10.8
per cent past the published one (7.4 per cent at 250,000 rows); held, 0.2
per cent, its root-mean-square 1.1 per cent under, the spread 0.9 per
cent. A clipped bell at one place reached 360 points against 355; drawn
together inside the tail, its derived end holds one cell and its high
tail's mean distance is 0.13 per cent off.

**Why each step** (measured on the 16-shape battery of plan P4-D344 at
floors 1 and 11). The two moments are what the rows beyond the boundary
publish, and no published number is one of their values: before stage
3 a description published 13 to 46 numbers per shape equal to a value
fewer than eleven rows held; with it, none. The ends of step 4 are a
function of published facts alone, so the twin's range tells a reader
nothing the description does not. The outward move is there for code
developed on the twin: the fitted end of a light tail stands inside the
real extreme, and 16 real cells of a 20,000-row normal column fell
outside the twin's range without it (the skeptic's B6).

### G5.3c The moment ladder (stage 3)

A tail block publishing its moments and no rung (`tails` with two null
sides, TL3) is read as the straight stretch from `lo = mean - sqrt(3) *
std` to `hi = mean + sqrt(3) * std` -- the uniform with that mean and that
spread -- each placed on the grid of G5.3b step 4 and held to the sign
counts by G5.5a, the mean standing for `b` -- and every rung
`L[p] = (1 - t) * lo + t * hi`, `t = p / 100`,
held into `[lo, hi]`, with `L[0] = lo` and `L[100] = hi`. Where the mean
or the spread is withheld the ramp of G5.3d stands in. Measured on a
15-value block at floor 11: the twin's mean 1.9 per cent from the
table's and its spread 6 per cent, nothing missed on the twin or the
table. This ladder is the reading of a block whose two SIDES are null
(TL3). A side publishing neither distance under plan P4-D349 is not
read through it: it is G5.3b's narrowest reading, and plan P4-D353
publishes its pair wherever that reading would leave the column's mean
or spread window short of the published value. A block read through
this ladder at a raised floor has no pair to publish, and where its
twin misses a moment that is held at `K-S3-22`.

**AND THE STRETCH IS HELD INSIDE THE NUMBERS THIS FORMAT HOLDS** (stage
3's review, verdict item 2). Where `mean - sqrt(3) std` or
`mean + sqrt(3) std` is not a finite binary64 there is no uniform with
that mean and that spread to place at all: the reach is then
`LARGEST_FINITE - |mean|`, held at nought or more, so `lo` and `hi` are
the widest stretch the format holds about the published MEAN, which the
stretch then has exactly. Each end is afterwards held into
`[-LARGEST_FINITE, LARGEST_FINITE]` and `hi` at `lo` or above, and this
section answers for the block whatever comes out — the ramp of G5.3d is
the ladder of a block whose moments are WITHHELD and is never taken for
one that publishes them. Measured before this clause: 22 cells at the
top of the range publishing a mean of `-9.75e305` and a spread of
`1.73e308` gave two infinite ends, fell through to G5.3d, and the twin
was written between -11 and 11. The spread of the held stretch falls
short of the published one and the twin's report says so on the
spread's own line.

### G5.3d The made-up ramp (stage 3)

A tail block below its floor (`tails: null`, TL2) publishes no rung and
no moment, so the only shape left to build on is what it says about
SIGNS. Of its `K` values `G = n_negative - n_negative_unrepresentable`
are negative, `Z = n_zero` are nought and the remaining `P = K - G - Z`
are positive (`G` held into `[0, K]` and `Z` into `[0, K - G]`), so the
block's made-up values are

```
-G u, ..., -u,    nought Z times,    u, ..., P u
```

`u` one step of the grid step 4 of G5.3b names (one where no width is
named), each placed on that grid. Rung `p` of the ladder is the value at
the whole rank nearest `(K - 1) p / 100`, halves DOWNWARD — taken in
whole numbers, the rank being the whole part of `(2 (K - 1) p + 100) /
200`, less one where that divides exactly. Every rung is therefore one
of those values and the ladder names no number the block's own counts
forbid. The strata then take points about one step apart on their own
sign bands, so the twin keeps the block's type, its sign counts and its
count of different numbers and claims nothing else.

**ZERO IS BUILT FROM `n_zero` AND NOT ASSUMED** (stage 3's review,
verdict item 5). The ramp ran from `-G u` to `(K - G - 1) u` whatever
the block published, so nought was one of its points on every block.
Measured: a 100-row table holding the numbers 1 to 8 and 92 blanks
publishes eight different numbers and no zero, the ramp spanned 0 to 7,
G5.5's sign repair moved the invented nought onto a number another
stratum already held, and the twin wrote seven different numbers against
the eight published — while its report named `percentiles` as a fact the
twin missed and printed the invented `0.0` as though the description had
published an end it withheld. Measured before the ramp existed at all,
on the same block: the sign fallback wrote `1.0` eight times and the twin
was re-described as another role.

### G5.3e The listed tail (stage 3, plan P4-D324)

A tail whose `values` list is not empty -- on a block with a grid, a
tail of at most six different values, or one whose published facts
would otherwise solve for its end (contract 6.7, TL6) -- is read as a
STAIRCASE over its own rows. The listed values are taken OUTERMOST FIRST
(ascending on the low side, descending on the high side), each holds at
least `q` rows, and the `R = m - L q` rows over (`L` values) are placed
by this rule:

- every binary64 of the tail -- `b`, the values, `d1`, `rms` -- is
  written as a whole number of one shared power of two, exactly, so a
  value's distance `A_i = |b - v_i|` and its square are whole numbers,
  and so are the targets `S1 = m * d1` and `S2 = m * rms * rms`;
- the candidates are the count vectors `c_i = q + e_i` whose extras
  `e_i >= 0` sum to `R` and are nonzero on at most THREE values;
- the chosen one makes `|sum c_i A_i - S1|` least, then
  `|sum c_i A_i**2 - S2|` least, then is the smallest vector of extras in
  lexicographic order, outermost first.

**`q` IS THE LISTING RULE'S OWN FLOOR AND NOT ONE** (plan P4-D346). `q`
is TWO where the tail names MORE THAN TWO values and `m >= 2 L`, and ONE
otherwise. A tail of more than two values was listed because the listing
rule ADMITTED it, and that rule admits a tail only where every value it
names stands on at least TWO of the COLUMN's own cells -- and a scale's
outermost value stands on the tail's cells and nowhere else, so a twin
standing ONE row on it is a twin the same rule would refuse to list, and
`tails.<side>.values` is MISSED on the twin although it holds every
value the description named. Measured on a count of children at 1,800
rows: the solver gave the value 9 one row against a real two, and the
twin missed. Counting from the rule's own number is nearer the truth
besides, because the real counts are all at least it. A tail of one or
two values
is not admitted by that rule at all -- it is listed under the other road
above, its end otherwise being solved for -- so its floor stays one, and
so does the floor of a tail with no room for two rows apiece. **AND A
HEAP'S VALUES COUNT FROM THE FLOOR** (stage 4 lane G2T's repair, plan
P4-D405). Where the column is no small fixed set -- more than 256
different numbers, or fewer than two cells a number -- the listing rule
admitted the tail only as a HEAP, every value it names on at least the
description's `small_cell_floor` of the column's cells, so each listed
value holds at least that many rows, but one the boundary itself holds,
whose other cells stand inside the boundary and which keeps `q`; where
those floors pass `m` they all stay `q`. Counted from two, a length of
stay at one place (`lognormal(1.2, 0.9)`) held `0.2` on 2 twin cells at
100,000 rows where the source holds 182, and `0.1` on 2 at 250,000
against 76, and `validate` MISSED `tails.low.values` in both. WITH `q`
AT ONE THE RULE INVENTS A SINGLETON THE LISTING RULE EXCLUDES: for
boundary `4`, values `[0, 1, 2, 3]`, `m = 12`, `d1 = 2.25` and
`rms = 2.5` it allocates `[1, 5, 2, 4]` against this clause's
`[2, 3, 3, 4]`.

On a grid the summed distance of the real tail is what the published
`d1` rounds from, so the twin's `d1` is met exactly and its
root-mean-square as closely as whole counts on three values allow. The
share `N / D` inside a listed tail reads, counting the rank position
`t = N K / D` from the tail's outer end (`t` on the low side, `K - t` on
the high), the first listed value whose running count exceeds that
position on the low side and reaches it on the high side, and the
innermost listed value past the tail's rows. The layout of G5.2a
neither joins nor divides a band's leading or trailing runs that lie
wholly inside a listed tail's rows: each is one listed value at the
count solved for it -- UNLESS those runs are the whole band and it is
owed more strata still, where they are left to the ordinary walk,
because there is no other run to divide and the twin would otherwise
hold fewer values than the description names (twenty-four offsets
written `+0100` and `0100` over eight values: both tails list four
each, those eight runs are the band, and sixteen different SPELLINGS
ask for sixteen strata). The pinned end is the outermost listed value.

**A RUN THAT REACHES ACROSS A TAIL'S EDGE IS ONE OF THOSE RUNS**, whole,
WHERE THE BAND'S RUNS MUST BE JOINED to reach its stratum count: the
protection reads a run as the tail's where any of its ranks is the
tail's, and not only where all of them are, on a band with more runs
than strata. Two qualifications, each measured. Only where the runs
must be joined, because that is the only case a run can be joined away
in and the protection is not free: on 150 cells over three values
written `+100.25`, `200.25` and `300.25`, whose three runs already had
three strata, protecting the two that reach into a tail split the fifty
published pluses across two values and the twin wrote four spellings of
three numbers. And the band is still LEVELLED after it, because the
runs a listed tail names are the ladder's and the ladder's own boundary
can stand a rank from the column's: what the tail needs is that the run
not be joined away, not that it be held still, and holding it still
gave that same band 49, 53 and 48 cells where the source holds fifty of
each. A tail's innermost listed value
is commonly the column's value just inside the boundary as well, so the
ladder reads one number across the edge, and counting only the runs
lying WHOLLY inside left that one to the ordinary walk. Measured on 240
rows of clinical codes at a floor of one, whose high tail lists two
values and whose inner one stood at eleven ranks, the outer two of them
the tail's own: the walk joined that run to its neighbours, the stratum
that swallowed it read its own share instead, and the twin wrote five
cells at `920759` where the table holds `920760` -- so `validate`
MISSED `tails.high.values`. The run is kept WHOLE rather than cut at the
edge, which was the first repair and cost more than it bought: a cut
spends one of the band's strata on the tail's own part, and on 1,140
readings over eleven values it took that stratum off the published
MODE -- 210 cells written nowhere, `-1.4` written in 307 cells against
170, and the median moved with them.

Why. On a bounded scale the tail holds a handful of values each held by
several rows, and G5.3b's smooth reading rounded onto that grid wrote
values the scale does not have and never wrote its real end: a pain
score of 0 to 10 at floor 11 wrote 50 cells at 11 and none at 10, and its
twin's mean was 25 per cent high with nothing missed (the skeptic's B1).
The owner's ruling of 2026-09-22 settles what may be said: "many people
will be there and there is no big deal in knowing that it's there".
With the listed tail, 13 columns of pain, GCS, a surgical risk grade,
Apgar, children and Likert scales at two seeds write no off-scale cell
and every real value.

### G5.4 The integer rule

When `integer_valued` is published **true**, every value of the K
numeric cells is a whole number. The rule is applied to each stratum
value after G5.3 and before G5.5, and it is applied by the FACT and not
by the role (P2-D6): a `continuous` column publishing
`integer_valued: true` gets it, and a `count` column publishing false
does not.

```
b = int(v)                  exact truncation toward zero
r = v - float(b)            exact; |r| < 1, sign follows v
if r >  0.5:  n = b + 1
elif r == 0.5: n = b + 1                  ties go toward +infinity
elif r < -0.5: n = b - 1
elif r == -0.5: n = b                     ties go toward +infinity
else:          n = b
```

**Rounding direction, stated once:** to nearest, and **ties toward
positive infinity**. Not banker's rounding, and not toward zero: two
implementations that disagree here disagree on bytes, and half-even
would make a twin's rounding depend on the parity of a neighbour.

**AND THE ONE PLACE THAT RULE DOES NOT GOVERN, named here so that
"stated once" stays true.** The integer rule above places ONE value at
a time and a bias in it moves that value. Phase 4's fixed-fraction
snap — the rule that writes a `decimal`-styled cell at a width the
column's own census publishes (plan P4-D4.5, with amendments A-P4-5,
A-P4-6, A-P4-8 and A-P4-15) — places a whole column of them at once,
and a bias toward positive infinity applied to every tie there walks
the column's own mean up with it. That snap rounds **half to even**,
which the plan fixes in those words. Nothing else in this method does.

**WHAT THE SNAP ROUNDS, which half to even alone does not settle.**
The operand is the value's SHORTEST ROUND-TRIP DECIMAL FIGURES — the
shortest decimal string that reads back as exactly this binary64,
which is what `repr` produces and what G6.2 already builds every
spelling from — and NOT the binary64 itself. The two give different
answers and a second implementer has to be told which: `2.675` is held
as a double a shade BELOW two and sixty-seven and a half hundredths,
so rounding the double at two figures gives `2.67`, while rounding its
shortest figures `2675` at two gives the tie, and the tie goes to even,
so `2.68`. Both are defensible half-to-even; only one is this method's.
Review round 2 of the integer-grid landing found this document silent
on it while two implementations agreed on `2.68` for no stated reason.

**AND THE SIGN SURVIVES A MAGNITUDE THAT SNAPS TO NOTHING.** Where the
figures round away entirely the sign is still written: `-0.004` at two
figures is `-0.00`, not `0.00`. This is NOT the "never `-0`" rule of
G6.2, which governs the canonical spelling of zero itself; here the
value is not zero and the width is what hides it. A second implementer
who dropped the sign would write a different cell, and the twin would
carry a positive-looking cell where the column held a negative value.

**THE REST OF THE SNAP IS NOT WRITTEN HERE YET, and that is a recorded
debt, not an omission this sentence closes.** **R-P4-146** owes this
document the width assignment, the pinned-cell order, and the
same-class and endpoint guards. It is named here because review round 3
of the integer-grid landing found this paragraph assigning that debt to
R-P4-17, which is CLOSED — so the unwritten half of the snap had no
live owner at all. R-P4-18 owes a vector in which a value is actually
rounded, and now owes it twice over, because no frozen case reaches the
operand rule above either. Both
are named in the Phase 4 plan's register. What the paragraph above
settles is only the contradiction: a second implementer reading this
section used to find a global tie rule the shipped snap violates by
name, with nothing saying an exception existed.

Both subtractions are exact. For `|v| >= 2**52` the value is already
integral and `r` is zero; below that, `b` is exactly representable and
`v - float(b)` needs no more than 53 bits, so no rounding occurs.

`min` and `max` are themselves whole numbers whenever `integer_valued`
is true (every value was whole, so the extremes are), and rounding a
value inside `[min, max]` to a nearest integer cannot leave that
interval. The pinned strata are not rounded — they already carry the
published rungs — which is what keeps the endpoints exact.

**AND NO STRATUM READ BETWEEN THE TWO TAILS IS A STAND-IN NUMBER** (plan
P4-D353 part 4). After this rule — or, on a column written at one width,
after the grid value G5.3 reads there — a stratum whose value the convex
form gave and which equals `-9999`, `-999` or `9999`
(`parsing.NUMERIC_SENTINELS`) and is not one the column keeps (G5.3b
step 5) takes the neighbouring point of its grid
TOWARD NOUGHT: one unit on a whole-valued column, one step of the one
width, and the next number binary64 holds where there is neither. Where
that point lies outside the published `min` to `max` it takes the
neighbouring point away from nought, and where that one does too it
keeps the value. Where the grid is finer than binary64 near the
stand-in, so that the point's grid text reads back as the stand-in
itself, the neighbouring point is the next number binary64 holds that
way (plan P4-D357 A): on 200 values a few binary64 steps either side of
`-999` at fourteen figures, none of them `-999`, every twin wrote
`-999.00000000000000` once before this sentence. Toward nought keeps the stand-in's figure count —
`-998`, `9998`, `-9998`, the answer G6.6's width walk takes — and a
magnitude of 998 or more keeps its sign, so G5.5 has nothing to repair.
A stratum read inside a tail is the tail's (G5.3b step 5); a pinned
end, a listed value and the zero stratum are not drawn. Measured by
skeptic Ad on the 899 whole numbers `-1400` to `-1000` and `-998` to
`-501`, which hold no `-999`: at floors 11, 20, 36 and 50 and seeds 0, 4
and 9 one or two strata read `-999` and every twin wrote it deep in its
interior. With the rule no stratum does; G6.5a's walk, which took `-999`
at seeds 4 and 9 as the one free point between the column's own `-1000`
and `-998`, now passes it over too (G5.3b step 5) and the twin writes
none.

### G5.5 Placing `n_zero` and `n_negative` exactly

The strata of G5.2 give the exact counts by construction: `G` cells sit
in negative strata, `Z` cells in the zero stratum, `P` in positive
strata. Two repairs make that construction true of the VALUES as well,
because the ladder and the sign counts are separate published facts and
nothing forces them to agree:

```
negative_fallback = the larger of L[0] and -1
positive_fallback = the smaller of L[10] and 1
```

Applied to every stratum after the integer rule, including the pinned
ones:

- a stratum in the negative band whose value is `>= 0` takes
  `negative_fallback`;
- a stratum in the positive band whose value is `<= 0` takes
  `positive_fallback`;
- the zero stratum's value is exactly `0` and needs no repair, because
  it was never drawn.

Both fallbacks are inside `[min, max]` whenever they are reachable: a
column with `G > 0` has a negative value, so `min < 0`, so
`max(min, -1) < 0`; symmetrically for the positive side. Both are whole
numbers when `integer_valued` is true, because a whole `min < 0` is at
most `-1`.

**On a column written at one width `f > 0`** (the grid of G5.2a step 1
and G5.3; integration repair of landing 2b.1) a stratum that is not
pinned takes instead the nearest point of that grid on its own side of
zero that no other stratum holds -- `-0.01`, then `-0.02`, and so on at
`f = 2`, never past `L[0]` on the negative side or `L[10]` on the
positive -- and the first such step where every one within reach is
held. The strata are repaired in stratum order, and "held" is the value
every other stratum has at that moment. The grid value of G5.3 puts a
negative stratum whose rank lies within half a step of zero on `0.00` or
`0.01`, so the plain fallback made such strata `-1`: on a 2,000-row
column of changes rounded to two places two of them landed on `-1.0`
beside a third that held it, one number spent the count of different
values, and its six cells were written `-1.0` against a published width
of two. The pinned strata keep the plain fallbacks.

**The precedence is stated, not implied:** where the ladder and the sign
counts disagree, **the counts win** (P2-D6 feasibility rule 4). The
repair moves at most one value per conflicting stratum onto a fallback,
the deviation is measured against the published rungs, and the report
names it. Where a repair changes a PINNED stratum — which can happen
only for a profile whose `min`/`max` contradict its own sign counts —
the endpoint stops being EXACT-OBSERVABLE for that column and the report
names the achieved endpoint beside the published one.

### G5.5a The sign rule on a derived end (stage 3)

A derived end (G5.3b step 4, G5.3c) is held to the sign counts after it
is placed on the grid: where the block has no negative number the low
end is at least nought -- nought where `n_zero > 0`, otherwise the
smaller of `b` and one grid step where it would be nought or less --
and symmetrically the high end where the block has no positive number;
ONE STEP HERE IS THE SMALLEST POSITIVE NUMBER THE FORMAT HOLDS where
the block names no width, its boundary rung gives no places, and the
step that leaves is not smaller than that rung: `min(b, one)` hands
back `b` itself there and the tail's rows have nowhere to stand (120
subnormal numbers, `5e-324` times 1 to 120, whose whole column is
smaller than one);
then the low end is at or below `b` and the high end at or above it. A
published heaped end is never moved. The pinned strata keep G5.5's plain
fallbacks for anything this leaves (a profile whose ends contradict its
sign counts).

### G5.6 The two-sided rung envelope

This is the acceptance bound the disposition battery applies to a
numeric column, and it is stated here because the method is what makes
it true.

Let `Ladder(p)` be the published ladder read as a piecewise-linear
function of a probability `p` in `[0, 1]`, using the same segment rule
and the same convex form as G5.3. Let `g_max` be G5.2a's `Cap`, read off
the numeric block the numbers are described by — a column's own block,
or the block of one joined position, one affixed wrapper or a compound
column's numeric half — and the count of numeric cells that block
describes where `Cap` is 0 (landing 2b.1, part 2, 2026-09-15). It is a
function of the description alone, so the twin's own report and the
quality report read one number without either rebuilding the layout
(validation method V1.4), and

```
d = (g_max + 2) / K
```

Then, for each of the nine INTERIOR rungs `i = 1 .. 9`, the rung `T[i]`
recomputed from the twin's own written numeric cells (by the profiler's
own type-7 quantile, over the parsed values) must satisfy

```
Ladder(max(0, PCT[i]/100 - d))  <=  T[i]  <=  Ladder(min(1, PCT[i]/100 + d))
```

and the two extreme rungs must be met EXACTLY:

```
T[0] == L[0]        and        T[10] == L[10]
```

**Why that window.** The cell that lands at recomputed rank `k` comes
from the stratum covering rank `k`, whose share of the distribution is
at most `g_max / K` wide, and a recomputed rung interpolates two
adjacent order statistics, which adds one more rank. So `d` is the
widest ladder displacement the construction can produce, and the bound
is a statement about the method rather than a tolerance somebody
measured and rounded up.

**Why no stratum is wider than `g_max`.** G5.2b's band floor gives every
band enough strata to hold its cells under `Cap`, and G5.2a's levelling
holds every stratum under it. **The one exception is named, not
absorbed.** On a column publishing `integer_valued: false` beside a
point-free style count, G5.2b's carrier and reach steps may move cells
past `Cap`, because the published style count wins (plan P2-D6, rule 4).
The twin's own report, which built the layout, then reads `g_max` as the
widest stratum built, so its bound still holds of the construction. The
quality report cannot read that layout (validation method V1.4) and reads
`Cap`, so there the two reports print different windows for one fact and
the quality report's is the narrower: it can call a rung MISSED that the
twin report calls inside. Closing that needs a second writing of the
carrier and reach steps outside the generator. Measured: of 11,134
layouts the generation test files build, 305 stood above `Cap`, every
one of that shape; on a 4,000-row column of halves written without
their trailing zero one stratum held 315 cells beside a `Cap` of 268,
and no rung left the narrower window at the seeds tried. **A second
exception of the same kind** (lane G2 of stage 3b, plan P4-D377): where
G6.6.8's rule 3 writes a tail block on the division its width rule
withdrawn gives, that division was cut by a ladder whose width-held end
makes a run of equal rungs, which raises G5.2a's cap, so a stratum can
stand past the `Cap` the published ladder gives -- 15 rows beside a
`Cap` of 11 on 150 two-figure readings beside one `188` at a floor of
20. The twin's own report reads `g_max` as the widest stratum of either
division, so its bound holds of whichever was written; the quality
report reads `Cap`.

**What it must reject.** A mutant that ignores the nine interior rungs
and interpolates only between `min` and `max` produces
`T[i] ≈ min + (PCT[i]/100) * (max - min)`, which leaves this window on
any column whose ladder is materially non-linear. The battery is
therefore required to include at least one fixture whose interior ladder
is far from a straight line and whose `K` is large enough that `d` is
small — a fixture where the collapse mutant misses the window by more
than one rung — and to assert this bound on it. Rung mutants that
permute or swap the interior rungs are rejected by the same window.

**The same window holds rank by rank, not only at the nine rungs.** The
argument above never uses the fact that `i` is one of the eleven ladder
positions: it bounds the value at ANY recomputed rank. Writing `p_k =
k / (K - 1)` for the share the profiler's own quantile rule attaches to
sorted position `k`, every value `V[k]` of the twin's own sorted numeric
cells satisfies

```
Ladder(max(0, p_k - d))  <=  V[k]  <=  Ladder(min(1, p_k + d))
```

with the same `d`. On a column publishing `integer_valued: true` both
ends widen by the one half unit the whole-number rule of G5.4 can add;
on a column written at one fraction width, by half a unit of its last
place, which is how far G5.3's grid value stands from the ladder at its
own rank; and by nothing else. G12.3 derives the moment bounds from this rank
form, so the moments and the rungs rest on one statement about the
construction rather than on two.

Moments (`mean`, `std`, `skew`) are APPROXIMATED, and **G12.3 fixes a
formula and a finite two-sided bound for each of them**, derived from
the rank form above. Revision 1 of this document left that bound to a
test battery; review item P2-C1-F4 ruled that delegating a normative
bound to a battery leaves an approximated fact with no bound at all,
since a battery is not a document an independent implementer can
conform to.

### G5.6a The envelope on a tail block (stage 3)

On a tail block the ends are DERIVED and not EXACT-OBSERVABLE: `min`
and `max` are checked only where published (a heaped end), and then
ONE-SIDED and silently -- no cell of the file beyond the end, and the
file's own extreme never printed (validation method V5). The rank form
and its `d = (g_max + 2) / K` stand unchanged over the tail ladder of
G5.1a, so G12.2's and G12.3's windows are drawn through it. A rung the
tail rule withholds carries no window and is LISTED.

**Where G6.6.8's rule 1 reads a tail toward a further end, the `skew`
and `kurtosis` windows drawn through it can cover the statistic's whole
range, and are then LISTED, not checked** (lane G2 of stage 3b, plan
P4-D377; the second skeptic of its repair, item 2). Measured over 3,459
twins of eleven batteries, 175 lose a `skew` or `kurtosis` check that
110cb46 gave and that held -- 23 at a floor of 11, 39 at 20, 62 at 36 and
51 at 50, on 82 column-floors, among them a thousand two-figure readings
shaped like a bell beside one `188`, and P4-D377's million rows. The
listing is the
honest answer on the rule's reading; drawn with the rule withdrawn
instead, those windows would fail 13 checks on 9 twins the rule
improved, a kurtosis of 352.1 against a published 356.6 outside a window
of 1 to 250 among them, where 110cb46's twin held 7.9 inside it.

### G5.7 The L0 band totals (layer L0 of stage 6, plan P4-D404; specified, NOT BUILT)

**No generator in this repository runs anything in this section yet;
lane BT builds it.** It fixes how an ELIGIBLE number column makes its
cells so that each of its published L0 bands holds EXACTLY its
published count, with every other published fact of the column still
met, or, where this construction cannot meet both, settled by a rule
stated here (G5.7h). G7.3l does the same for a date column and G7A.4d
for a clock column. Where `relationships.statistical` is `null`, or
gives a column no L0 block, nothing here runs and the column's cells
are byte for byte what G5 and G6 make today.

**Why.** Today a column meets its percentile rungs inside a window and
not its counts between them, so its twin puts some rows on the wrong
side of a rung. Measured on the product's own twins of an invented
ten-column table (G5.7i): at the decile edges, every number, date and
clock column missed its band totals at every seed, by 4 to 94 rows a
column at 5,000 rows and by 8 to 262 at 20,000, and an invented patient
cohort's columns by up to 375 at 20,000. A band holding one value of a
count column (the fours of a count of visits) held 1,400 rows against
1,320. On a count of few values with one rare high value the product's
own twins miss by thousands: 5,717 rows off its band totals at 20,000
rows and 29,676 at 100,000, with 30,000 rows on the value 3 where the
real column held 12,465 (lane M6 measured the same twins at 29,729 rows
off and 30,000 against 12,471, plan P4-D394 at b762720c, not merged).
The cause there is not the ties but the strata beyond the ladder's runs
(G5.7i): G5.2a step 3 divides the longest run, and G6.5a's separation
lifts every stratum above it by one value; read back without that lift,
the same strata miss by 416 rows of the 29,676. A table between two
columns can be met cell for cell only where
each column's own band totals are the table's margins. So stage 6 makes
those totals exact in the generator, as its layer L0, rather than
adjusting each table to the twin's own margins.

**What it keeps.** The single stream: nothing here draws a word, and
every word G4.3 hands a column is still drawn, in the same order. The
arithmetic: binary64 `+ - * /` and exact integers, in the order
written, and G5.3's four-operation convex form; no logarithm,
exponential or sine. The floor: nothing here is published, and no count
of the real table is printed anywhere it was not printed before.

#### G5.7a When it runs, and what it reads

A number column is ELIGIBLE where `relationships.statistical` gives it
an L0 block. Lane MBC's contract fixes which columns are eligible and
which rungs form L0; this section takes both as given. The block
publishes:

- the EDGES `e_1 < e_2 < ... < e_m`, each a published, non-null rung of
  the hundred-and-one-rung ladder G5.3 reads (after G5.1's fill);
- one COUNT `c_j` for each RANGE band: band 0 holds the readings below
  `e_1`, band `j` the readings at least `e_j` and below `e_(j+1)`, and
  band `m` the readings at least `e_m`. Each count is nought or at least
  the floor. A narrower band is merged into its neighbour before it is
  published, so every published count is a count of the real column,
  never a rounded one;
- the counts of the bands `missing`, `other` and `labels`.

The CUT RANK of edge `j` is `R_j = c_0 + ... + c_(j-1)`: the number of
cells below `e_j`. Five PRECONDITIONS, each a fact of the description
alone, are checked before G5.2:

- **(P1)** `c_0 + ... + c_m = K`, the cells G5 lays out (on an affixed
  column, the cores' count of G6A.2);
- **(P2)** the cut ranks agree with the sign counts: `R_j <= G` where
  `e_j <= 0`, with `R_j = G` where `e_j = 0`, and `R_j >= G + Z` where
  `e_j > 0`;
- **(P3)** every band with cells has room, and so does every piece with
  cells of G5.7b (a band cut by the sign cuts): it holds at least one value
  the column may write, that is a whole number where `integer_valued`
  is true, a point of the grid of the WIDEST named width where G5.2a
  step 1 finds a written grid (G5.7b's piece grid), inside `min` and
  `max` where they are published, and outside every stretch
  `empty_edges` names;
- **(P4)** on a tail block every edge lies at or between the two
  boundary rungs (the rungs outside them are null, G5.1a), `R_j >= m_lo`
  for every edge above the low boundary rung, and `K - R_j >= m_hi` for
  every edge below the high one (a tail's rows lie at or beyond its
  boundary);
- **(P5)** a published `min` lies in the band holding rank 0, and a
  published `max` in the band holding rank `K - 1`.

Every description a producer writes passes (P1), (P2), (P4) and (P5),
because each is an identity of the real column, whose counts the L0
block and the column's own facts both publish. **(P3) holds on every
description a producer writes EXCEPT where a band's or a piece's cells
were all written at widths the census counts into its commonest width**,
each such width written by fewer than `parsing.census_floor` cells: the
validation method (amended 2026-09-17, plans P4-D221 and P4-D222)
counts such a width into the commonest one and never names it, so no
named width's grid need hold a point of that band or piece. Elsewhere
(P3) holds because it is read on the widest named width's grid: a cell
written at a named width is a point of the grid of every width at least
as wide, so each band or piece holding one such cell holds a point of
that grid, inside `min` and `max` and outside every empty stretch. The
exception is measured (lane BTp's verify of 11dd0b6b, on the
profiler): a 400-row column of 20 cells at each of `0.1` to `1.0`, 40
cells from `1.01` to `1.09` written ten each at two, three, four and
five figures, and 16 at each of `1.1` to `2.0` publishes
`fraction_widths` `{"1": 400}`, its 50th percentile `1.005` and its
60th `1.094`; every band holds 16 cells or more, and the band between
those two holds the 40 cells and no tenth (G14.3a case 17). Such a
column is made WITHOUT L0 under rule B3 and named, a limit plan P4-D404
names. Read on the
grid G5.2a step 1 chooses, the commonest width's, (P3) failed a real
column (the outside review of this page, its item 3): 100 cells at each
of `0.1` to `0.6`, 150 at `1.01`, 150 at `1.02` and 100 at `2.0` are on
the grid of tenths, and the band from the 70th percentile, `1.01`, to
the 80th, `1.02`, holds 150 real cells and no tenth (G14.3a case 14).
Where one fails, on a hand-written description or on a column of the
exception above, the column is made WITHOUT L0, exactly as G5 and G6
make it today. G4.2b says so to G16, which then meets that column's
families by G16.6, and the twin's report names the column and the
precondition that failed (rule B3, G5.7h).

#### G5.7b Cuts and pieces

A CUT is a value with a rank: exactly `R` of the `K` cells lie below the
value. The method already holds the two sign cuts of G5.2 and G5.5
exactly: `G` cells below 0, and `G + Z` cells at or below it. L0 adds
one cut for each edge, at `R_j`.

Taken together in rank order, the cuts divide the `K` ranks into
PIECES. A piece is a maximal run of ranks between two consecutive
cuts, together with the stretch of values between their two values,
lower end included and upper end excluded; the ZERO PIECE is the value
0 alone. Each piece's cell count `C_p` is a difference of two cut
ranks, so it is a count of the real column itself, and (P2) and (P4)
make the cut ranks rise with their values.

**THE PIECE GRID.** On a column G5.2a step 1 puts on a written grid of
`f` figures, a piece keeps that grid where its stretch holds an
admissible point of it (G5.7e's admissible values, read on that grid).
A piece with cells whose stretch holds none is read on the grid of the
NARROWEST named width of `fraction_widths` whose grid holds an
admissible point inside it; the widest named width's always does, by
(P3). That grid is the PIECE GRID, and every clause of G5.7 that reads
"the grid", "a grid point" or "a grid unit" reads, inside a piece, that
piece's grid: G5.7d's reading (`GridValue` at the piece grid's width),
its free points, `hi_p` and item 3a, G5.7e's admissible values and
fallbacks, G5.7f's separation, fill and snap, and G12.15's fallbacks.
Off a written grid, and on the whole numbers, every piece's grid is the
column's. A value of a finer piece grid needs more figures than `f`,
and the real column's cells in that piece did too, since its stretch
holds no point of `f` figures; G5.2a's width steps count it at its own
width, as they count every stratum.

**A piece is what G5.2 calls a band, refined.** G5.2's negative band is
the union of the pieces below 0, its zero stratum is the zero piece,
and its positive band is the union of the pieces above 0. This
section's one rule follows, and the rest of it is that rule applied:

**EVERY CLAUSE OF G5, G6, G6A AND G6B THAT KEEPS A CELL, A STRATUM OR A
VALUE INSIDE ITS SIGN BAND KEEPS IT INSIDE ITS PIECE.** The method meets
the sign counts exactly because nothing it does moves a cell across
zero. The layout moves cells only by moving the boundaries between
strata of one band, and every value step either keeps a stratum's
value on its band's side of zero or repairs it there (G5.5). A piece is
the same object with more walls, so the same steps meet each piece's
count, and a band's total is a sum of piece counts.

#### G5.7c The band map: where the ladder is read

G5.2a step 1, G5.2b's reach step and G5.3 read the ladder at a rank
POSITION: the rank of a cell, or a point `N_s / 2**64` inside a
stratum's share, against the scale `K` (the comparisons of `100 * N`
with `PCT[j] * D`, `D = K * 2**64`). Today rung `j` stands at position
`K * PCT[j] / 100`. On an eligible column the rungs stand at KNOTS:

- **an edge.** Let `k_j` be the SMALLEST percent whose rung equals
  `e_j`, and `P_j = K * k_j / 100`. The edge's LOWER KNOT, of value
  `e_j`, stands at position `R_j`. Its UPPER KNOT, of the same value,
  stands at `min(max(R_j, P_j), R_next)`, where `R_next` is the next
  edge's cut rank (the high boundary's knot after the last edge on a
  tail block, `K` otherwise), so every position between the two knots
  reads `e_j` and nothing else, and no knot ever stands behind the one
  before it. An edge whose band holds no cell has its two knots on one
  position;
- **the ends and the tails.** Rank 0 keeps percent 0 and rank `K` keeps
  percent 100. On a tail block the tail rows keep G5.3b's and G5.3e's
  own readings, row by row, so the map moves no tail row; the low
  boundary rung is a knot at `m_lo`, the low tail's rows, where the body
  begins, and the high boundary rung a knot at `K - m_hi`. An edge equal
  to a boundary rung takes the boundary's knot;
- **every other rung** stands between the two knots around it in
  proportion to its percent: a rung at percent `q` between knots at
  percents `k < q < k'` and positions `X <= X'` stands at
  `X + (X' - X) * (q - k) / (k' - k)`, the knot below it being an
  edge's upper knot and the knot above it an edge's lower knot.

Positions are rationals. A segment whose two knots share a position
holds no position and is passed over. The segment search of G5.3 is taken over them
with the denominators cleared, so every comparison is between whole
numbers, and the fraction inside a segment is one integer quotient: for
a position `x` between knots at `X_a` and `X_b`,
`T = floor(2**53 * (x - X_a) / (X_b - X_a))`, then `t = ldexp(T, -53)`
and G5.3's convex form and clamp, unchanged.

**How far the map moves a position.** The profiler reads a numeric rung
by the type-7 rule at `h = (K - 1) * k_j / 100`. Where the rung falls
strictly between two different order statistics, `R_j` is the next
rank above `h`, so `R_j` and `P_j` lie less than one rank apart. Where
the rung IS a value the column held, `R_j` lies at or below `P_j`, by up
to about one percent of `K` where that value is held by many rows (the
twos of a count). There the flat segment between the two knots is that
value's heap, which the real column holds at those ranks too. So on a
column whose edges are not heaped, the map moves no position by a whole
rank.

#### G5.7d The layout over pieces

G5.2, G5.2a and G5.2b run with PIECE in place of BAND wherever they read
a sign band:

1. **Reading.** G5.2a step 1 reads the ladder through the band map at
   every rank of each piece, `lo` being the piece's first rank, with
   G5.4's integer rule and, on a written grid, `GridValue` at the width
   of the piece's grid (G5.7b), as that step says. Step 1a, the band's own sign, becomes the PIECE'S OWN STRETCH:
   in a piece of values from `a` up to `b`, every value read below `a`
   is replaced by the first value of the piece read at or above `a`, and
   every value read at or above `b` by the last value of the piece read
   below `b`. A piece none of whose ranks reads a value inside it keeps
   what it read, and G5.7e answers for it.
2. **Runs, joins and the cap.** Steps 2 to 4 run inside each piece. A
   run never crosses a cut; step 3 joins only two runs of one piece and,
   off a grid, divides the longest run of a piece (on a grid, item 3a
   says where the strata beyond the runs go); the levelling under the cap moves
   cells only to the nearest run of the same piece; and `Cap_band` is
   taken per piece, `max(Cap, ceil(C_p / M_p))`.
3. **The share over pieces** replaces G5.2b's share between the two sign
   bands. `M_zero` and `M_rest` are G5.2's. Each piece `p` with cells,
   other than the zero piece, has `C_p` cells and `A_p` runs from step
   2 (on a tail block, the tail's strata counted as G5.2a counts them
   today). It starts at `lo_p = 1`, raised to `ceil(C_p / Cap)` where
   `Cap > 0` and the raised floors together come to at most `M_rest`
   (G5.2b's own condition), and is held to at most
   `hi_p = min(C_p, A_p + F_p)` on a grid (the whole numbers, or a
   written grid of `f` figures) and `hi_p = C_p` off one. `F_p` is the
   number of the piece's FREE POINTS: the admissible grid points of
   G5.7e, inside the piece, that no run of the piece reads, lying
   strictly between the values of two consecutive runs of the piece, or
   between the piece's lower end and its first run, or between its last
   run and its upper end, an end counting only where it is published (an
   L0 edge, the sign cut at 0, or a published `min` or `max`; the end
   beside an unpublished `min` or `max` holds no free point, because no
   point beyond the last run is one the real column is known to reach).
   Where `lo_p` exceeds `hi_p` (the cap's floor asking more strata than
   the piece has places), `hi_p` is raised to `lo_p`, and what G6.5a's
   separation cannot then pull apart is named under rule B1. The
   remaining `M_rest - sum(lo_p)` strata are handed out one at a time,
   each to the piece below its `hi_p` with the largest
   `A_p / (2 m_p + 1)`, compared exactly as
   `A_p * (2 m_q + 1) > A_q * (2 m_p + 1)`, the lower piece on a tie.
   This is the Sainte-Lague rule, which rounds to the nearest share, as
   G5.2b's formula does for two bands. **Strata that no piece can take
   are not made**: where every piece stands at its `hi_p` with strata
   left over, `M` is lowered by the strata left over, and the count of
   different numbers gives way under rule B1, named in the twin's
   report beside the published count. Where the pieces with cells
   outnumber `M_rest`, `M` is raised to their number and the raised
   count is named, as G5.2 raises it for the sign facts (on a
   description a producer writes this happens only where `M_rest` falls
   below the real column's count of different non-zero numbers, which
   G5.2b's floor already names). **Neither
   moves the word budget.** G4.3 reads the column's `S` without L0, and
   the column draws exactly those words, in G5.3's order: the drawn
   strata take them in ascending `s` while they last; where `M` was
   lowered, the words left over are drawn after the last stratum's and
   set aside, read by nothing, as G4.3's reserve is drawn whether or not
   its walk reads it; where `M` was raised, a drawn stratum left without
   a word reads its share at its middle, as if its word were `2**63`,
   and draws nothing. Read off the lowered `M`, the budget would hand
   every later column other words: a 1,000-row eligible column of 800
   cells at `1.0`, one at each of `1.001` to `1.100` and 100 at `2.0`,
   on the grid of tenths, has `M = 102` and 100 words without L0, while
   its pieces hold at most eleven grid points between them (the outside
   review of this page, its item 4; G14.3a case 15). **Why `hi_p`.** Held only to `C_p`, the
   rule gives a piece holding one value several strata where the
   strata outnumber the runs, and no step can separate them inside it:
   pieces from 1 to 2, 2 to 4, 4 to 5 and 5 up, with runs 1, 2, 1 and 8
   and `M_rest` 18, took 2, 3, 1 and 12 strata, two strata for one whole
   number and three for two (lane BTp's first skeptic, `share_probe.py`).
   With `hi_p`, the top piece's eight runs reading 5 to 11 and the
   pinned `max` of 18, its free points 12 to 17, they take 1, 2, 1 and
   14 (G14.3a case 6).
3a. **WHERE THE STRATA BEYOND THE RUNS GO.** Where a piece on a grid
   holds fewer runs than its strata, step 3 of G5.2a does NOT divide the
   piece's longest run. Each stratum beyond the runs is made, one at a
   time, in the piece's WIDEST ELIGIBLE GAP. A GAP is the stretch of
   free points between two consecutive strata of the piece (or between
   the piece's published end and its first or last stratum). **A GAP
   holds at least one free point; a stretch of none is not a gap.** It is
   ELIGIBLE where a stratum beside it holds two or more cells (beside a
   published end, where the one stratum there does). Of the eligible
   gaps the one holding the most free points is taken, the lowest gap
   on a tie; a gap no stratum beside which can be divided is never
   taken, however wide. Of the two strata beside that gap, the one of
   more cells (the lower on a tie; beside a published end, the one
   stratum there) is divided as step 3 divides a run, into
   `floor(L / 2)` and `L - floor(L / 2)` cells in rank order, and the
   part on the gap's side takes the gap's free point NEAREST the
   divided stratum's value: the first free point above it where the gap
   is above, the first below it where the gap is below. That stratum still
   takes the word G5.3 hands it, exactly as before, and its value is
   then set to that point, as G5.5's repair sets a value without a word.
   Since the stratum divided holds two or more cells, both parts hold
   at least one, and no stratum of the layout is ever empty. Where no
   gap of the piece is eligible, the stratum is not made and `M` is
   lowered by one, named as above. Taken among every gap, the widest
   could be one between two strata of one cell each: at strata `(value,
   cells)` = `(1, 1), (10, 1), (11, 100), (13, 100)` with one stratum to
   make, the gap 2 to 9 is the widest, and dividing the one cell beside
   it makes a stratum of none, while the eligible gap, 12, divides the
   100 cells at 11 into 50 and 50 (the outside review of this page, its
   item 5; G14.3a case 16). With the last stratum at 12 and the
   published ends 1 and 12, the free points 2 to 9 lie beside two
   strata of one cell, and the stretches from 10 to 11 and from 11 to
   12 hold no free point, so they are no gaps: none is eligible, the
   stratum is not made and `M` is lowered by one (lane BTp's verify of
   11dd0b6b, its finding 2; G14.3a case 16 (b)). Off a grid, step 3 divides the piece's longest run as it does
   today, and G6.5a's separation finds a free number between any two
   different values inside the piece. **Why.** Today the strata beyond
   the runs come from dividing the longest run, and on a grid with no
   spare point between that run and the next G6.5a's separation and its
   fill lift every stratum above it by one value. That was all but 416
   of the 29,676 rows off of G5.7i's count of few values at 100,000
   rows: the ones were divided into 20,749 and 20,750 cells, the second
   half lifted onto 2, the twos onto 3, and every value above them by
   one.
   Walls alone move the same division into the top piece, where the
   threes would be divided and lifted onto 4 in turn (lane BTp's
   statistics skeptic, worked by hand from this section's first text).
   A gap is where the ladder skipped a value the real column held at
   fewer rows than the ladder resolves, so a new stratum belongs there,
   and no run that a stretch of the ladder reads moves off its value.
4. **The carrier and reach steps** of G5.2b read piece for band. The
   band step moves one stratum into a piece that cannot carry from the
   nearest piece in rank order (the lower on a tie) that keeps at least
   its `lo_p`. The cell step moves cells only within one piece. The
   reach step asks for a whole number inside the stratum's own piece
   (and, as before, inside `min` and `max` and on its sign), and the
   fallbacks it treats as spoken for are G5.7e's piece fallbacks.

Every step of the layout moves cells only by moving boundaries between
strata of one piece. So when the layout ends, the strata of piece `p`
hold exactly `C_p` cells.

#### G5.7e The values inside their pieces, and the piece fallback

G5.3 gives each stratum its value as before, reading the ladder through
the band map: the pinned `min` and `max`, the zero stratum's 0, a
drawn stratum's convex form at its share, a grid stratum's grid value
at one of its own ranks, and the tail readings of G5.3b to G5.3e on the
tail's own ranks. G5.4's integer rule follows. Then G5.5's sign repair
is widened into the PIECE REPAIR, applied to every stratum in stratum
order: a stratum whose value is not inside its piece takes the piece's
FALLBACK on the side it left.

The pinned strata are never moved by it. By (P5) `min` stands in the
lowest piece with cells and `max` in the highest, and the zero stratum
is 0.

**The piece fallback.** For a piece of values from `a` up to `b`, a
value is ADMISSIBLE where it is inside `min` and `max` where they are
published, on the piece's side of zero, a whole number where `integer_valued` is
true, a point of the piece's grid where the column is on a written grid
(G5.2a step 1, G5.7b), and outside every stretch `empty_edges` names.

- **On a grid** (the whole numbers, or a written grid of `f` figures),
  the low fallback is the smallest admissible grid point at or above
  `a`, and the high fallback the largest admissible grid point below
  `b`. Where another stratum already holds that point, the walk goes
  inward one grid unit at a time, at most 64 units, to the first
  admissible point no stratum holds, as G5.5's grid rule walks; where
  every point within reach is held, the first point is taken.
- **Off a grid**, the low fallback is the first admissible value at or
  above `a`: `a` itself, or, where `a` lies in a stretch `empty_edges`
  names, that stretch's upper end. The high fallback is the largest
  value any other stratum of the piece already holds below `b`, and the
  low fallback where none holds one. Neither is a value the walls make
  up, so neither can stand in an empty stretch, and a stretch holding
  `a` ends inside the piece, because the piece's real values lie outside
  every empty stretch (P3). Where a fallback is a value another stratum
  holds, the two strata share it until G6.5a's separation, which acts
  inside the piece, pulls them apart.
- **Beside zero**, on a piece whose upper end is 0 or whose lower end is
  0, G5.5's own fallback (`-1`, `1`, or its grid walk) is taken where it
  lies inside the piece, and the piece's fallback otherwise.

By (P3) and the piece grid every piece with cells holds an admissible
value, so the repair always ends inside the piece. After it, every stratum's value lies in
its piece, so every piece holds its cells where its cut ranks say.

#### G5.7f The value passes after G5 keep each stratum in its piece

Every later step that changes a stratum's VALUE takes its candidate
values inside the stratum's piece, wherever today it takes them inside
the stratum's sign band, inside `min` and `max`, or inside a histogram
bin. No step changes a stratum's size across a cut. The steps are
named here so that an implementer finds each one:

- G5.2a's narrower-width exchanges and moves: two neighbouring strata
  exchange values only within one piece, and a move's new number lies
  inside the stratum's piece, beside "keeps the sign, and stands in the
  same histogram bin";
- G6.4's values step, which may take a stratum to a whole number: the
  whole number lies inside the stratum's piece;
- G6.5a's separation and its fill: a stratum moves only onto a free
  grid point inside its piece, and "a grid with no spare point is
  filled" is read piece by piece, so where a piece's strata number
  exactly the grid points it holds inside `min` and `max`, they take
  those points in ascending order, each once. This is how a count of
  few values gets the cells of a band holding one value onto that one
  value. A stratum G5.7d item 3a made in a gap already stands on a
  point no other stratum holds, so the walk never moves it, and since
  `hi_p` never gives a piece more strata than its runs and free points
  (save where the cap's floor raised it, G5.7d item 3), the fill of a
  piece takes every run's own value and lifts none;
- G6.6's snap to a published width, and G6.6.8's rules: the snapped
  value lies inside the stratum's piece;
- G6.7's moves out of an empty stretch: the stretch a stratum moves to
  is the nearest occupied one inside its piece, and (P3) proves there is
  one;
- G6A: the core view is G5 and G6 unchanged (G6A.2), so it takes all of
  the above. G6B: where lane MBC's contract gives a joined column's
  positions an L0 block each, each position handed to G5 (G6B.2) runs
  this section on its own block; the pairing walk of G6B.4 exchanges
  values between cells without changing either position's multiset, so
  it moves no band total;
- G6.8: a count column publishing every spelling is written as those
  spellings at their counts, which is the real multiset itself, so every
  band holds its count with nothing to do.

Where a step finds no candidate inside the piece that its own rule
accepts, it leaves the stratum where it stands, never outside its
piece, and the fact the step was serving gives way, named (rule B1,
G5.7h).

#### G5.7g The last guard

After the last value step (G6.7 and G6.8) and before any cell is
written as text, every stratum's value is read against its piece once
more, and a stratum outside its piece takes the piece fallback of
G5.7e. On the rules above this finds nothing to do. It stands so that
the band totals hold by construction even where a later amendment adds
a value step that forgets the walls. Every stratum it moves is named in
the twin's report, with the fact the move cost, if any.

#### G5.7h What each published fact owes on an eligible column

**The band totals are EXACT.** By G5.7b to G5.7g, every piece holds the
cells its cut ranks give it, every stratum's value lies inside its
piece, and a band is a union of pieces.

| fact | class today | with L0 | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_zero`, `n_negative`, `n_negative_unrepresentable` | EXACT | held | the sign cuts are cuts; the zero piece is the zero stratum; the piece repair keeps the sign |
| `min`, `max` where published | EXACT | held | pinned in the extreme pieces with cells (P5) |
| a tail block's rows, distances, listed values, heaped ends and derived ends | as G5.6a and G12.13 | held as today where no edge equals a boundary rung; where one does, rule B1 | the band map moves no tail row and (P4) keeps every edge inside the boundaries; where an edge equals the low boundary rung, the piece repair puts on the boundary the tail rows the cut puts at or above it, as the real column's own rows at that boundary stood, and a tail distance that moves is named |
| the four class counts, `n_present`, `n_missing`, `numeric_share`, `n_used_in_statistics`, `n_left_out_of_statistics` | EXACT | held | L0 lays out the `K` cells G5 lays out and touches no other cell |
| `integer_valued` | EXACT | held | every fallback on a whole column is whole |
| the eleven rungs and `percentiles_between` | APPROXIMATED | held, in windows read through the band map | G12.15 |
| `mean`, `std`, `skew`, `kurtosis` | APPROXIMATED | held, in windows read through the band map | G12.15 |
| `mode`, `mode_count` | REPORT-ONLY, the count a ceiling | held | the cap is kept piece by piece; a piece of `C_p` cells with `v_p` admissible values held at most `v_p * Cap` cells in the real column too, and `lo_p` asks only `ceil(C_p / Cap)` strata |
| `empty_bins`, `empty_edges` | EXACT | held | every candidate and every fallback lies outside the named stretches, and (P3) gives each piece room |

| `value_histogram` | REPORT-ONLY | measured as today | |

**RULE B1: the band totals stand.** Where a step cannot meet another
published fact without moving a cell across a cut, the cut stands and
that fact gives way, named in the twin's report exactly as the step
names a miss today. Why the cut wins: the band totals are the margins
of every published family table holding the column, so giving one up
sends every such table to G16.6's moved targets, while a missed style
count or count of different values costs that one count; and plan
P2-D6's feasibility rule 4 already ranks a published count above ladder
conformance. The real column meets both facts at once, so each such
miss is this construction's and not the description's. Rule B1 is how
the generator behaves, and it excuses nothing: K-S6-02 (iv) below
counts every B1 miss as a KPI miss, beside the target 0.

**RULE B2: no conflict where the arithmetic proves none.** The sign
counts, the ends, the class counts, `integer_valued` and the empty
stretches never conflict with the band totals on a description passing
(P1) to (P5), because each is an identity of the real column that the
cut ranks restate.

**RULE B3: a description L0 cannot lay out.** Where (P1) to (P5)
fail, the column is made without L0 and named, and G16.6 meets its
families. A hand-written description reaches it, and so can a real
column a producer describes: a column where a band's or a piece's
cells were all written at widths the census counts into its commonest
width can fail (P3), and where it does it is made without L0 under
this rule and named (G5.7a; G14.3a case 17).

**`K-S6-02`, reworded.** The stage-6 KPI read "every within-column fact
unchanged with and without stage 6". With L0 an eligible column's cells
are no longer today's cells, so a twin made with stage 6 can no longer
be compared with one made without it. For lane BT to stamp, it reads:

1. with `relationships.statistical` `null`, every twin is byte for byte
   today's twin, over the every-role battery: 0 differences;
2. each eligible column's cells, as a multiset, are identical before
   and after G16's arrangement, and so is every column's description of
   the twin: 0 differences;
3. each eligible column's twin holds every published L0 band count
   exactly, on the every-role battery and on the product's own twins at
   5,000, 20,000 and 200,000 rows: 0 rows off;
4. 0 within-column facts that the twin made without L0 HOLDS and the
   twin made with it MISSES, on the every-role battery and on the
   product's own twins. Both twins are judged by one yardstick: every
   EXACT fact exactly, and the rungs and moments in today's windows of
   G12.2, G12.3 and G12.3a, at G12.2's half unit, extended only beside
   a cut as G12.15 says. Each such fact is a KPI miss, rule
   B1's among them, listed by column and fact; the count of them is
   stamped beside the target 0, and a count above 0 is a named residual
   in the plan, never a pass. Rule B1 says how the generator settles a
   conflict; it is not an allowance of this KPI. The only columns
   outside this clause are the rule-computed columns of stage 6 (a
   column computed from an order rule, a column rebuilt from the visit
   order), listed by name as the between-columns design names them;
5. within the bands, on every count column of the every-role battery
   and of the product's own twins (where the real table is at hand):
   the twin's count at each value, summed over each band as
   `sum |twin count - real count|`, is no larger with L0 than without
   it, and each published rung the twin's own description reads is no
   further from the published rung with L0 than without it: 0
   regressions. G14.3a case 1 is the case this clause exists for: walls
   that only moved the count of few values' cascade into its top band
   would pass items 3 and 4 and fail this one.

No new KPI is added, and no count is published that was not published
before.

## G6. Numeric spelling

### G6.1 The permitted family

Owner decisions 7, 8 and 10 fix the family. A numeric cell is written in
exactly one of six **styles**, and in no other form:

| style | what it writes | changes the type a reader infers? |
|---|---|---|
| `plain` | the canonical spelling (G6.2) | no |
| `leading_zero` | canonical, with one or more `0` characters inserted immediately after the sign | no |
| `leading_plus` | canonical, with a `+` written before a non-negative canonical spelling | no |
| `decimal` | the value in fixed-point notation with at least one digit after the point | yes — a whole-number column reads as a decimal one |
| `exponent_lower` | the value in exponent notation with a lower-case `e` | yes |
| `exponent_upper` | the value in exponent notation with an upper-case `E` | yes |

**A thousands separator only where the column publishes one** (`group_separator`, contract 6 numeric block; stage 2, 2026-09-14). The ruling that stood here — that a separator is never written because the comma breaks the CSV row itself — was false: a cell holding a comma is quoted by the CSV writer and read back unchanged. It was the whole cause of a defect in which a grouped charge column came back ungrouped and code developed on the twin silently discarded every charge over a thousand from the real table. Where `group_separator` is `,` or `.`, every `plain` cell, and every `leading_plus` or `decimal` cell at leading-zero order zero, is grouped with a comma, so a column whose proving cells were the majority is written wholly grouped; a `leading_zero` cell, an exponent form and a cell at a raised order are never grouped (the stage 2 audit, 2026-09-14). A column declared to write its decimals with a comma publishes `.`: it is grouped with a comma like any other and then has its points and commas exchanged, so `42,037.34` is written `42.037,34`.

**Every mark a column may publish, and every notation of a negative, and a plus on a decimal** (landing 2b.2, 2026-09-15; plan P4-D41). A column publishing a space, an apostrophe, U+2019, U+00A0, U+202F or U+2009 is grouped with that mark itself, under the same rule of forms and order; no exchange touches it, so a declared decimal-comma column grouped with a space is written `1 234,56`. Where `decimal_plus` names a count, the cells allocated `decimal` whose value is not negative are taken in cell order, P being the lesser of the named count and their number E, and the plus is placed on WHOLE VALUES (integration repair of landing 2b.2: placed cell by cell, three values written fifty times each, one with a plus, came back as six spellings, and 900 signed changes publishing 690 spellings as 780). Those cells form runs of one value, in cell order; a run from cell `a` to cell `b - 1` is offered `floor(b·P/E) - floor(a·P/E)` pluses and takes one on every cell where that offer is at least half its length. While the cells taken exceed P, the taken run with the smallest offer per cell no longer than the excess is given up; while they fall short, the untaken run with the largest offer per cell no longer than the shortfall is taken, the earlier run first on a tie. What whole runs still cannot meet is spread inside one run -- the last taken run where the total is over, keeping its length less the excess, or the first untaken run at least as long as the shortfall -- and a run of length m holding k pluses gives its j-th cell, counting from nought, a plus exactly where `floor((j+1)·k/m)` exceeds `floor(j·k/m)`; so a column whose decimal cells all hold one value is spread one in every `E/P` exactly as before; a pooled count names no form and adds no plus; the plus stands in front of any zeros the cell spends. Before any fraction width is assigned (G6.6), where fewer cells are allocated `decimal` on a value not negative than the named count, cells exchange forms: each cell allocated `plain` or `leading_zero` whose value is not negative, from the first cell upward, takes the first cell, from the last cell downward, allocated `decimal` whose value is negative, has a point-free spelling, is not yet taken, and -- where the giver is `leading_zero` -- writes no more figures than the giver does, so the field width the padded exchange fitted it to is still reachable; each pair swaps its two forms, for as many pairs as the shortfall allows; no form count moves (integration repair of landing 2b.2: only `plain` gave, and a column of `-001` beside `+2.00` and `+3.00` came back with none of its hundred pluses). Where E is still below `decimal_plus` every eligible cell carries one and the report names a deviation of `decimal_plus`. Every negative cell is then written in the column's `negative_form`: the figures after the hyphen-minus, zeros and mark included, inside brackets, after the minus sign U+2212, or followed by a hyphen-minus -- the last only where those figures carry a decimal point, because neither `12-` nor `1,234-` is read as a number, so such a cell keeps its hyphen-minus in front. So `(001234.5)` and `(1,234.5)` are written and `(0,001.00)` never is.

**A mixture of conventions is written as a mixture** (landing 2b.7, 2026-09-15; plan P4-D65.2). `negative_form` and `group_separator` publish the column's MAJORITY, and writing every cell that way threw the minority away: 480 negatives with a minus beside 120 in accounting brackets came back as 600 minuses, and 200 cells grouped with a space beside 100 grouped with a narrow no-break space came back as 300 ordinary spaces, each with no deviation reported and no check missed. Where `negative_notations` names a notation, each named notation takes its count in turn from the cells holding a negative value that no earlier notation took; where `thousands_marks` names a mark, the cells that CAN be grouped are taken the same way. **EACH COUNT IS SPREAD ACROSS THE VALUES, NOT TAKEN FROM THE FIRST CELL UPWARD** (plan P4-D149, the repair pass of the final Codex review).
