   midnight of the boundary's own day.

7. **A rank standing at ONE PLACE steps off a hole and onto a midnight.**
   The outermost rank and the tie group draw no word, so each stands at
   one place and two rules apply to them, in this order:

   - a tail group of a column whose count at midnight is published and
     whose unit is a minute or a second stands at the midnight NEAREST
     its own distance inside the strata it covers -- the local midnight of a
     named offset's wall clock, the inner taken on a tie, its own
     distance where none lies in reach. Its strata reach
     `k * a((m - (F - 1)) / m)`, rounded as above. NOT where the
     published count is held whole by the tails listing only midnight
     values (landing 3b.2-H, plan P4-D371): `n_at_midnight` less the rows
     of every tail whose listed values all stand at midnight is nought, so
     no other cell stands at one, and a group stood there wrote cells at
     midnight the description does not count -- an epoch sentinel's
     clinic at a floor of 36 missed `midnight.count` at every seed, two
     over;
   - a rank whose unit is named by one of the column's own published
     absent spellings, read under the column's own member, steps one
     unit INWARD until it is not, never below one unit. A derived end
     that is a declared missing value would be written as a cell the
     twin's own description reads as absent (the skeptic of the tail
     design, B8);
   - the END of a column of moments whose count at midnight is published,
     read on its own clock, its unit a minute or a second, standing at a
     written midnight -- after the step off the holes -- takes one of the
     cells at midnight the count leaves the ends, the low tail's first: the
     published count less the body's cells at midnight for certain (hour
     0's count where the hour census counts it alone, less the body's
     cells off minute 0 -- the body less the minute's heap or lone census
     group at 0 -- and less those off second 0, none written to the minute;
     nought where below nought, finer than the second or hour 0 grouped)
     and less the rows each tail listing its values holds at midnight for
     certain (all, where every listed value is one; else one for each
     that is). Where none is left it steps one unit INWARD, as off a hole,
     until it stands at no midnight and on no hole, never below one unit;
     the checker's window reads the same (G12.14). A column on the hour
     at 1,000 rows owed 11 cells at midnight, all of them its body's hour 0, and
     its high tail's end derived at 2024-12-31 00:00 held a twelfth: the
     heap at minute 0 came back one short at every seed (the Codex review
     of landing 3b.4, item 4).

   The end is then raised to the group's distance where the group is
   further out, so the two stay in rank order.

8. **The gap of a tail rank IS its stratum** (G12.4): the two distances
   its own construction gives it at a word of nought and at the largest
   word, widened to the whole DAY it may be moved inside where one unit
   is a day of the shared clock -- half a day below and one second less
   than half a day above, so the room is exactly one day wide and two
   neighbouring ranks' rooms never name one instant twice -- inside
   which the move onto a local midnight may take it anywhere. Every later pass -- the step off a hole, the counts of
   different values and of widths, and the moves onto and off midnight
   -- moves a rank only inside its gap, which is what keeps every
   published tail fact inside the window of G12.14.

9. **The tie group gives way where the distinct count is short** (plan
   P4-D354, landing 3b.0). The group's gap is its one distance, so the
   count pass can never split it, and a column holding a value on every
   day of its range came back a day short: two years of admissions, 731
   days, twin 730 at every seed, the day one unit beyond the boundary
   never written and both distinct counts missed. So where the column's
   count of different units is still below its published count once the
   count pass is done (G7.3, plan P4-D192), each tail's group of `G >= 2`
   ranks -- outer indices `max(F - 1, 1)` to `m - 1` -- is offered the
   units no rank holds from one to its REACH `t`: `k * a((m - (F - 1)) /
   m)` rounded as in step 5, at least the group's distance `g` and never
   past the end. A unit an absent spelling of the run names (step 7,
   G7.3), or of another width kind or midnight standing than the group's,
   is not offered, so
   a group at a midnight is offered only units at a midnight and a group
   off one no unit at one. Each offer is a tail and a distance `d`, and
   the offers are taken in this order until the count is met: the
   smaller `|d - g|` first; at one `|d - g|`, the smaller `d` first --
   on one tail the unit inside `g` before the one outside it, across the
   two tails the unit nearer its own boundary; at one `|d - g|` and one
   `d`, the low tail first. Each group keeps one rank on `g`, and the
   window of G12.14 is summed with it there. A group's
   units inside `g` go to its innermost ranks, the smallest to the
   innermost; its units outside `g` to its outermost ranks, the largest to
   the outermost. Every drawn rank stands at `t` or beyond, so no rank
   passes another. No word is drawn. `rows` and the boundary stand, and
   G12.14 draws its window to hold every twin this writes. Two bounds
   have no witness, because no description found reaches them: the
   reach itself -- offering the unit one past `t` changed none of 1,107
   twins of the 427 descriptions searched for it (plan P4-D354) -- and
   the width kind, whose offer changed none of 640 twins of 80
   month-first columns on the days 10 to 31 of a month, each at its
   published count and raised by one, two and three.

10. **The dial's half day** (landing 3b.2-H, plan P4-D371; plan P4-D370's
   carve-out). On a slashed stamp the person declared a 12-hour clock
   written with no marker (`--twelve-hour`) -- or a layout whose hour is
   that dial's, `{hh}`, `{h}` or `{_h}`, beside no marker field (landing
   R2b, at batch 3's integration) -- every value the column holds
   reads from 00:00 to 11:59 of its day, and a twin instant past noon is
   written on the dial and reads twelve hours earlier. The half day is a
   half of the day each cell writes, so it is taken only where the
   column is read at its own wall clock: a column of several offsets is
   read at UTC, its moments count UTC seconds, and a morning written at
   -0500 is a UTC afternoon there; such a column takes no step here, nor
   G7.3g's half day, and is drawn over its UTC day as P4-D370 states (the
   Codex review of landing I3a, item 1: 1,000 SAS stamps written 10:00 to
   10:08 at -0500 and -0400 had their low tail taken onto the UTC
   morning and missed 15 obligations at seed 0, none since). So every distance
   of such a tail -- counted in seconds and minutes as every other moment
   tail is -- stands on the HALF DAY: its place, `u` seconds a unit
   beyond the boundary, lies from one unit past midnight to the last unit
   before noon. Once steps 1 to 6 have drawn a distance whose place does
   not, it is taken to the nearest distance whose place does -- the
   later place of the morning after, or the earlier of the morning before
   -- the nearer the boundary on a tie, and at least one. Where the
   ranks must all differ, the two passes of step 5's all-different rule
   are made again over such distances alone: from the innermost out,
   each made the next one past the one inside it, then, from the
   outermost in, the one before the one outside it; and each is kept at
   the furthest such distance within the edge. The tie group's own
   distance is taken so before the ranks are drawn, so step 9 offers
   around the distance the group stands at, and step 9 offers no unit
   off the half day. Every one of these steps is monotone in every
   distance, so the strata of step 8 and the window of G12.14, drawn
   through it, bound every rank. A tail of the shared clock's days, and
   a column wholly at midnight, take no step: their ranks stand at a
   midnight already. No other tail rank of the half day stands at a
   written midnight, so the move onto a midnight spreads the published
   count over the body alone (G7.5). Measured at 1,000 rows of a year of such stamps,
   seeds 0 to 2: 10, 11 and 5 obligations MISSED before (rungs, tail
   distances and both distinct counts), none after.

#### G7.3c A tail that publishes which values it holds

*Stage 3, plan P4-D329 (the owner's ruling of 2026-09-22).* Where a tail
holds few different values, or where its two distances would settle the
outermost value or a count below the floor, the description publishes
the tail's sorted distinct `values` instead of its root-mean-square
distance, and its mean distance beside them only where that settles no
count below the floor (contract DT1, DT3). It publishes them only where
each of its DISTANCES carries one canonical text; where a distance
carries two -- which a day of the shared clock does, holding a bare
date's midnight and a moment's two hours before it -- the tail
publishes its two distances instead, and the ranks it holds are drawn
through the shape below like any other.

The twin then writes the tail ON THOSE VALUES AND NOWHERE ELSE. With the
values in distance order, outermost first, and `m = rows`:

- every value takes at least one rank;
- with the mean published, `T = round(m * mean_distance)` halves up is
  the whole sum the counts must reach exactly. Each value from the
  outermost inward takes the FEWEST ranks that still leave the values
  inside it able to reach `T` exactly -- asked by a table over how many
  ranks are left and what they must still add, in whole numbers -- and
  the innermost takes the rest;
- with no mean published, or where no count can reach `T`, rank `i` of
  the tail takes value number `floor(i * v / m)` of the `v` values, so
  the ranks are shared as evenly as the values allow, the outer values
  first;
- **except that a column publishing `n_at_midnight` shares them by that
  count instead** (stage 3). With the mean withheld the description says
  only that each value is held at least once, so every other rank is the
  construction's to place, and it places them where the column's other
  EXACT facts need them: each value takes one rank, and the rest go to
  the first value, outermost first, that stands at a local midnight
  where the column publishes more cells at midnight than not, or that
  does not where it publishes fewer. Where no value answers, the even
  share above stands. Measured: 1,000 moments over five days under two
  offsets, 980 at local midnight, whose high tail lists a midnight and a
  noon and withholds its mean because three rows held the noon -- the
  even share wrote 102 noon cells for those three and the twin missed
  `n_at_midnight` by 84 and `all_at_midnight` with it.

Each of those ranks stands at its value's own ordinal and draws no word.
Its gap is that one place, so no later pass moves it.

#### G7.3d A column with no tails: the made-up ramp

*Stage 3, plan P4-D330.* A column too small for a boundary on each side,
or one so tied at an end that the two boundaries cross (contract DT2),
publishes no tail, no rung and no value of the table at all. Its cells
are still counted, so the twin writes a RAMP that meets the counts and
claims nothing: rank `0` stands at 1970-01-01 -- ordinal nought in every
space of G7.1 -- and rank `P - 1` at `(D - 1)` steps later, where `D` is
the column's published count of different values less the cells that
read as no date, capped at `P` and at least one, and the step is one
unit of the space, a whole DAY for a column counted in seconds so that
the passes onto and off midnight have a midnight of each day to reach. Every rank
between the two is drawn in the gap between them exactly as a body rank
is, and every later pass runs unchanged, so the published counts of
different values, of values at midnight, of resolutions and of written
forms are reached where the construction can reach them. The quality
report lists every value-bearing obligation of such a column as
withheld (validation method V3.5).

#### G7.3e The readable window a tail is kept inside

*Stage 3, plan P4-D331 (the skeptic of the tail design, B2 and B3).* A
twin cell must read back as the value the twin holds, so no rank of a
tail is placed where the column's own spelling cannot spell it:

- the calendar itself, the years 0001 to 9999, for every member;
- 1969-01-01 to 2068-12-31 for a member that writes a TWO-FIGURE YEAR,
  whose century the reader settles at `parsing.TWO_DIGIT_YEAR_PIVOT`:
  a twin that writes 1968 as `68` is read back as 2068 (measured:
  8 of 16 twins of a `dd/mm/yy` column wrote 1 to 3 such cells, each
  missing 4 to 7 of the tail's own checks);
- for a LAYOUT (landing R2a, plan P4-D383), its year band,
  1800-01-01 to 2299-12-31, where its year is four figures, and its
  window where it is two: 1969 to 2068 under `{YY}`, and under
  `{YY1900}`, `{YY1930}` or `{YY1940}` the window the person chose
  (question Q5), 1900 to 1999, 1930 to 2029 or 1940 to 2039 -- a twin
  writing a year outside it would be read back as another, or not at
  all;
- from the first day the workbook's date system can store, where the
  twin's cells are stored as workbook days: 1900-01-01 for the 1900
  system and 1904-01-01 for the 1904 one;
- on the SHARED clock, those edges come in by the widest offset the
  census names, because each cell is written on its own offset's wall
  clock -- and by one whole day where the unit is a day of that clock.

The edge is then the furthest distance from the boundary inside that
window, at least one unit. **The calendar is not inset on the local
clock**: a column holding a heap of `0001-01-01 00:00:00` -- the "no
date" value of two common systems -- is floor-safe, and its twin writes
that day exactly (measured: 40 cells of 40, against 0 under a one-day
inset).

#### G7.3f The weekday census: the day pass

*Stage 3b, landing 3b.1, plans P4-D355 and P4-D359.* Where a column of whole dates
publishes a non-empty `weekday_census` (contract WC1 to WC4 and WC6), with both
tails, at least three parsed cells and no bare date, its ranks are moved
once G7.3's count passes and G7.3b step 9 are done and before any cell
is spelled, until the cells between the two boundary ranks fall on the
published groups. No word is drawn.

A COLUMN OF MOMENTS (landing 3b.D2, plan P4-D367; contract WC3 and WC10)
is moved by the same pass over its instants: its unit and its day are
86,400 seconds, so a move of whole units keeps the moment's clock; its
written unit is the minute where it is written to the minute and the
second otherwise; its bin is the weekday of the day an instant falls on;
and its holes are the days the description publishes empty -- an absent
spelling of the run names one instant of a day there, never every
spelling of it, so it makes no day a hole -- save, on a column of dates
written as counts, the placeholder days every instant of which reads
back as no value (G7.10). A column of moments every
value of which stands at midnight on its own clock is counted in days
(G7.1) and moved as a column of dates is. Steps 7c and 8.7 below are
asked of moments alone.

THE CENSUS AS WRITTEN (Codex's review of landing 3b.D2, item 1). The
census counts a cell on the day it is WRITTEN on, and the pass counts a
rank on its ordinal's day. The two differ only on a body rank the layout
pins at a published boundary or rung whose seconds field is 60, standing
at that pin, or standing between two such pins of one moment, which G7.5
writes from that moment's own fields at that sixtieth second while its
ordinal is the next second: at `23:59:60` its ordinal's day is the day
after the one it is written on. These are the ranks G7.3g's clock pass
counts in the hour they are written in, one set for both censuses. Before the
pass, each such rank whose ordinal's group is not the group of the day
of the second before its ordinal is asked one more in the first group
and one fewer in the second; it never moves, so the pass, meeting these
counts by ordinal, meets the published census as written (fifty
`2016-12-31 23:59:60` beside noon stamps publish Saturday 130 and Sunday
80, and the twin, its pinned 25th percentile at that second, wrote 131
and 79 without this).

A day `d`, counted from 1970-01-01, falls on weekday `(d + 3) mod 7`,
Monday nought; its GROUP is the census group holding that weekday. Its
KIND is whether a date on it counts into the width census's one word,
where the member can show a width and that census names exactly one
word, and one kind for every day otherwise. A HOLE is a day between
the two boundary days that the description holds empty: one the
column's own member writes -- at its one width word and its one
month-name word, the defaults where it has none -- in an absent spelling
of the run, folded (every column's `missing_by_source` keys, and the
placeholder days the settings' declaration of missing values names);
one its `sentinel_verdicts` read as no value; and one its censuses of
written forms leave empty -- a width word naming the first field alone
leaves every day whose second field is below ten, one naming the second
field alone every day whose first is, and a month name of the length
`either` every day outside May (contract WC6, the holes the producer
asks with, plan P4-D365). `held(d)` is how
many ranks of the column stand on `d`. A rank is MOVABLE where it lies
between the two boundary ranks, both included, the layout does not pin
it and its gap (G7.3) is more than one day; the movable ranks form GAPS,
each a run of consecutive movable ranks sharing one gap. A rank's
CANDIDATES are the days `d - 1, d + 1, d - 2, d + 2, ...` from its own
day `d`, up to 400 days away, those inside its gap only, the search
ending once both sides lie outside it.

**THE SEAMS** (landing 3b.D0, plan P4-D366). The pass is ONE over any
census of bins, and every landing that publishes one states its seams;
for the weekday census of a column of whole dates they are the ones the
text above reads, and for a census of hours they are an hour's. An
ORDINAL is a rank's value in its column's space -- a day for a date, a
second for a moment. The UNIT `u` is how many ordinals lie between two
places a rank may take: 1 for a date's day, 86,400 for a moment's day,
3,600 for an hour, 60 for a minute. A rank's candidates are then
`o - u, o + u, o - 2u, ...` from its own ordinal `o`, up to 400 UNITS
away, so a move keeps the rank's place inside its unit -- its clock, on a
day of moments. The WRITTEN UNIT `s`, a divisor of `u`, is how many
ordinals one written value spans: `held` counts the ranks on each
written unit `o div s`, and the count of different values is the count
of written units held. The DAY `D` is how many ordinals a day spans; a
hole is a day, `o div D`, and so is what the width kind reads. An
ordinal's BIN is the bin the census counts it in -- here its weekday --
and its GROUP the census group holding that bin; where bins follow one
another unit by unit they repeat every PERIOD units (seven here). An
ordinal's KIND is three things: whether its day counts into the width
word, as above; what every move KEEPS besides -- nothing here, the day
`o div 86,400` for a census of hours, so an hour moves inside its own
day, and where the day is kept the searches of steps 2 to 8.4 ask the
rank's own day alone, the only part of its gap its kind allows (the
Codex review of landing 3b.D0, items 2 and 3: step 8.3 built every unit
of a group across a gap of D days for each of its D cells, and step
8.4 walked every day of it for each unit); and a second
census's group, nought where there is none, which only step 8.6
changes. Bin, kind and hole are read alike on every ordinal of
a unit. A unit is FREE where no rank stands on any ordinal of it. Where
a step below says a day, it is a unit; where it says a day's ranks, a
written unit's.

1. **Owed.** Each group owes its published count less the ranks
   between the two boundary ranks, both included, that are not movable
   and whose day falls in it.
2. **The holes.** A movable rank drawn onto a hole moves off it before
   anything else moves: to its first candidate that is no hole and of
   its own kind and that KEEPS the count of different days -- the rank
   alone on the hole and no rank on the candidate, or sharing the hole
   and a rank on the candidate -- or, failing one, to its first
   candidate that is no hole and of its kind. No later step puts a rank
   on a hole.
3. **Shares.** For gap `j` of `n_j` ranks and group `g`, the prior
   `a[j][g]` is how many of the gap's ranks stand on a day of `g`,
   times `2**20`, plus `d * n_j // D`, where `d` counts the gap's days
   of `g` that are no hole at `2**20` each and its two end days -- the
   pinned days it is drawn between -- at `2**19`, and `D` is the sum of
   `d` over the groups divided by `2**20`, rounded down (`d * n_j // D`
   is nought where `D` is); and `x = a`. The ranks as drawn and the
   calendar weigh the same: the drawn ranks keep the moves few and a
   gap drawn only a few days wide from piling its share of a weekday
   onto its one day of it, and the days give a gap drawn with no rank
   on a weekday its part of that weekday, so the census's few cells of
   one weekday are not all sent to the one gap whose draw held them.
   Sixty times over: each gap whose
   `S = sum_g x[j][g]` is above nought takes
   `x[j][g] = x[j][g] * n_j * 2**20 // S`; then each group whose
   `C = sum_j x[j][g]` is above nought takes
   `x[j][g] = x[j][g] * max(owed_g, 0) * 2**20 // C`. Each gap is then
   rounded: where `S > 0`, `q[j][g] = x[j][g] * n_j // S`, and the ranks
   left over go one each to the groups in order of
   `(x[j][g] * n_j) mod S`, largest first and then the lower group,
   passing over a group whose prior is nought; where `S` is nought,
   every `q[j][g]` is nought. While one group's total `sum_j q[j][g]`
   stands above its owed total, taken at nought or above, and another's
   below, one share moves, at most 20,000 times: of every group over,
   every group under and every gap, in that order, the move from `g+` to
   `g-` inside a gap where `q[j][g+] > 0` and `a[j][g-] > 0` whose
   `(x[j][g-] - q[j][g-] * 2**20) - (x[j][g+] - q[j][g+] * 2**20)` is
   largest, the first met on a tie.
4. **Where a rank may go.** A candidate is a DESTINATION for `k` ranks
   where it is no hole, its kind is the rank's, and its group then
   holds no more than its share: `have + k <= want`.
5. **Whole runs**, gap by gap, up to eight rounds while the gap's
   holding is not its shares: every run of the gap's ranks on one day,
   days ascending, of two ranks or more, with no other rank of the
   column on its day, whose group holds at least its size above its
   share, moves whole onto its first candidate that is a destination for
   all of it and that no rank holds.
6. **Single ranks**, gap by gap after its runs, up to sixteen rounds
   while the gap's holding is not its shares. Each rank whose group
   holds more than its share is OFFERED, of its candidates that are
   destinations and KEEP the count of different days -- the rank alone
   on its day and no rank on the candidate, or sharing its day and a
   rank on the candidate -- the one holding the fewest ranks, the
   earlier candidate on a tie; or, failing any, the same of every
   destination, which CHANGES the count. Where the column's distinct
   count is not reachable (contract `datetime_counts_reachable`) every
   destination keeps it. Taking the fewest rather than the nearest
   spreads what a gap sends to a group over all of that group's days. The offers are taken in order of keeping
   first, then distance, then rank, each offered again when its turn
   comes. A changing offer is taken only once a round has made no
   keeping offer, or moved nothing, and from then on; a round that
   moves nothing then ends the step.
7. **The leftover.** Where the movable ranks together still do not hold
   the owed totals, taken at nought or above, step 6 runs once over all
   of them against those totals, up to sixty-four rounds, a changing
   offer taken from the start.

   **7b. The chain** (plan P4-D366). Where they still do not hold them,
   up to 256 rounds. A LINK from group `g` to group `h` is the first cell
   (step 8.3's cells, of the movable ranks, in its order) that holds a
   movable rank of `g` whose MOVER, as step 8.3 names it, has a place of
   `h`: step 8.3's `take(g, h)` is asked, and is not withheld. Breadth
   first from the groups over their totals, ascending, a group reached
   once and a group over its total never, each group's links asked in
   order of `h`, the first group under its total reached ends the search;
   each link of the path from the group over to the group under then
   makes, in turn, one move in its cell, from `g` to `h`: the mover of
   `g` there AS THE RANKS THEN STAND onto the place of `h` a move of
   step 8.3 takes, or, where that rank has no place of `h`, the mover
   the link was asked of (the repair of the verification of the Codex
   review of landing 3b.D0, item 1). A move of the path can put its rank
   on the next link's cell as that group's mover, at a place inside its
   unit the link was not asked of -- a unit of an hour, minutes written,
   the day kept, a gap from 00:47 to 10:39 holding 00:47 and 08:37, and
   the chain hour 0 to hours 1 to 9 to hour 10 moved 00:47 to 01:47,
   whose hour 10 place stands past the gap's close, and the chain was
   left half made where 08:37, the mover asked, has 10:37. Each group
   gives once in a path, so the mover asked is still there and its place
   still stands: every move finds its place, every group between keeps
   its holding and one rank goes from the first group to the last. On a
   date's day every rank of a cell has the same places, so the mover as
   the ranks then stand always has one. The step ends where no path is
   found.

   **7c. The escape to an end day** (landing 3b.D2, plan P4-D367). Where
   the unit is the day and spans more than one written unit -- a day of
   moments -- and the movable ranks still do not hold the owed totals,
   taken at nought or above, once step 7b is done. A rank's candidates
   keep its clock, so on the first and the last day of its gap, its END
   DAYS, only the ranks whose clocks stand inside the gap may move: a
   gap from a Wednesday at 11:00 to the next at 09:15 holds no Wednesday
   for a rank drawn at 10:00, and a census of Wednesday sessions is
   left short. Up to eight rounds, the movable ranks asked in rank order: a
   rank whose group holds more than its total is offered, on each end
   day of its gap other than its own day whose group holds less than its
   total, that is no hole and of the rank's kind, a PLACE -- an ordinal of
   that day inside the gap, a whole number of written units from the one
   nearest the rank's own place in its unit moved to that day, asked
   nearest that wished place first and then the earlier, at most 64 of
   them, and standing at the start of the day exactly where the rank's
   own place does, so no clock is put on midnight or taken off it. Of
   those places, the first that keeps the count of different values --
   onto a written unit no rank holds where the rank stands alone on its
   own, onto one a rank holds where it shares -- or, failing any, the
   first, which changes it; where the column's count is not reachable,
   the first. Of its two end days, the offer that keeps the count, then
   the nearer to the rank's own ordinal, then the lower. A round takes
   only the offers that keep the count until a round moves nothing, and
   every offer from then on; a round that moves nothing after that ends
   the rounds. Where the totals still do not hold, THE SHIFT, up to 64
   times: an end day whose group holds exactly its total offers its
   places as well, where a LINK of step 7b leads on from that group to a
   group under its total (a cell holding a rank of the group whose mover
   has a place of the group under). The first rank, in rank order, of a
   group over its total with such an offer takes it, chosen as above, and
   step 7b runs again; a shift after which the ranks the groups over their
   totals hold past them, summed, are no fewer ends the step, as does a
   round with no such group or no such offer. A Wednesday schedule at a
   floor of 36 had ranks at 15:16 to 17:58 in a gap from Tuesday 18:04 to
   Thursday 11:24, both of those groups at their totals and the group
   under them, Saturday, outside the gap, and fell five short of its
   census before the shift. It changes only the clocks of the ranks it moves;
   beside it only step 8.4's merge at another clock, step 8.5's pairs and
   step 8.7 change a written clock, each on the ranks it moves, and every
   other step keeps each rank's written clock.
8. **The count of different days**, where the column's distinct count
   is reachable, put back to what it was before step 2, by moves that
   keep every group's count:
   1. up to eight rounds, ranks in rank order: where the count is
      short, a rank sharing its day moves to the first candidate of its
      own group and kind that no rank holds; where it is long, a rank
      alone on its day moves to the first such candidate a rank holds;
      holes are never candidates, and at most 64 candidates of that
      group and kind are asked;
   2. where the count is still long, up to eight rounds: each RUN --
      the movable ranks of one day, all of one gap, with no other rank
      of the column on it -- the smallest first and then the earlier
      day, moves whole onto the first candidate of its own group and
      kind that a rank holds and that is no hole, until the count is
      back;
   3. where the count is still SHORT, up to 64 EXCHANGES across groups
      (review of landing 3b.1, item 5, plan P4-D359). A CELL is a gap
      and a width kind. In a cell, group `g`'s MOVER is its rank on the
      written unit holding the most ranks, the lower rank on a tie: the
      rank a move of `g` takes. `give(g)` is nought where the mover
      shares its written unit and minus one where it stands alone, and
      `take(g, h)` one where a PLACE the mover may take -- an ordinal a
      whole number of units from its own, inside its gap, of group `h`
      and the cell's kind, no hole -- stands on a written unit no rank
      holds, and nought where every such place's written unit a rank
      holds; neither is asked where the cell has no rank of `g` or the
      mover no such place. THE TAKE COUNTS WRITTEN UNITS at the mover's
      own place inside its unit, never whole units (the Codex review of
      landing 3b.D0, item 1): forty ranks each at 00:15, 01:15 and 02:30
      of one day, on a unit of an hour with minutes written and the day
      kept, asked for eighty in hour 1, forty in hour 2 and three
      values, were left on two, as hours 1 and 2 each held a rank while
      01:30 and 02:15 stood free. On a date's day a unit is one written
      unit and every rank of a cell has the same places, so the take is
      the day's. Each ordered pair
      of groups `(g, h)`, one group twice included, takes the largest
      `give(g) + take(g, h)` over the cells, the first cell on a tie,
      cells in order of their gap's first day, last day and kind, the
      kind a day outside the width word first. A CYCLE `g1, ..., gk`, each
      group once and `g1` the lowest, gains the sum over `(g1, g2)` to
      `(gk, g1)`; of the cycles gaining more than nought, the one whose
      gain is the largest not past what is short, else the smallest,
      then the fewest groups, then the earliest. Each pair in turn
      moves, in its cell, the mover its gain was asked of -- the mover of
      `g` as the ranks stood before the cycle -- onto the place of `h` of
      the cell's kind nearest it inside its gap, the whole gap asked and
      the earlier on a tie, whose written unit no rank holds and that is
      no hole, else the nearest one whose written unit a rank holds.
      EVERY MOVE FINDS ITS PLACE AND A CYCLE IS MADE WHOLE (plan P4-D366,
      the landing's review; restated where its Codex review's item 1 was
      verified): each group gives once in a cycle, so no move before a
      pair's moves its mover, and the place its take found still stands;
      every group keeps its count, and the count gains at least the
      cycle's gain. The mover of `g` as the ranks then stand lost gains:
      a move can put its rank on the next group's written unit holding
      the most ranks, or tie it lower in rank order, and that rank was
      moved straight back -- a unit of an hour, minutes written, the day
      kept, a day holding 00:14 three times and 01:07 alone, and the
      cycle hour 0 to hour 1 and back moved one 00:14 rank to 01:14 and
      back again, the count left one short where that move and 01:07,
      hour 1's mover, onto 00:07 meet it -- or found no place of the next
      group for it, and the cycle was undone. Where a unit is one written
      unit and every cycle is asked, the count, as a function of how many
      ranks each cell puts on each group, is a sum of `min(ranks, free
      days)` -- concave -- so where no cycle gains it is the most the
      census allows the body around the tail dates the twin wrote, which
      may hold fewer different days than the real tails. A count left
      long is steps 1 and 2's again. THE CYCLES ASKED ARE BOUNDED (plan
      P4-D366): every cycle where the census has at most seven groups,
      and only cycles of at most three groups where it has more, as
      every cycle of thirty-one groups of days of the month is too many
      to ask. SO A COUNT LEFT SHORT MAY BE BELOW THE MOST THE CENSUS
      ALLOWS where it has more than seven groups, or where a unit spans
      more than one written unit (the Codex review of landing 3b.D0,
      item 6). Ten groups of days of the month -- the first to the ninth
      each alone, the tenth to the thirty-first together -- with two
      ranks each on 1 January, 2 February, 3 March and 4 April, their
      gaps ending on 2 January, 3 February, 4 March and 1 May, asked for
      eight different days, keep four: only a cycle of four groups, one
      rank of each day onto its gap's last day, reaches eight. And on a
      unit wider than its written unit a group's ranks in a cell stand
      at different places inside their units, so the count is no such
      sum, and the take is asked of the mover alone.
   4. **Units merged** (plan P4-D366), where the count is still LONG, up
      to four rounds, a round that merges nothing ending the step: every
      written unit whose every rank is movable, the fewest ranks first
      and then the earlier unit, where it still holds those ranks and no
      other, moves WHOLE -- every rank on it onto one place -- inside the
      gap all its ranks share (the latest first day and the earliest last
      day of their gaps), the whole of it asked. First onto the nearest
      ordinal a whole number of units away, the earlier on a tie, of its
      own group and kind, no hole, whose written unit a rank holds: so at
      its own place inside the unit, its clock on a day of moments (the
      3b.2-W skeptic, minor 2). Else, where a unit spans more than one
      written unit, onto the nearest ordinal a rank stands on, the
      earlier on a tie, of its own group and kind, no hole, on another
      written unit, that is the start of a day exactly where its own
      place is. The step stops once the count is back.
   5. **Long pairs** (plan P4-D366; landing 3b.6's step), where the count
      is still long, up to 512 PAIRS. A cell's units here are the written
      units its movable ranks stand on, ascending. In a cell A, the first
      rank on a unit `x` that no other rank of the column holds, of group
      `a`, moves onto the ordinal the first rank on `y` stands on, `y`
      A's first unit of a group `b` other than `a` that is no hole; in
      another cell B, the first rank on `z` moves onto the ordinal the
      first rank on `w` stands on, `w` B's first unit of group `a` that is
      no hole, and `z` B's first unit of `b` that one rank of the column
      holds alone where the count is long by two or more and one is,
      else B's first unit of `b` that two ranks or more hold (no pair
      where neither is). Every group's count and every cell's size are
      kept, and the count falls by one, or by two where `z` was held
      alone. Of every pair, the one falling most, then whose two gaps'
      first days lie nearest, then the first in the order of A, `x`, `b`
      and B, cells in step 8.3's order.
   6. **The two-census exchange** (plan P4-D366; the 3b.3 skeptic's
      blocker 1 (b)), where the pass keeps a second census's group and,
      once step 7b is done, the movable ranks still do not hold the owed
      totals: up to 200 TRADES, while the totals do not hold. A rank of a
      group over its total moves, up to 62 units away inside its gap,
      onto an ordinal no hole of a group under its total, of its own
      width kind and keep but of any second group: from second group `a`
      to `b`. Where `a` and `b` differ, a second rank, of second group
      `b`, moves up to 31 units away inside its own gap onto an ordinal
      no hole of its own group, width kind and keep, and of second group
      `a`, so every second group keeps its count. A move SCORES nought
      where it keeps the count of different values -- a rank alone on its
      written unit onto one no rank holds, or one sharing its own onto
      one a rank holds -- and one where it does not. For each pair of
      second groups, the second move is, as the ranks stand when the
      trade's round begins, the one scoring least, then the nearest,
      then of the lowest rank, then onto the lower ordinal. Ranks are
      asked in rank order and each one's candidates in their order; of
      every trade, the one whose summed score and then summed distance in
      units is least, the first met on a tie, the asking ending with the
      first rank that offers a trade scoring nought. The step asks
      whether the count is reachable no more than step 7b does; where a
      trade was made and it is, steps 8.1 to 8.5 run again.
   7. **The count put back on a moment's own day** (landing 3b.D2, plan
      P4-D367), where the unit is the day and spans more than one
      written unit -- a day of moments -- and the count is still SHORT
      once step 6 is done. Steps 1 to 6 move a rank by whole units, so
      each keeps its clock, and where the census sends many moments onto
      few days their kept clocks meet: 2,400 visits on seven Wednesdays,
      minutes from 07:00 to 19:59, came out of the pass 1,882 different
      minutes for 1,933. The movable ranks in rank order: a rank sharing
      its written unit, on a day no hole and not at the start of its day,
      moves onto the first of the 64 places of its own day inside its gap
      nearest its own place -- a whole number of written units from it,
      the earlier on a tie, never the day's start -- whose written unit
      no rank holds, until the count is back. On its own day the rank
      keeps its group and kind, so every group's count holds, and no
      clock is put on midnight or taken off it.

   What the steps leave off is reported as the column's count of
   different values, and where the census holds, as the count that gave
   way to it: SHORT in the twin's own tails where every day the census
   allows between the boundaries, no hole, holds a date -- on a column
   counted in days alone, as a full day of moments still has instants
   free -- short elsewhere, or LONG -- each in the recount's own
   sentence's place only where the twin's recounted values went the same
   way, and the long one for the folded count beside it too; on a column
   of moments counted in different values, never days (the 3b.2-W
   skeptic, minor 1).
9. Each run of ranks the layout does not pin is sorted.

Where the census still does not hold, the report names `weekday_census`
as a published fact the twin missed, and the column's sentence on how
its dates are spread across the calendar says the published counts per
day of the week are NOT met. That sentence is read off this same
measurement, the count of the body against the published groups once
step 9 is done, and never off the census alone: a description the
loader accepts can publish a census its own tail boundaries leave no
twin able to meet, and the sentence said it was met beside the line
naming it missed (review of landing 3b.D1, item 1).

**The shared steps' frozen cases** (plan P4-D366) are states of ranks,
not columns: at the default floor of 11 the pass with steps 7b and 8.4
to 8.6 writes on every date battery the twin it wrote before them, so no
column of whole dates reaches them there through the whole generator;
at a floor of 36 eight twins of 15,152 move, steps 8.4 and 8.5 merging a
count already left long one or two values nearer the published one. The
fifteenth vectors file, `tests/reference/generation-branch-vectors-15.json`,
holds fifty-three such states -- the landing's ten (an hour inside its
day, a day of moments, the index of steps 5 and 6, a chain, step 8.4 at
its own clock and at another, a long pair, a two-census trade, and the
cycles of seven and of ten groups), its review's twenty-four (each new
step once through the whole pass, and a state for every clause a
reviewer's mutant changed), its second review's six (a state for
every line of that review's repair whose mutant changed an answer), its
Codex review's seven (step 8.3's take in written units on its own state
of forty ranks each at 00:15, 01:15 and 02:30 and on a day of moments,
a place past the gap twice, a link past its gap, and each step's mover;
and two cycles restated, where a move puts its rank in the next group's
mover's place), the two that review's verification found one short
there too, of hours and of moments, two chains of step 7b whose
mover as the ranks then stand has no place, of hours and, through the
whole pass, of moments, and step 3's last pass on four alike weeks whose
every move ties across the gaps, one tying two giving groups and one two
taking groups (the lane T2 skeptic's second report, finding 4) -- with
the answer this section gives each, and no G14.3 case.

#### G7.3g The hour census: the clock pass

*Stage 3b, landing 3b.2-H, plan P4-D371.* ONE PASS FOR EVERY FIELD OF
THE WRITTEN CLOCK (the 3b.4 skeptic's M4). A census of a FIELD counts a
column's body by bins of `unit` seconds, `period` of them in one turn:
the hour of the day, 3,600 and 24, and, when landing 3b.4 publishes
theirs, the minute of the hour, 60 and 60, and the second of the minute,
1 and 60. An instant's BIN is `(o div unit) mod period` and its GROUP
the census group holding that bin; its PARENT is the turn it stands in,
`o div (unit × period)` -- a day for the hour, an hour for the minute --
and its SEAT that parent's place in its day, from nought, always nought
for the hour. Where the parent is shorter than a day, each seat has a
KIN group, its group in the coarser census every move keeps (for the
minute, its hour's group in the hour census); the hour has none. The
hour census is the only field published so far. Each field's landing
names its unit, its period, its kin and where its pass runs; the steps
below are every field's, read for the hour where they name it.

Where a column of moments publishes a non-empty `hour_census` (contract
HC1 to HC6) -- or stands on the dial's half day (G7.3b step 10), whose
census is then hours 0 to 11 holding the body and 12 to 23 none,
published or not -- with both tails, at least three parsed cells,
counted in seconds and with no bare date, its ranks are moved once
G7.3f's day pass is done and before any cell is spelled, until the cells
between the two boundary ranks fall on the published groups. No word is
drawn. A moment's HOUR, its bin, is the hour of its written wall clock,
`(o div 3,600) mod 24` -- but for a rank the twin writes at a SIXTIETH
SECOND: a body rank pinned at a published boundary or rung whose seconds
field is 60, or standing between two such pins of one moment, which G7.5
writes from that moment's own fields, `HH:MM:60`, while G7.1 stands its
ordinal at the next minute's first second. Its bin is that of `o - 1`,
the second before, the hour (and the minute) it is written in. No other
rank is written at a sixtieth second: the other cells a source wrote
there are met in the twin by ranks at ordinary seconds of the same
hour. Every step below counts a rank by its ordinal, so before
step 2 each such rank whose two bins lie in different groups asks its
ordinal's group one rank more and its written group one fewer, and the
pass, meeting those counts by ordinal, meets the census as written (the
landing's review, item 1: eleven 23:59:60 a date over 100 dates counted
all 1,078 body cells, and wrote them, in hour 0). A rank is written AT MIDNIGHT where its cell,
cut to the column's precision, reads 00:00:00. Its DAY STANDING is its
weekday's group in the column's `weekday_census` where one stands, and
its weekday itself where none does. No step below moves a rank to a day
of another standing, but for two LAST RESORTS where no weekday census
stands (steps 3 and 6), each taken only once every move keeping the
standing has been made: nothing published then counts a weekday. Where
one stands, the one such move is step 3's ESCAPE PAID BACK, which moves
as many ranks of the other standing onto days of the unit's own, so
every weekday count is kept.

1. **Pinned.** No rank the layout pins moves (G7.3), nor one whose gap is
   a single place, nor -- where `n_at_midnight` is published -- one
   written at midnight. The count of different values the pass keeps is
   the count of written units the ranks stand on as it begins.
2. **The shared steps.** G7.3f's steps 1 to 9 at the field's unit with
   the parent kept -- for the hour: bins the hours, groups the census's,
   the unit 3,600 seconds, the written unit a minute or a second at the
   column's precision, the day 86,400 seconds, a period of 24 bins, and
   every move keeping the rank's day (THE SEAMS of G7.3f), so a move
   shifts a rank by whole hours on its own day and keeps its minute and
   second.
3. **SAMEPARENT, the ESCAPE, SPLIT and RELIEF** (the design skeptic's B1 and B2),
   where a group is still over its count, up to four rounds, a round
   that moves nothing ending the step. A unit leaves whole while its
   group is over, so one of `k` ranks leaving a group over by fewer than
   `k` leaves that group under its count, and a unit asked earlier that
   had no place at its turn may find one there in a later round (the
   lane's second skeptic, finding 2: a census one round left two cells
   off, four meet). In group
   order, each group over
   its count asks its movable units in PROPORTIONAL ORDER (the 3b.4
   skeptic's B1): of its `n` units, those the smooth rotation chooses --
   each adds the number the group is over by to a credit and is chosen
   where the credit reaches `n`, which is then taken back -- first, the
   rest after, in rank order. A UNIT is every movable body rank of one
   written unit where no other rank of the column stands on it and all
   share one gap, and otherwise each movable rank alone. Asked while its
   group is still over, a unit of `k` ranks takes:
   - SAMEPARENT (SAMEDAY, for the hour): on its own parent, in each bin
     of a group with room for `k` more ranks, the FREE place nearest its
     own place in its bin -- for the hour, its minute and second --
     inside its gap -- a place free where it is no hole, no rank holds
     its written unit and it is not written at midnight, found a
     written unit at a time outward, the earlier on a tie -- and of
     those, the one whose place in its parent -- for the hour, its
     clock -- is nearest the unit's own, the earlier on a tie;
   - else the ESCAPE: where the parent is shorter than a day, the
     nearest other parent of its own day whose seat has its own seat's
     kin group, the earlier on a tie, and there SAMEPARENT's place (for
     the hour, none); then the nearest other day of its gap, the earlier
     on a tie, that is no hole, of its day standing and of its width
     kind, and there SAMEPARENT's place in the parent at its own seat;
   - else SPLIT: where `k` is more than one, each rank of it alone, in
     rank order, as above, while its group is over.

   Then RELIEF, where a group is still over its count: in group order,
   each such group asks its units again, in proportional order, whole
   and then rank by rank, and a unit takes, in the first group with a
   count of its own and no room for it, SAMEPARENT's place there on its
   own parent inside its gap -- asked of that group alone -- once a
   RELIEF unit has left that group: the first, in rank order, of that
   group's units as they stood when RELIEF first asked that group, of as
   many ranks, that has SAMEPARENT's place on its own parent in a group
   with room. Where the unit then has none, the relief unit goes back
   and the next is asked; one that finds no place is not asked again in
   this step, though a whole unit leaving a group over by fewer than its
   ranks gives that group room, as in the rounds above.

   Last, where no weekday census stands and a group is still over its
   count, the rounds above once more, the ESCAPE free at last to take,
   where no day of the unit's standing has a place, the nearest day of
   another weekday on the same terms (the LAST RESORT; plan P4-D371's
   measured baseline: a cell on a rung's day may move to the nearest
   other day inside its gap where same-day moves cannot meet the
   census).

   And where a weekday census stands and a group is still over its
   count, the rounds above once more with THE ESCAPE PAID BACK (lane J,
   plan P4-D367), asked of a unit SAMEPARENT and the ESCAPE leave with
   no place: the other days of its gap, nearest first, the earlier on a
   tie, no hole and of its width kind, whose day standing is another,
   and on each SAMEPARENT's place at its own seat, taken only where as
   many PAYERS as the unit has ranks are found and moved. A payer is a
   movable body rank, not of the unit, still on the day of that other
   standing it stood on as the round began, whose PLACE is its own
   clock on the nearest day of its gap of the unit's standing, no hole
   and of its width kind, the earlier on a tie. The days of that
   standing are asked nearest the unit's own day first, the earlier on
   a tie, each day's ranks in rank order; of the ranks with a place,
   the first whose move keeps the count of different values -- alone on
   its written unit onto one no rank holds, or sharing its own onto one
   a rank holds -- among the first and the 1,024 asked after it is
   taken, else the first, and each moves before the next is asked.
   Where fewer are found than the unit has ranks, every payer goes back.
   A standing is asked once for a unit, and a pair of standings for
   which no payer at all was found is not asked again in the step.
   The walk reads only the days holding movable ranks as the round
   began, once for a unit, each payer starting past the days whose
   ranks are spent (Codex's review of lane J, item 3: a unit of 32,000
   ranks took 6.3 CPU seconds for its payers, and a walk restarted for
   each payer read every empty day between, both now linear). The
   unit leaving its standing while as many payers enter it keeps every
   weekday count, and a payer moving whole days keeps every field of its
   clock, so both censuses hold (batch 2b's integration: five noon
   stamps a day for 118 days, a weekday census of seven single days
   beside hour 12 alone, wrote five cells at 05:23:40 on the high
   boundary's day, before its noon, its gap holding no other day of
   their weekday -- 4 twins of 10 short of the hour census).

   A UNIT IS ASKED AS IT STANDS (Codex's review of lane J, item 1). A
   payer moves a rank by whole days, perhaps a rank of a unit its group
   listed and has not yet asked. So at its turn a unit is its ranks
   still on the written unit it was listed on, whole only where they are
   every rank standing there, else each alone, and it is not asked where
   none is; a rank a payer moved off is asked in a later round, where
   its group is listed again. Asked as listed, a Sunday pair at 05:10,
   one of which paid a Monday 05:23 onto a Sunday, moved whole onto the
   Monday at 12:10, and Monday's 2 and Sunday's 5 came back 3 and 4,
   every hour met and the count kept.

   THE ROUND GIVEN BACK (lane J's skeptic, finding 1). Where that
   round placed a unit and, once steps 4 to 6 have run, the count of
   different values stands off the count step 6 asks -- by any distance
   where the count is one the construction reaches, else by its
   shortness alone, and that only where the count drawn is not above
   the published one -- steps 4 to 6 run again on the state the round
   began from, and that state stands where it comes nearer the count;
   on a tie the round stands. A SPLIT rank the round puts on a day of
   another standing whose own values stand in another group of the
   field writes a value no merge of step 6, which keeps the day
   standing and the group, takes back: ward rounds at 08:00 on weekdays
   and 10:30 at weekends, a million rows over 150 days, came back with
   260 different values of a published 150 and the hour census missed
   all the same.
4. **Off midnight.** A movable rank the steps above left written at
   midnight that was not there when the pass began, with every such rank
   of its written unit, takes the free place of the day's first bin --
   hour 0, for the hour -- nearest midnight inside all their gaps; where
   there is none, they stay. A published count at midnight stays exact,
   and a withheld one only falls (plan P4-D191). Where the hour pass runs
   on a column whose body is drawn on a lattice of the clock coarser than
   its written unit (G7.3's drawing rule), the free place of that lattice
   nearest midnight is asked first, and a written unit at a time only
   where the bin of their gaps holds none (lane J2's Codex review, the
   leftover: stamps every fifteen minutes, half the slots kept, each
   written three or four times, had a pair put at `00:00:01`, which no
   field pass could put on second 0 but at midnight).
5. **The half day's tails** (the hour's alone). On the dial's half day,
   each tail rank past noon or written at midnight takes the nearer of
   the half day's places on either side of it inside its stratum, the
   earlier on a tie: G7.3b step 10 draws it there, and a pass after it
   may have moved it a unit.
6. **PUT BACK** (the design skeptic's B1), where the count of different
   written units is not the one the pass began with and the column's
   count is one the construction reaches
   (`contract.datetime_counts_reachable`), last of the moves, so it
   repays every move before it. Where the count is LONG: the runs --
   every movable body rank of a written unit no other rank holds, in one
   gap -- the fewest ranks first, in proportional order within one size,
   each move a run whole onto the nearest written unit another rank
   holds of its own group inside its gap, at no written midnight: on its
   own parent first, else on the parents the ESCAPE asks, in its order
   -- the other parents of its own day in its seat's kin group, then its
   seat on the nearest other day of its gap, of its day standing and
   width kind, no hole, the earlier first. Where no weekday census
   stands and the count is still long once every such merge is made, the
   same once more, a run free at last to merge onto the nearest day of
   another weekday on the same terms (the LAST RESORT). Where it is
   SHORT: in rank order, a movable body rank sharing its written unit
   takes the free place of its own bin, parent and gap nearest it (for
   the hour, its own hour and day). Where the column's count is not one
   the construction reaches, a long count is left, and a SHORT count is
   put back, as above, only where the count of written units the pass
   began with is not above the column's published `n_distinct`: the
   first movable ranks in rank order that share a written unit are split
   off it, whichever move made the tie (the lane's skeptic, finding 4:
   2,000 different moments written with two marks between day and clock
   came back 1,999 at one seed in three, their count from HELD to its
   envelope). Where that count is above the published one, a short count
   is left too: on a dense column the ties the moves make bring the twin
   nearer the published count, as the real column's own ties do (the
   lane's second skeptic, finding 1: 20,000 lab draws to the minute over
   twelve days, written with two marks, came back 18 to 19 per cent long
   when the count drawn was put back, and within 1.2 per cent of the
   published count when it was not). Each move keeps every group's
   count; the step stops once the count is back.
7. Each run of ranks the layout does not pin is sorted.

Where the census still does not hold, the report names `hour_census` as
a published fact the twin missed, and the column's sentence on how its
dates are spread across the calendar says the published counts per hour
are NOT met; where it holds, the sentence no longer names the time of
day among what the twin does not reproduce, and where a group counts
several hours it says the twin's split among them is its own.

**Measured** (the lane's battery, plan P4-D371): the shared steps alone
met the census on every column but the clinics, whose rank on a rung's
day before the rung, hours 0 to 7 counted empty, had no whole hour on
its day inside its gap; SAMEDAY placed it. The 10-week clinic at
10,000 rows left two tied units no group had room for (step 3's SPLIT),
and a lab panel of 2,000 results on 1 to 25 rows an instant came back
62 values long until step 6 merged the split runs back; the shared steps'
own count steps (G7.3f step 8) look only at a unit's place inside an
hour, which on a column of seconds almost never holds another rank.
OR starts -- ten rooms at 07:30 on 100 weekdays, cases from 09:00 --
left the ranks before the 07:30 rung on the last day of their gap in the
empty hours 0 to 6 at every seed, hour 7 full and no day of their
standing in the gap; RELIEF meets the census at 10 of 10 seeds. Where
no weekday census stands, the strict escape and PUT BACK left three older
columns unmet -- 400 noon moments at a floor of one, a rank on a rung's
day with no other day of its weekday in its gap; 400 moments on 60
values written at 78; visits a minute either side of midnight at 21 and
22 values for 20 -- and the last resorts meet them; on the lane's
battery neither fires, every twin's statistics as before. Made one pass
for every field, it gave the hour pass's answer on 3,000 random states
of hours and every twin of the lane's battery its statistics, and the
product and the oracle answer alike on 1,500 random states of hours and
1,500 of a field of minutes whose parent is the hour.

**Cost** (the lane's skeptic, finding 1). At a unit of an hour the
shared steps' CHAIN and exchange (G7.3f steps 7b and 8.3) filed every
movable rank by cell again each round, up to 256 and 64 rounds, and step
3's shares made their totals exact asking every pair of groups over
every gap: a million moments of daytime visits spent 397 seconds in this
pass, and fifteen in a hundred moments at midnight over two years -- a
gap between every day's cells at midnight, which step 1 pins -- spent 5.7
seconds of 10,000 rows' pass in the shares. Filed once a call and kept
as each move changes them, and the shares asked gap by gap, every answer
of those steps is the same: in one window the million moments take 18
seconds of a 130-second generate, where the column with no hour census
takes 126, their twin byte for byte the one before, and those 10,000
rows' shares 0.47.

**A stated limit** (the lane's skeptic, finding 5). A 12-hour stamp
whose census is withheld -- three days of stamps, HC4 -- holds its body
on the half day by the half day's own census, each afternoon draw taking
the nearest morning place of its own day inside its gap; the gaps of a
column of a few days are hours wide, so the place twelve hours earlier
is rarely inside one, and the dial's hours 10 and 11 come back heavier
than the real (a dial-hour TVD of 0.145 to 0.185, against 0.056 to 0.085
with the pass withdrawn, whose twin, written on the dial, reads its
afternoon cells back twelve hours early and misses published facts).

**Its frozen cases** are states of ranks, as G7.3f's are: the sixteenth
vectors file, `tests/reference/generation-branch-vectors-16.json`, holds
thirty-three -- SAMEDAY, the escape with a weekday census's groups and its last
resort, the escape paid back, its payer keeping the count asked past the
first, its payers given back where too few are found, a payer kept off a
hole, the whole pass beside a weekday census, and the whole pass with the
round given back where it costs the count, given back where the count is
nearer without it though still missed, and kept where the count is no
nearer without it (lane J), a unit a payer took a rank of asked as it
stands (lane J's Codex review), SPLIT, RELIEF and its give-back where the room it made is not
enough, PUT BACK long and short and its last resort, PUT BACK never onto
a written midnight and its short count moving only a rank that shares
its written unit, the proportional order, the step off midnight and the
step off midnight on the body's lattice (lane J2's Codex review), the half
day's tail ranks and a tail rank kept inside its stratum, SAMEPARENT
asking no place of a hole, step 3's later round, where a whole unit's
leaving gave a group room, and the whole pass, and, on a field of minutes
whose parent is the hour, the escape's and PUT BACK's tier in their kin
group and the escape kept to it -- and three of G7.3b step 10's
distances, on a low tail of minutes, a high tail of seconds and a tail
whose ranks must all differ, each with the answer this section gives it
and no G14.3 case.

**Steps 7c's and 8.7's frozen cases** (plan P4-D367) are states of ranks
too, on a day of moments written to the minute, in the seventeenth
vectors file, `tests/reference/generation-branch-vectors-17.json`: three
Wednesday sessions through the whole pass, and step 7c alone keeping the
count of different values, keeping the midnight, taking the nearer end
day, keeping off a hole and keeping to an end day of the moment's own
width kind -- an unpadded month-first column whose one width word is
`second-field-unpadded`, its nearer end day in September, of the other
kind -- and its shift through a group at its total;
and step 8.7 through the whole pass on crowded
Wednesdays, and alone taking the nearest free minute of a rank's own
day, the earlier on a tie, inside its gap and off midnight -- each with
the answer this section gives it, and no G14.3 case.

#### G7.3i The day of the month: the joint day plan

(Landing 3b.3, plan P4-D368.) A column counted in days -- whole dates,
and moments every value of which stands at midnight on the local clock
(G7.1's ordinal space `date`) -- that publishes a `day_of_month_census`
is moved in the day pass's own slot by two passes of G7.3f's shared
steps, in place of the weekday pass alone; every other column, a column
of moments with a clock among them, is moved by G7.3f exactly as before,
so its twin is unchanged byte for byte. Each day falls in one of the
census's thirty-four BINS: the day of its month from 1 to 27; the 28th,
29th and 30th where that day is not its month's last; and the month's
last day in bins 31, 32, 33 and 34 by its month's length of 28 to 31
days. The bins follow one another with no period, so G7.3f counts a
gap's days one by one -- and a gap wider than 1,024 days by the
calendar, in 400-year cycles and whole months, the same counts without
asking each day (the Codex review of landing 3b.3, item 3); a day's bin
is kept once asked, at most 65,536 days; past them a day is reckoned
each time it is asked, never kept.

1. **Pass A** is G7.3f over the day-of-month census: each day's group
   is its bin's, and every day between the two tail boundaries whose
   weekday the weekday census counts nought is added to the holes, so
   no rank is put where pass B would have to take it off -- read as a
   rule on the day's weekday, never stored day by day (the Codex review,
   item 2: a business-day column over years 0001 to 2000 stored 202,436
   such days). Every other
   seam is the weekday pass's: the width kind of the column's one width
   word, the description's holes and the count of different days the
   ranks held before the pass, kept where it is reachable.
2. **Pass B**, where a weekday census is published, is G7.3f over it,
   each move keeping the rank's day-of-month group as G7.3f keeps a
   second census's group, so the day-of-month counts pass A met stand;
   step 8.6 trades two ranks across those groups where the weekday
   totals are still off, each second group keeping its count.
3. **The core holds.** Where the two passes leave the weekday census
   missed over the body, or the count of different days off where it
   is kept, G7.3f alone is run from the same ranks; where its days miss
   neither of the two the passes met and meet one they missed, the
   column takes them -- its twin before this landing, byte for byte --
   and the twin names `day_of_month_census` given way to the weekday
   census and the count.

4. **The spelling repair keeps the groups** (the Codex review, item
   1). A cell G7.5 writes in a spelling the run declares absent moves
   after the census is met. On a column publishing a day-of-month census
   the repair first asks, inside each window it asks (the rank's gap,
   then the body), the days at most 400 away, nearest first and the
   earlier first at one distance, that are no hole, keep the rank's
   day-of-month group and, where one is published, its weekday group,
   keep its width kind where the column keeps one, and write no absent
   spelling: a rank alone on its day takes the first no rank holds, one
   sharing its day the first a rank holds, else the first found. Only
   where none is found does it move as G7.5 always did.
5. **The census as written.** The finished cells are recounted as V5-W2
   counts them; where they miss the census and nothing above names it,
   the twin names `day_of_month_census`, and the sentence on its spread
   says missed, never met.

Where a census still does not hold, the twin names it
(`day_of_month_census`, or `weekday_census`); where both hold and the
count of different days does not, the weekday pass's own cause is named,
the tails' only where every day both censuses allow between the two
boundaries holds a rank. The pass draws no word. Its frozen cases are
states of ranks in the eighteenth vectors file,
`tests/reference/generation-branch-vectors-18.json`: billing on the 1st
and the 15th with no weekday census, a visit on the 10th beside seven
weekday groups, month ends on each month's own last day, billing rolled
to business days beside an empty weekend, births with a weekend dip, and
the 1st heaped beside a hole on each 15th, and one state of step 4's
repair -- each with the answer this section gives it, and no G14.3 case.

#### G7.3h The minute and second censuses: the clock pass on two fields, and the drawing rule

*Stage 3b, landing 3b.4, plan P4-D372.* A column of moments may publish,
beside its hour census, each FIELD's HEAPS -- values standing out, each
with its count -- and its CENSUS of the cells on no heap: `minute_heaps`
and `minute_census` over the minutes of the hour, and, written to the
second -- not finer, as the twin writes no figure below the second (SE3)
-- `second_heaps` and `second_census` over the seconds of the minute
(contract 6.6.2, MC1 to MC6, MH1, MH2, SE1 to SE6, SH1, SH2).
For the same reason a column written finer than the second publishes its
minute's facts only where its body, cut to the second, keeps its count
of different values: the real column so cut is then a twin meeting both.
A cell counts at the minute and second it is WRITTEN at,
`canonical[14:16]` and `canonical[17:19]`; a sixtieth second, `HH:MM:60`,
counts in its own minute at second 59.

**THE DRAWING RULE (G7.3's body draw, the design skeptic's M2, m2 and
m3).** Where a minute or second census or heap is published, the body is
drawn on a LATTICE of the clock its facts pin: the seconds are pinned on
a column written to the minute, or where the second publishes heaps and
no census and the body's cells off them are fewer than the census line --
a rest the merge rule could only have withheld, not a census withheld for
its few values (the lane's skeptic, item 2: bursts of check-ins a third
off their heaps at 0 and 30, drawn on half hours, came back with that third
on :01 and :29) -- the lattice the greatest step dividing sixty and every
heap's value; or a census and no heap whose one non-zero group holds second 0,
every published body value on second 0; a lattice finer than the minute
is the DRAWING UNIT. With the seconds on 0, the minute's own lattice,
found the same way, widens it to sixty seconds times its step -- the
hour for a column on the hour, half an hour for a half-hour grid --
sixty where the minute pins nothing (one on a column written to the
minute). Every unpinned body draw is floored to the unit, or set on the
next multiple where its floor leaves the rank's gap, and left where no
multiple lies inside it. Each TAIL draws on the same unit where both
boundaries and every value a tail lists stand on it, each draw inside its
stratum, and on the written unit elsewhere; a tail's outermost rank,
standing where its published distances put it, is not moved. Both steps at midnight step a
body rank off a midnight by the drawing unit and a tail rank by its
tail's (with G7.3h withheld, 10,000 cells written `HH:MM:00` stood seven
body cells off second 0 when stepped by the written second). The count
pass and the hour pass (G7.3g) step by the written unit, as before this
landing: stepped by the drawing unit, no twin of the lane's batteries met
or missed anything else, nor stood a body cell off the lattice (the
lane's skeptic, item 5). Where no minute or second fact is published the
unit is one and every draw is the one before this landing.

**THE PASS.** After G7.3g, under its run conditions -- the one scope of
the clock's censuses (`calendar_rules.census_scope`), asked of the facts
the pass is handed, the shared clock's frame's where G7.3k puts the
column on its ranks' own clocks, and every bare date pinned as G7.3k's
step 3 pins it (batch 3b's merge of lane J2) -- G7.3g's clock pass
runs once for the minute and then once for the second. The minute's bins
are 60 seconds, 60 a turn, its parent the hour, and its kin each hour's
group in the hour census -- one group over the day where none is
published. The second's bins are one second, its parent the minute, and
its kin each minute of the day's pair of hour group and minute group,
the minute's groups those of its own pass, one group where it publishes
none -- each pair its own kin group, however many groups the minute has.
KIN SHARES: where G7.3f's moves fill a gap's shares (steps 5 and 6) and
the gap's ranks stand in two kin groups or more, by their parents' places
in the day, each kin group, in the order its first rank stands in the
gap, takes its own shares of the gap's, and its ranks move to them as a
gap's do, whole runs and then single ranks, but no rank leaves a written
unit it shares by a move changing the count (a kin group's few ranks
split bursts of check-ins to meet its own shares: 1,000 of them at a
floor of 36 came back 108 values long); single ranks over the whole gap
follow. A kin group's IDEAL share of each group G is its R of the gap's S
ranks times G over S, in 2**20ths of a rank, plus what it CARRIES from the
gaps before -- the ideal it was owed there less what its ranks there HOLD
once the gap's moves are done, its own and the gap's single moves after
them, not less the share it was given -- so the rounding is made over the
whole body (CONTROLLED ROUNDING, the lane's skeptic, item 4: rounded gap by
gap, hour 8 of 10,000 admissions took minute 6's remainder in most of 38
gaps and came back with 36 cells there against 11; and the Codex review,
item 3: four daily gaps of 120 stamps, the second's hour 8 standing on no
minute 0, carried as given came back with 94 of hour 8's and 146 of hour
9's on minute 0 where 120 each could stand). The kin groups so far take together, of each group, their
ideals summed, rounded down, never less than they took, never more than
the gap's G nor than this kin group's ranks beyond what was taken; the
ranks still unplaced go one each, as often as it takes, to the groups of
the largest remainder, the lower group on a tie; ranks placed beyond
come back from the groups raised above what was taken, the smallest
remainder first, the lower group on a tie; a kin group takes the
difference. WHERE THE COUNT AT MIDNIGHT IS PUBLISHED and value 0 is a
group alone, a rank whose place on value 0 of its own parent is written
at midnight -- on a column written to the minute, every rank of hour 0 --
is not FREE to take it, as the real column's own cells there are those at
midnight: that group's ideal is its want spread over the kin groups by
their free ranks, where these number at least its want, each kin group's
other ranks over the other groups as they want, and no kin group takes
more of it than its free ranks (the lane's skeptic, item 1: 200,000 cells
written `HH:MM:00`, hour 0 given its share in proportion, had 327 ranks
moved onto a midnight, 217 of which stayed, and came back 602 at midnight
against 385). And on such a pass A WRITTEN MIDNIGHT IS A KIND OF ITS OWN
(G7.3f's kind, its keep read as a kind apart): its ranks are pinned and
every step of G7.3f keeps the kind, so none moves a rank onto it (the
lane's repair: 1,000 check-ins in bursts, drawn on the second, had four
ranks of hour 0 moved onto 00:00 by the gap's single moves after KIN
SHARES; the exchange took two back, and the twin came back 13 at midnight
against 12). KIN SHARES' REACH (the verifier's item 10 on the Codex round):
a kin group's rank REACHES a group where it stands in it or a place of it
on its own place in the unit, inside its gap and its parent, on no hole,
is of its kind (a written midnight read as of its parent's); its ranks
ABLE to take a group are those reaching it, and of value 0 alone those
free to take it too. Where some kin group reaches none of a group the gap
wants, every wanted group whose kin groups are not all able to take it
with every rank is shared as value 0 alone is -- its want over the kin
groups by their able ranks, each kin group's other ranks over the other
groups as they want -- and the carry of a kin group reaching none of
some wanted group is offered, group by group, to the other kin groups by
their ranks able to take the group, rounded down, its own carry kept and
taken where it reaches again. A kin group takes no more of a group than
its able ranks, and none of what the kin groups after it CLAIM: of each
group, the whole ranks of their parts that those carrying a whole rank
or more of it are able to take (four gaps
of three hours, hour 8 off minute 0 in each: its carry, asked of hour 8
itself, grew gap by gap and handed it every share of minute 0, which the
gap's single moves gave hour 9 -- 200 against hour 10's 40 where 120
each could stand; hour 8 reaching minute 0 with 4 of its 34 ranks a gap
passed its growing carry to hour 9 alone, 57 against hour 10's 27, where
the claims leave 51 and 33; and taken first by the earlier kin groups'
largest remainders, the want of minute 0 left hour 23 of cells written
`HH:MM:00` at 10,000 rows none of its carried share in twelve gaps
running, 6 of its 45 cells on minute 0 against 16). After each field's pass THE TAILS MAKE ROOM AT MIDNIGHT: with
value 0 a group alone holding fewer body ranks than its count, each body
rank in order -- not pinned, of a group over its count -- whose place on
value 0 of its own parent (its place in the bin kept) is a written
midnight inside its gap and no hole, takes it, while the first tail rank
not yet stepped, not pinned by its tail, at a written midnight, that can
step off it inside its stratum does so -- the search starting past the
tails taken (the Codex review, item 6: started at the first, t ranks made
t(t+1)/2 checks, 50,005,000 at a million rows) -- as the tails keep their count
below -- where the count of different values is reachable, only a tail
whose step and the rank's move together do not raise that count, the
first keeping it where any does, and SPREAD then puts back a value lost.
The count at midnight is kept (a column on the hour at 1,000 and 10,000
rows: the hour pass stepped a rank of hour 0 to 00:01 while a tail held a
midnight, and the heap at minute 0 came back one short).
Filled nearest first and whole runs first over the whole gap, 10,000
clinic slots came back with 20 per cent of hour 8 on :00 and 47 per cent
of hour 10, against 35 in every hour of the real column; kin group by kin
group, every hour stands within its sampling scale.
The pass asks no count step of G7.3f (8.1 to 8.6): over sixty
values they ask cycles among as many groups, and the count is put back
by G7.3g's PUT BACK and the steps below. A field's GROUPS are its
census's, in order, each over its values,
or, beside heaps with no census, one group of every value counting the
body less the heaps; then each heap, its value alone, at its count. A
field whose ranks already meet its groups is not passed. Where the
column's count is reachable, A SHARED WRITTEN UNIT MOVES WHOLE in G7.3f's
single moves (steps 6 and 7, and KIN SHARES' own): a rank whose move
would take it off a written unit it shares onto a free one moves only
with every rank of that unit, onto the same place -- as a move keeping
the count where every rank of it is among the ranks moved and finds the
place inside its gap, its group can give them all and the place's group
take them all; in the leftover, where none fits, once per unit past that
room, its group over and the place's under, whole units and single
ranks then putting both back; else not at all (the lane's second
skeptic, item 1: check-ins in bursts at 200 to 500 rows and a floor of
36, their minute census holding empty groups, came back 157 values long
over 45 twins, the gap's single moves splitting bursts, and 105 long
over 90 twins at floors 11 and 36 with the rule, none at 11). Each unit
is judged once for each place, group and question while nothing moves
(the Codex review, item 5: each of a unit's 400 ranks judged it over all
400, and a 10,000-row burst in a million rows asked some 100 million). After the
clock pass, for the field:

1. *The exchange off midnight.* The ranks the pass left on a written
   midnight that stood off one before it, unit by unit in rank order,
   take together the place of their own group on another parent of their
   day in their kin group, the nearest first, the earlier on a tie;
   where none has one, the free place of another group G of the field on
   their own parent nearest their own, inside the gap they share and at
