   no written midnight, while runs of G holding as many ranks -- each run
   every movable rank of one written unit, no other rank on it, one gap;
   the longest first, each length's in rank order, at most 64 asked --
   each take the free place of the ranks' old group on its own parent
   inside its gap; where they fall short, every run goes back and the
   next place is asked.
2. *PUT BACK once more*, where the exchange left the count of different
   written units long and the column's count is reachable: G7.3g's PUT
   BACK, its merges keeping the day standing first and, where no weekday
   census stands, its last resort. A pass that moved one rank of a tied
   pair onto a held midnight kept the count; the exchange that took it
   off wrote one value more (a column on the hour beside three cells off
   it, at 10,000 rows and a floor of 36).
3. *SUBSTITUTE*, where the count of different written units is still
   long and the column's count is reachable: each run in rank order joins
   a unit another rank holds in another group G of the field, inside its
   gap and at no written midnight, on its own parent, else on another
   parent of its day in its kin group, else at its own parent's place on
   another day of its day standing and width kind, nearest first, and
   where no weekday census stands on a day of another weekday, else, on
   those days in the same order, at the other places of its kin group,
   nearest its own first, 400 parents asked at most; and runs of G
   holding as many ranks take free places of its old group, as in step 1.
   Each pair puts back one unit. A group, a parent's place in the day and
   a gap whose search found no unit to join are not asked again in the
   round; SUBSTITUTE runs again while a round puts a value back, three
   rounds at most (the lane's skeptic, item 3: 300 check-ins in bursts
   came back 5 or 6 values long after one round and met their count
   after two; 200 of them, about one burst a day, a value long without
   the kin on other days).
4. *SPREAD*, where the count is still short and reachable, or the count
   drawn is not above the published one: each rank sharing its written
   unit, in rank order, takes the free place of its own group nearest its
   own on its parent, else the escape's (G7.3g step 3) in its own group;
   a group, a parent's place in the day and a gap that found none are
   not asked again.
5. Each run of unpinned ranks is sorted.

THE COUNT STEPS PAID BACK BESIDE A WEEKDAY CENSUS (lane J2, plan
P4-D391). Where a weekday census stands, the steps above move a rank
only to a day of its own standing, and a gap of about a week holds none:
merged beside lane D2's weekday census on moments, a ten-week clinic of
10,000 weekday visits heaped at minutes 0, 15, 30 and 45 came back 1,563 to 1,609
values of a published 2,175 at a floor of 11, and 1,000 check-ins in
bursts 288 to 295 for 285. So two steps are paid back, as G7.3g step
3's escape is, and a third swaps on the rank's own parent. The two paid
steps ask STRICT PAYERS: G7.3g step
3's payers -- ranks of the other standing moving by whole days onto the
nearest day of the unit's own, every field of their clocks kept -- but
only one whose move keeps the count of different values, among the first
with a place and the 1,024 asked after it, none standing on the written
unit a run joins and, for PUT BACK PAID BACK, none whose place stands on
the written unit the run leaves (its skeptic's item 2: the run still holds
it while its payers are asked, so a sharing rank there read as keeping the
count, and once the run had gone the unit stayed held -- a merge counted
that removed no value), and every payer given back where fewer are found
than the unit has ranks; so every weekday count is kept and each step
counts its own moves exactly. Where no unit is joined or left, none is
named -- never a unit number standing for none, which a written unit
before 1970, negative, would be (its Codex review, item 1).
- *PUT BACK PAID BACK*, after step 2, where the count is still long and
  reachable: PUT BACK's runs, the fewest ranks first and in proportional
  order within a size, each ASKED AS IT STANDS (its ranks still on the
  written unit it was listed on, whole only where they are every rank
  there; lane J's Codex review, item 1), each merged onto the nearest
  unit another rank holds of its own group at its own parent's place on
  the other days of its gap, nearest first, the earlier on a tie, no hole
  and of its width kind, whose standing is another -- taken only where as
  many strict payers as the run has ranks are found and moved.
- *SPREAD PAID BACK*, after step 4, where the count is still short and
  step 4's condition holds: each rank sharing its written unit, in rank
  order, takes step 4's place -- its own group's free place nearest its
  own on its parent, else the escape's in that group -- and else its own
  group's free place at its own parent's place on those days, paid back
  alike. Step 4's place is asked again, as step 4 passes over a group, a
  parent's place and a gap that found none on a day of another standing,
  whose own days it never asked.
- *SPREAD BY SUBSTITUTE*, after it, where the count is still short: each
  rank sharing its written unit, in rank order, takes the free place of
  ANOTHER group G of the field on its own parent nearest its own, inside
  its gap and at no written midnight, while a run of G holding one rank,
  in rank order, takes the free place of the rank's own group on its own
  parent nearest its own inside its gap; where no run of G has one, the
  next place is asked. Every group's count, parent and day is kept. Each
  pair of groups keeps a cursor past the runs it has asked, so no run is
  asked twice for one pair. (The ten-week clinic of 10,000 weekday visits,
  minutes' heaps at 0, 15, 30 and 45, came back 2,100 to 2,161 values of
  2,175 at a floor of 11 without it: every free place of its groups at
  their hours stood on the weekend, which its census counts nought.)
In each a standing is asked once for a unit, a pair of standings no payer
at all was found for is not asked again in the step, and a group, a
parent's place in the day, a gap and a day standing (for SPREAD BY
SUBSTITUTE, a parent) that found nothing are not asked again, so each
step's work grows with the rows. NO DAY IS READ TWICE IN VAIN (its Codex
review, item 3: a run `weeks` days from the one unit of another standing
it could join walked every day between, and every search for payers the
occupied days of the other standings between, once a run, the work four
times over as the rows doubled): each search reads, outward from the
unit's day in the order above, only days that can answer it -- the
payers' walk the days of the standing it asks not yet read or holding a
payer whose move keeps the count, each rank's place and status kept as
ranks move, and the payers keeping nothing before it counted, not read
(its verifier: a wall of pairs whose moves keep no count, between the
runs and their payers, was read again for every payer, the work four
times over as the rows doubled); PUT BACK PAID BACK the days whose parent at
the run's place holds a unit of its group that some rank still holds;
SPREAD's escapes, paid and not, the days whose parent has a free place
of the rank's group -- each next such day found by halving, and each
index kept as ranks move. The days asked, and their order, are those
above; doubling the rows doubles the work, the unit to join, the place
and the payers near or far, or behind such a wall. The tails making room at midnight are
followed by SPREAD PAID BACK and SPREAD BY SUBSTITUTE too. Where no
weekday census stands none of the three runs, and every twin is as
before: the last resorts of steps 2 and 3 and G7.3g's free a run to a day
of another weekday there.

Where a field's groups still do not hold, one deviation names its census;
where they hold and the reachable count is left long, THE CENSUS STANDS
AND THE COUNT GIVES WAY, and the report says so in place of its long
sentence: no placement keeping each burst of cells written alike together
met both (the plan's RESIDUAL; a burst holding a tail's pinned boundary
cannot move whole, and bursts larger than what a group owes cannot be
carried in whole units -- 7 of the 90 twins above, against 2341173,
which publishes no minute census); and where they hold and the steps left
the reachable count below both the count they keep and the count they
were handed, the report names the clock pass as its cause in place of
the short sentence (lane J2's skeptic, item 1: stamps five minutes apart,
every one different, were moved onto their heaps at 893 values of 1,000,
and the report blamed the ways of writing a value). A column whose
different values crowd the lattice its minute's and second's facts would
pin publishes neither (contract NF121 and NF122), so no field pass runs
on it; a dense grid of random times, filling it no more than a uniform
draw of its rows would, is not crowded and keeps them (lane J2's second
skeptic, item 1), nor is a grid no value of which is written once,
publishing no count at midnight and holding no more than 1,000 different
values, that fills it less than a fifth more than that draw (its Codex
review, item 2: 1,000 stamps five minutes or a minute apart, each written
twice, met every fact; where a count at midnight is published such grids,
written twice from five minutes up, missed and stay withheld, and so do
grids with a value written once -- with the fifth, two minutes apart
with a third once, 1,000 and 1,100 values came back 999 and 1,096 at
floor 11 -- and grids of more different values: of 276 grids with no
value written once swept with the fifth at any size, 1 to 60 minutes
apart, each written two, three or four times, 500 to 2,500 values,
floors 11 and 36, every twin of fewer than 1,250 values met its facts,
and 1,000 is 80 % of that first miss; its two verifiers and the
orchestrator's ruling). Its points are counted on the lattice at its
own phase (lane J3: `calendar_clock.crowding_unit`, the step dividing
sixty and every difference between two heaps' values), and a lattice the
body is drawn finer than -- stamps fifteen minutes apart from 07:13,
drawn a minute at a time and moved onto their heaps -- is crowded where
no value is written once once filled to the share and above that draw
by any margin (its Codex review: not at or below it),
as is a grid no value of which is written once beside a published count
at midnight and more than 1,000 different values (a sweep of 512 grids
on d3712a1, 1 to 60 minutes apart from midnight, 00:37, 07:13 and
07:13:20, written once to four times, 500 to 5,000 values, floors 11
and 36, three twins each: 254 published pairs that missed now withhold
and meet, 372 that met withhold too; the same grids drawn on midnight met
in 96 of 100 published pairs, so the drawing rule at the lattice's own
phase, not changed here, could keep their facts: untested, inferred
from those 96; every grid swept held a value in every lattice slot; its
Codex review: 1,500 of 2,000 quarter-hour slots from 00:13, each written
twice, 0.7557 of their lattice against a draw's 0.7795, keep the facts
their twins meet, and of 103 grids with up to 30 % of their slots empty,
floors 11 and 36, the 70 pairs at or below the draw publish and 68 meet
every fact, the other 2 missing in one twin of three as on d3712a1; its
verifier: both exceptions ask the share and the draw on the places the
published counts leave -- the points on an hour the hour census counts
and a minute and second the fields' facts hold
(`calendar_clock.lattice_places`) -- so a grid written only by day or
with every third slot empty, below the draw on every point and missing,
withholds and meets; of the verifier's 231 grids, floors 11 and 36, 6
published pairs still miss: 2,500 stamps five minutes apart, 3 % empty,
each written four times, floor 11, 0.004 below the draw, in 3 twins of 3
from 07:13 and 2 of 3 from 00:13, and four grids fifteen minutes apart
written four times in one twin of three, two of them as on d3712a1). So
a dense grid filling the places its counts leave no more than a uniform
draw keeps its facts under both exceptions. The rule
claims no impossibility: it withholds where twins were measured to miss.
Last, where the column publishes its count at midnight -- or withholds it
for its size, and so still owes the count it held before these passes
(plan P4-D191) -- THE TAILS KEEP IT:
while more ranks than it stand at a written midnight, the first unpinned
tail rank at one steps off it by its tail's drawing unit inside its
stratum, or by the written unit where the stratum is narrower than that;
while fewer, the first unpinned tail rank off one takes the
nearest midnight inside its stratum; each tail's ranks are then sorted.
Where the count is withheld for its size, most of the column stands at
midnight and the strata leave it short, each tail rank still off a
written midnight -- pinned or not, a tie of tail ranks together, in rank
order -- takes its own day's midnight where that stands strictly after
the rank before it, else the next day's where that stands strictly
before the rank after it, never on a hole's day: no rank meets another
and the body is not moved (lane J2's skeptic, item 3; R4's `%.15g`
column nine in ten at midnight, its ENDs derived off midnight, came back
at 989 of the 990 owed). The producer now withholds both fields where
fewer parsed cells than the line stand off 00:00:00 beside such a count
(contract NF123 and NF124, a reason of its own since the lane's Codex
review, item 4; lane J2's second skeptic, item 2), so the step serves a
profile that publishes them beside it.

**Its frozen cases** are states of ranks and drawing units: the twentieth
vectors file, `tests/reference/generation-branch-vectors-20.json`, holds
forty-five -- SPREAD and PUT BACK paid back beside a weekday census, a
payer that would change the count passed over, SPREAD by substitute, a
payer standing on the
unit a run joins passed over and a run asked as it stands (lane J2), both
payer exclusions moved back 28,000 days to 1947 (its Codex review, item
1), the
pass on a field of minutes with heaps and on a field of
seconds with a kin group of minutes, KIN SHARES over two hours,
carried from gap to gap over four days, reconciled against what each hour
holds where a gap's hour 8 can stand on no minute 0, and never splitting
a unit two tied ranks of an hour share, a written midnight a kind of its
own (85 days, where by nearness 85 ranks took a midnight and 21 stayed
there), KIN SHARES keeping the cells at midnight with hour 0 a kin group
alone and beside hour 1, the exchange's three answers,
PUT BACK once more after it, SUBSTITUTE, SPREAD, the tails keeping the count at midnight by their
drawing unit and, in a stratum narrower than it, by the written unit, and
taking a midnight where the count there is short, every tail rank giving
way to a count owed for its size and none onto a hole day, the tails making room at
midnight for a rank of the body, never by a tail step raising the count
and with SPREAD after them where the step left it short, KIN SHARES
giving no kin group more of minute 0 than its ranks free to stand there,
and none a part of a group its ranks never reach (hour 8 off minute 0 in
every gap, hours 9 and 10 an even split) nor what the kin groups after
it claim,
a shared written unit moved whole, and past its groups' room in the
leftover, a draw laid
on its unit, G7.3b step 7's tail END held off a midnight the count leaves
it none of, a tail listing a value written 00:00:00 on any day charged
for it, and the drawing units of a half-hour grid, a column on the
hour, a column whose seconds alone are pinned, one census group
holding minute 0 and heaps beside a withheld census of the rest, which
pin nothing -- each with the answer this section gives it.

#### G7.3j The dates that stand out: pinned, the parts split and drawn by key

(Landing 3b.6, plan P4-D369.) A column counted in days -- G7.1's ordinal
space `date` -- that publishes `heavy_dates` holds each listed date at
its published count; every other column is drawn and moved exactly as
before, so its twin is unchanged byte for byte. The KNOTS are the body's
pins: the two tail boundaries and each published rung, at its rank.

1. **The layout.** Each listed date's rows are a RUN of ranks pinned on
   it. A knot on a listed date is COVERED: the run stands around it,
   starting inside the interval contract HD4's carrying forward and
   back gives it. The unlisted knots cut the body into SEGMENTS and the
   covered runs cut each segment into PARTS; a listed date with no knot
   on it is LOOSE, its run standing at the start of the part it lies in.
   A part's ORDINARY ranks take its days -- an unlisted knot's day is a
   day of both parts beside it -- and its FREE days are those that are
   no listed date and no hole of the description.
2. **The split.** How many ordinary ranks each part holds, inside the
   bounds the covered runs' starts leave. Open first every part a split
   cannot leave empty and every part with free days that touches an
   unlisted knot; in a segment holding ordinary ranks with none open,
   its part with the most free days; while the segment's bounds hold no
   split, the next by free days; then the rest, most free days first,
   while their cost fits the BUDGET: the column's count of different
   values, where the twin keeps it, less the listed dates, the unlisted
   knots' days and each tail's (its published values, or one). A part
   costs the weekday groups it offers a free day of that still owe rows
   (one where no census stands), a part touching a knot one less where
   the knots force it open. Inside, the ranks go by WEIGHTED ROOM: each
   free day weighs what its group of the first census beside the list
   owes the ordinary ranks -- its count less its listed rows and its
   unlisted knots -- over that group's free days in the whole body.
3. **The repair.** The split's SCORE is the rows the parts cannot place
   on the groups of the weekday and day-of-month censuses that owe them
   (a capacity max-flow from the parts to the groups, per census), and
   then the new days the budget asks beyond the most the parts can open
   (a min-cost max-flow placing every owed row, a part's first rows on
   a group, up to its free days there, cheaper). While the score is
   above nought, the one move that lowers it most -- some ranks from one
   open part to another of the same segment, every covered run still
   around its knots, the count found by halving -- is made, at most 64
   times (the 3b.6 skeptic's B1).
4. **The draw.** The body keeps one word per ordinary rank, in rank
   order, so the high tail reads the words it always read. A part's
   ranks are split by KEY, its free days of one group of each census
   beside the list: SPREAD rakes the keys' free days (a day the part
   shares with the part before it not counted) to the parts' ranks and
   each census's owed rows sixty times and rounds them by a flow; where
   SPREAD fills more keys holding no knot's day than the new days the
   count leaves -- the twin's count of different days less those the
   listed dates, the knots and both tails already hold -- the lightest
   keys take none and the rest are raked again, at most eight times,
   and then FEW puts the ranks on as few keys as one flow per census
   finds; where SPREAD cannot open the new days the count leaves, WIDE
   puts as many ranks on days of their own as a min-cost flow allows.
   The first split placing every owed row and able to open exactly the
   new days left is taken, a rank no flow placed going to its part's
   widest key and a rank a rounding placed beyond the part's own leaving
   its fullest key. Each key opens at least one new day where it holds ranks
   and no knot's day, and the rest go where the ranks stand thickest (a
   density found by halving); its new days are drawn among its free days
   by the words of its first slots, no day twice, each taking that
   slot's rank, and every other rank of the key is drawn uniformly over
   its new days and its knots' days. Each part's values are sorted onto
   its ranks.
5. **The passes.** Every listed date is a hole of the count pass, of the
   day pass and of the step off an absent spelling, which offer it to no
   other rank. Where the drawn ranks already meet every census beside
   the list, keep off every hole and hold the count of different values
   as the validator judges it, the day pass leaves them as drawn;
   elsewhere it runs as before, its step 8.5 included. THE COUNT AS THE
   VALIDATOR JUDGES IT (the orchestrator's ruling (c) of 2026-10-13):
   exactly where the count pass reaches it and the published count lies
   inside G12.5's envelope drawn on the description's own gaps (the
   list's parts left out, as the validator draws it); elsewhere the
   distance outside that envelope, nought inside it
   (`contract.datetime_count_held_exactly`, the one statement the
   validator, the report and this section ask).
6. **The sort.** After every other pass the body's ranks are sorted
   again; every value stayed inside its part, so each boundary and rung
   reads its own value. A listed date not holding its count is named
   (`heavy_dates`).
7. **What gives way** (the orchestrator's rulings (a) and (b) of
   2026-10-13). Where the sorted ranks meet every group of the weekday
   and the day-of-month census beside the list, the listed twin stands,
   whatever the count of different values holds: beside a list the
   count gives way, and where it is off as step 5 judges it and the
   twin of the column listing nothing stands nearer it, one deviation
   says the count gave way to the listed dates, read as the count's
   cause. Where they miss a group, the column is drawn again
   from the same words as if it listed no date -- the twin of the
   column without `heavy_dates`, byte for byte -- and the two are
   weighed by ROWS OFF the published counts: over every group of both
   censuses and every listed date, the rows a twin holds more or fewer
   than its count, summed. That twin is taken only where it stands
   fewer rows off, and one deviation names the list and the census it
   gave way to (`heavy_dates`, "as if no date were listed"); a tie
   keeps the list, and then each missed census's deviation says it
   gave way to the listed dates wherever the twin listing nothing meets
   that census. The count of different values does
   not enter the weighing. At most twice the column's work. The pass
   draws no word of its own.
8. **The spelling keeps the date** (the Codex review of landing 3b.6,
   item 1). Once G7.5 has allocated every rank's spelling and before any
   cell is written, each rank on a listed date, ascending, whose cell
   would wear an absent spelling keeps its date (`_listed_date_respelled`,
   the one rule every step that would move such a rank asks first): it
   TRADES spellings with the first rank, ascending, standing on no
   listed date, not yet traded, of its convention class (the same form
   and offset; on a textual member the same month, elsewhere the month
   below ten or not; the day below ten or not) and wearing another
   spelling the column allocates, first allocated first, under which its
   date wears no absent spelling, where that rank's own date wears none
   in its spelling -- so every census of spellings keeps its counts; a
   refused date's ranks are passed over together, at most 64 dates per
   spelling. With no such rank it takes the first such spelling alone,
   the spelling censuses recounted on the cells; with none, G7.5's step
   off an absent spelling moves it as before. The listed counts are then
   recounted on the written cells as V5-D1 counts them, and a miss is
   named (`heavy_dates`) before any sentence says they are met. A TAIL
   RANK the step off cannot move is offered the same trade in the same
   walk (the Codex review of landing I3b1): one whose cell would wear an
   absent spelling and for which no date 1 to (absent spellings + 1)
   away, inside its own window (its stratum) and not listed, written in
   its spelling, wears none (`_listed_stuck`) -- a tail date alone in its
   stratum whose other spelling is declared missing, which kept that
   spelling and read back as no value. Its
frozen cases are states in the nineteenth vectors file,
`tests/reference/generation-branch-vectors-19.json`: a covered run, two
loose dates, a listed boundary day, two listed dates with a hole between
them, Monday and Thursday sessions whose split the census repair moves,
sessions with stray rows whose split the repair moves for the count's
new days, and six Mays beside both censuses -- each with the answer this
section gives it, and no G14.3 case.

#### G7.3k The calendar on each rank's own clock, and the form step

(Landing 3b.7, plan P4-D378.) The censuses of the calendar -- the weekday
(G7.3f), the day of the month (G7.3i) and the hour (G7.3g), and, since
batch 3b's merge of lane J2, the minute's and the second's heaps and
censuses (G7.3h) -- stand on a column whose cells wear more than one
offset, read on the shared clock, and on a column of the joint member,
each cell counted at the day, hour, minute and second it is WRITTEN at,
on its own clock, and a bare date at its midnight.
The order of G7 is unchanged: forms, instants, offsets (G7.4, its step 1a
fixing the pinned ranks' keys), the move to midnight with the FORM STEP
first, the step off midnight, the count pass, then the day, hour and
minute passes; offsets and forms come before the passes because a pass
can read a rank's clock only once its offset is known.

1. **THE FRAME.** Each rank's SHIFT is its offset in seconds east of the
   shared clock (nought for a rank written with none, and everywhere on
   a column read on its own clock). On the shared clock, where a census
   of the calendar is published, every place a pass reads -- each rank's
   ordinal, its gap, and the layout's pins and boundaries -- is put on the
   rank's own clock by adding its shift, so every bin a pass reads is the
   field the cell is written at, and a move of whole days or hours moves
   the written field by as much, the rank's offset fixed. A column all at
   a LOCAL midnight is put in days of the frame and read as on its own
   clock, so the joint day plan of G7.3i meets its day of the month;
   where a rank is not on a midnight of its own clock the frame stays in
   seconds. Every other column needs no frame and every pass runs on it
   exactly as before.
2. **THE FRAME TAKEN BACK, RUN BY RUN.** A pass keeps each rank inside
   its own gap on its own clock and then sorts each run of the ranks it
   moved by the written place, which may hand one rank's place to a rank
   of another offset. So within each run of body ranks between two pins
   -- one gap, no bare date -- the written places are kept and the run's
   offsets matched to them: the places ascending, each taking the least
   offset left whose instant is not past the gap's top (the largest left
   where none is); the run is then written in the order of its instants,
   each place with its offset. Every written field a census counts, every
   offset count and every gap stands. Pinned ranks, ranks whose gap is
   one place and bare dates in a frame of seconds are given back as they
   were. THE TAILS are taken back as a whole, as G7.3h moves a tail rank
   off or onto a midnight of its own clock to keep the count at midnight
   and then sorts each tail by the place it reads -- the ranks that never
   move with the others -- which may hand one rank's place to a rank of
   another offset: the places the passes left on EVERY tail rank are
   held; each rank that never moves claims its own place -- its instant
   plus its shift, in the frame's unit -- first; each movable one whose
   own place is still held keeps its instant; each other movable one, the
   one whose gap ends first on its own clock served first (ties by rank),
   takes the least place left that puts its instant inside its own gap,
   with its own offset, and stays where it was where none does (the Codex
   review of landing I3b2d, item 3: given back as they stood before the
   passes, 1,000 stamps on the hour at `+01:00` and `+02:00`, half at
   midnight, came back with 501 cells at midnight against 500; and its
   verifier: served in rank order, `-08:00` beside `+09:00` came back with
   501 at floor 36, and with the unmoving ranks' places left out, 250
   bare dates beside `-06:00` and `+05:30` stamps came back with 101 to
   103 stamps at midnight against 100).
   In a frame of DAYS a bare date moves as a day and stands in its gap's
   run, and a run holding one keeps every rank's form and offset, as a
   bare date's form cannot pass to another rank (the landing's Codex
   review, item 2): its days ascending each go to a rank of the least
   shift left whose instant is not past the gap's top, else of the
   largest shift left -- a bare date's shift nought -- and among one
   shift's ranks to the next by the day the passes left it and then by
   rank, so a rank whose day keeps it inside the gap keeps its day. A
   pass may hand a `+02:00` midnight's day at the
   gap's top to a bare date, whose midnight that day is past the top: an
   export of bare dates beside `T00:00:00+02:00` stamps then wrote a bare
   date beyond its high boundary, and the twin's boundary came back two
   hours late. The run is not re-sorted by instant.
3. **BARE DATES.** On a clocked column of the joint member the passes of
   G7.3g and G7.3h pin every bare-date rank, which counts at hour 0,
   minute 0 and second 0, a gap of movable ranks running across it, and so does
   the weekday pass where the column is counted in seconds or published
   on the shared clock; a column counted in days moves its bare dates as
   days, and so does a column the frame puts in days: each pass asks this
   of the facts it is handed, the frame's, never the column's own (the
   landing's Codex review, item 2: every month of 2020 to 2024, eleven bare
   dates on the 15th beside eleven `T00:00:00-03:00` stamps of that day,
   1,320 rows; pinned by the column's own facts on the shared clock, the
   bare dates stayed where the form step spread them, and the twin wrote
   654 cells on the 15th and 622 elsewhere for a census of 1,276 and
   nought at the floor of 11).
4. **THE FORM STEP** (the design's decision D4, its skeptic's major 2 and
   minor 4; residual R-P4-12 closed on clocked columns). G7.5's form
   allocation spends `resolution_mix`'s count of `iso-date` on a clocked
   column of the joint member: first on the ranks the layout fixes at a
   midnight of a rank written with no offset, in rank order, while it
   lasts, every other fixed rank a moment; then over the other ranks by
   the smooth rotation of the all-midnight column, CAPPED PER GAP at the
   days whose midnight lies in the gap -- less those fixed ranks hold,
   where the column's values are all different; every rank where they
   repeat, and none where the gap holds no midnight -- a gap at its cap
   passing its turn on, the credit carried, and the credit left at the end
   given to the first ranks with room; what every gap's free days still
   leave over goes to the first ranks whose gap holds any midnight, so
   every bare date the count names is written as one (the landing's
   repair, item 2: written as moments they took real offset keys and
   missed `utc_offsets` and `n_at_midnight`); never more ranks than the
   count, and never more in the body than hour 0's group counts, this
   pass too: where that cap stands and the tails' gaps hold fewer
   midnight days than the source's tails held bare dates, the dates left
   over are written as moments and `resolution_mix` gives way, named,
   the hour census held (its second skeptic, item 1: `noon_ends`, bare
   dates on the first and last eighth of a span of noon stamps with
   every value different, writes 98 of 100 at 400 rows, 248 of 250 at
   1,000 and 2,498 of 2,500 at 10,000 -- 97, 247 and 2,497 at the floor
   of 36; with the cap off the hour census misses instead; vectors case
   `leftover_capped_at_hour_zero`). The ranks are spent in rank order,
   so where bare dates and stamps share days the twin spreads the bare
   dates evenly over the span, wherever in time the source held them
   (P4-D378's stated limits). Then, as the first part of the move to
   midnight, each gap's
   bare-date ranks in rank order are stood on midnight days of the gap: off a
   day a published census counts nought on, where one of the gap's first
   400 days is not; each the first at or after its instant, else the
   nearest before; where the column is all different, on days of their
   own no fixed rank holds, the run laid back from the gap's top where it
   went past it, and a rank the free days cannot hold stood on its nearest
   midnight of the gap as where the values repeat, a day another value
   holds: the count of different values then falls short, inside G12.5's
   envelope, and the twin's report says so. The move to midnight then
   counts every bare date as standing at midnight and owes only the rest.

#### G7.3l The L0 band totals of a date column (layer L0, plan P4-D404; specified, NOT BUILT)

**No generator in this repository runs this section yet; lane BT builds
it.** An ELIGIBLE datetime column (G5.7's switch) carries an L0 block
whose edges `e_1 < ... < e_m` are among its published interior rungs,
with one count for each range band over its `P` parsed cells, compared
in G7.1's ordinal space on the clock its ladder is read on. The cut
rank of edge `j` is `R_j = c_0 + ... + c_(j-1)`, and `k_j` is the rank
the edge's rung is selected from (the smallest such rank where several
rungs select `e_j`). Its preconditions are G5.7a's, read for this role:

- **(D1)** the range counts sum to `P`;
- **(D2)** every pinned rank of G7.3 (the boundaries, the rungs, and the
  covered runs of G7.3j) stands below `R_j` where its value is below
  `e_j`, and at or above `R_j` where its value is `e_j` or later.

Every description a producer writes passes both, because the pins are
the real column's own order statistics. Where one fails, the column is
made without L0 and named (rule B3 of G5.7h).

**THE EDGE RUN.** G7.3 pins rank `k_j` to `e_j`. On an eligible column
every rank from `R_j` to `k_j` is pinned to `e_j`. The real column held
`e_j` at every one of those ranks: sorted, its first value at or after
`e_j` stands at rank `R_j` and its value at `k_j` is `e_j`, so every
rank between them holds `e_j`. A pinned rank spends no word (G7.3), so
the run's ranks read none; the column is still handed its `P - 2`
words, and no column after it moves.

**THE GAP BELOW AN EDGE RUN ENDS ONE UNIT SHORT OF THE EDGE.** Its upper
place is the START of the edge's unit, `X_b = e_j * 2**20`, and not the
unit's middle or the straightest place, and its ordinals are kept
inside `[Lo_a, e_j - 1]`. Since `Lo_a`, the pin below, is earlier than
`e_j` (D2), the gap is never empty of room. The gap above the run starts
at the run's value, as every gap starts at its lower pin.

**Every pass keeps the band totals.** G7.3's count passes, the day pass
(G7.3f), the clock passes (G7.3g, G7.3h), the joint day plan (G7.3i),
the dates that stand out (G7.3j) and the calendar and form steps
(G7.3k) move a body rank only inside its own gap and never move a
pinned rank. That is the method's own invariant, the one that keeps
every rung on its published value. With each gap below an edge run
ending one unit short of the edge, the same invariant keeps every band
total: `R_j` ranks stand below `e_j` and the rest at or after it,
whatever the passes do.

**And the spelling step keeps the piece.** One step after those passes
moves a parsed cell's instant: G7.5's exception, where every mark
offered to a rank spells an absent cell, steps a whole-unit rank to the
nearest unit whose spelling is not absent, first inside its G12.4
window and then inside `[earliest, latest]`. Neither range stops at a
cut, and G12.15 leaves a date column's windows as they are, so the step
could carry a cell across an edge: in a gap whose lower pin is
`2024-01-29` below the edge `2024-02-01`, with `2024-01-30` and
`2024-01-31` declared absent (each published at a count of 11), a rank
below the cut drawn on January 31 would be written February 1, nearer
than January 29, and the band below would lose a row to the band above
(the outside review of this page, its item 2). On an eligible column
both ranges are cut to the rank's PIECE, the units from its band's
lower edge up to the unit before its upper edge (from `earliest` in the
lowest band, to `latest` in the highest): the rank above is written
January 29. Where no unit of the piece qualifies, the allocated form
stands, as G7.5 lets it stand where no unit qualifies today, counted as
a deviation of `n_present`, and rule B1 names the band row it leaves
short. The cell never crosses a cut. The step reaches interior ranks
only, so neither end of the column moves. The partial
cells and the stand-ins of G7.5 stand inside `n_unparsed`, in the
`other` group, so their walks move no band total.

**A listed date on an edge** (G7.3j). A listed date equal to `e_j` is a
covered knot, and its run starts at `R_j`. That start lies inside the
interval contract HD4 gives it, because `R_j` is the real run's own
start and the real column meets HD4. Step 3's repair never moves it.
An unlisted edge's day is a day of the part ABOVE the edge only, where
G7.3j step 1 makes an unlisted knot's day a day of both parts beside it.

**The tails.** An edge equal to the low boundary has `R_j = m_lo` by
(D2), so its run is the boundary's own pinned rank, and the tails are
placed exactly as today: the low tail's ranks lie below the low
boundary, which is at or before `e_1`, and the high tail's after the
high boundary, which is at or after `e_m`.

**What each fact owes.** The rungs stay exact (every pin is still a
pin). The tails, their rows and their distances are as today. The
weekday, hour, day-of-month, minute and second censuses, the count at
midnight, the widths, the listed dates' counts and `n_distinct` within
G12.5's envelope are met wherever the passes find room inside the
gaps, which are now a unit narrower below each edge and short of each
edge run's ranks; otherwise rule B1 applies, and every census row the
walls leave unmet is named exactly as each pass names a miss today.
Inside the walls, the orchestrator's rulings (a) to (c) of 2026-10-13
order the list, the census and the count as before (G7.3j step 5). The
edge run adds no value the column did not hold, since each `e_j` is a
published rung.

**Measured** (G5.7i): the invented date column missed 8 to 12 rows of
its band totals at 5,000 rows and 33 to 45 at 20,000, over seeds 0 to
2.

### G7.4 Offsets: only where recorded

`utc_offsets` maps an offset text to a count, under the small-cell
floor, with a `(withheld)` key pooling everything below it and a
`(none)` key counting offsetless cells.

Allocation, over the `P` parsed cells in ascending rank:

0. A rank G7.5 writes as a bare date is settled first, with no
   offset: it consumes one from `(none)`, or from `(withheld)` where
   `(none)` has no count left (landing 2b.3).
1. **NO END TAKES AN OFFSET OF ITS OWN** (stage 3, plan P4-D328): the
   description names no offset for the two end rows, because it
   describes no end row at all, so both ends join the allocation of step
   2 like every other rank and the two keys are gone from the format.
   What remains of this step is the midnight rule. On a column G7.5
   moves onto a midnight -- wholly at midnight on the `utc` clock, or
   only partly at midnight on either clock
   (integration repair of landing 2b.3: 1,000 moments over five days
   under `+01:00` and `+02:00`, 980 of them at local midnight, stood
   mostly between pinned ranks of one instant, took their offsets in
   sorted order, and 82 were written an hour off midnight) -- each rank
   whose instant the layout of G7.3 fixes at ONE PLACE: a boundary rank,
   a published rung's rank, and a tail's derived end or group where it
   stands at one instant, with each rank standing between two pinned
   ranks of one instant -- takes the first offset,
   the real offsets in sorted order and then `(none)`, under which that
   instant stands at midnight and whose key has a count left (repair pass
   of landing 2b.3: a rung at a midnight of the shared clock whose `Z` was
   spent takes `(none)`, and ranks between p90 and the end on one such
   midnight were written `T02:00:00+02:00`).
1a. **THE PINNED OFFSETS** (landing 3b.7, plan P4-D378; the design
   skeptic's blocker 1 and item (a)). On the shared clock, where a census
   of the calendar is published, or where `n_at_midnight` is withheld for
   its size and some block of ranks the layout fixes at one instant stands
   at a midnight of the first sorted key: each such block -- a boundary, a
   rung, a tail's listed values, and the ranks between two pins of one
   instant -- in rank order, not taken by step 1, takes among the keys
   with as many ranks left as it holds, in this step's order, the first
   that breaks the fewest of two asks: off a local midnight where the
   count at midnight is withheld for its size; and, for a body block, its
   WRITTEN day, day of the month, hour, minute and second in a group of
   every published census with room left for it, room being the group's
   count less the blocks already placed there. The minute's and the
   second's facts are laid as groups of their sixty values: each heap a
   group of its own value with its count, each census group the values of
   it no heap holds with its count, and, with heaps and no census, every
   other value one group of the body's cells less the heaps' (the Codex
   review of landing I3b2d, item 2: 1,000 stamps on the hour at `-06:00`
   and `+05:30`, every body cell on minute 0 of its own clock, published a
   heap of 978 there; asked of the day and the hour alone, blocks took
   `+05:30` and stood on minute 30, where no pass moves a pinned rank, and
   the twin held 976). A pinned rank never moves, so the field it
   is written at is its key's alone; the source's own offsets prove a
   choice keeping every census exists. The keys' counts and the groups'
   room are spent as each block takes its key, and the block's other keys
   follow as step 1's fallbacks. Every other column takes no key here and
   is allocated exactly as before.
   **A BLOCK MAY BE SPLIT** (the landing's Codex review, item 1): where no
   one key breaks nothing, a body block under a census is shared out --
   the keys in this step's order, each written off a withheld midnight,
   taking as many of its ranks as their count left and the room of every
   group their written place falls in allow, until the block is spent,
   the ranks in rank order; one key a block cannot keep a census whose
   group under each key holds only part of it (150 cells each of
   `2024-07-19T09:00:00Z` and `T10:00:00+01:00` among 700 daily stamps at
   those two keys: two rungs fixed 251 ranks at that instant, `+01:00`
   wrote them all in hour 10, which holds 150, and the twin's hours came
   back 132, 251, 297, 298 for 150, 150, 339, 339 at every seed).
   **AND WRITTEN AT `:60`** (item 3): where no share breaks
   nothing either, a body block at a minute's first second, between two
   published values of one text on a column written to the second, asks
   the same two -- one key, then a split -- of the place one second
   earlier, the minute before's `HH:MM:60`, whose instant is the block's
   (G7.1): the shared clock publishes the instant of a cell written `:60`,
   never the `:60` the source wrote, and a leap second counts on the day, hour
   and minute it is WRITTEN. Where that breaks nothing the block's pins
   take that `HH:MM:60` as their text, so every pass counts the block where
   it is written and G7.5 writes it from those fields (400 cells at
   `2016-12-31T23:59:60Z` among 600 noon stamps at `Z` and `+00:00` in
   turn: the rungs fixed 251 ranks at the instant published as
   `2017-01-01 00:00:00`, written at midnight on a Sunday in hour 0, a
   group of nought, and no twin held the hour and weekday censuses or
   the withheld count at midnight at any seed). Where nothing
   breaks nothing, the one key breaking the fewest at the ordinary place
   takes the block whole, as before.
2. The remaining counts are spent over the remaining ranks, taking the
   offset keys in the profile's own sorted key order, `(none)` and
   `(withheld)` last. ON THE SHARED CLOCK WHERE A CENSUS OF THE CALENDAR IS
   PUBLISHED (landing 3b.7, plan P4-D378) the keys are spread over the
   GAPS instead: the open ranks of each gap of the body take one key
   together where its count left holds them, the gaps in rank order
   taking the keys by the smooth rotation of the counts left weighted by
   each gap's size -- the largest credit with room, the earlier key on a
   tie -- and a gap no key holds whole is filled key by key, the largest
   credit first. So each key's ranks stand across the column and each
   gap's ranks read one clock (G7.3k): spent in one block, the skeptic's
   `few_off` wrote its 196 cells at `+05:30` on the body's first ranks,
   whose first gap of 8.25 hours holds no hour the census counts on that
   clock, and 87 missed the hour census at 10,000 rows. The ranks are visited in ascending rank order,
   except on a column moved onto a midnight, where they are visited
   **SCARCEST FIRST** (stage 3, repairing plan P4-D254): each remaining
   rank is counted for how many keys both have a count left AND put a
   midnight inside that rank's own gap (the bounds of G12.4), and the
   ranks are taken in ascending order of that count, ties in ascending
   rank order. Measured on 1,000 moments over five days under `+01:00`
   and `+02:00`, 980 of them at local midnight: spending in rank order
   gave a key feasible for nearly every rank to ranks that had another,
   and the 84 ranks in the twelve-hour gap between the last rung and the
   high boundary -- where only `+02:00` puts a midnight inside the gap --
   found it gone, so the twin held 896 and missed both midnight
   obligations. Counting first and spending the scarcest first writes
   all 980. Where every key is feasible for every rank the count is the
   same for all of them and the order is ascending rank order again, so
   no column outside this rule moves a byte.
3. A cell allocated `(none)` is written with **no offset**.
4. A cell allocated `(withheld)` is written with **no offset** as well,
   and this is a loss, named as one: the profile does not say which
   offsets those cells carried, so the twin has no published way to
   spell them apart. See G11 instance 3.

**The clock conversion, which is not optional.** `datetimes_read_at`
says which clock the two tail boundaries, the values a tail lists and
the ladder are written on:

- `local` — one offset wrote the whole column, so the published text IS
  the local wall clock. The cell text is the canonical form of the
  ordinal, and the offset is appended as published.
- `utc` — two or more offsets appeared, so the published text is the
  INSTANT. A cell that carries an offset must be written on that
  offset's own wall clock, or the twin would re-profile to a different
  instant. So:

  ```
  local_ordinal = ordinal + offset_in_seconds     (resolution `datetime`)
  local_ordinal = ordinal                          (resolution `date`,
                                                    `month`, `quarter`:
                                                    no clock to shift)
  ```

  where `offset_in_seconds` is `+/- (3600 * HH + 60 * MM)` read from the
  offset text, and `Z` is zero. The cell text is the canonical form of
  `local_ordinal` followed by the offset.

`datetimes_read_at` is EXACT-OBSERVABLE (P2-R4-F3) and is met by this
construction whenever the published offset map holds two or more keys,
because the twin then writes two or more offset kinds. Where the map's
only key is `(withheld)` and the published reading is `utc`, the twin
writes one kind, re-profiles as `local`, and the report names it. That
corner is bounded: it needs two or more distinct offsets each used by
fewer rows than the small-cell floor.

**THE TWO KINDS ARE COUNTED OVER WHAT THE CELLS WEAR, AND NONE IS A
KIND** (*corrected by the dates pass of the stage-3 review, item 8*).
There are two kinds a cell can wear: a NAMED offset, written out after
the moment, and NO offset at all -- the census's own `(none)` member,
which is also what a rank spent from a withheld pool is written with.
The report counted the named ones alone, dropping the offsetless member
before measuring the diversity, so a column publishing
`{"(none)": 50, "+01:00": 50}` -- a census that withholds nothing --
was told that every offset it carried had been held back as too rare to
publish, on a twin that wrote both published members exactly. Measured
on 100 successive noon timestamps alternating no offset and `+01:00`,
at every seed.

### G7.5 Writing the cell IN ITS SOURCE'S OWN FORM, at the published precision

**Owner decision 5 is REVERSED** (owner ruling 2026-09-15, plan P4-D61,
landing 2b.6). The history is kept because it is the record of what this
rule cost while it stood. D12 fixed ISO 8601 with an explicit offset;
owner decision 5 amended it for twin CSV cells, because the producer
legitimately publishes offsetless dates and quarters and no output could
satisfy both D12 and the published facts, and it chose the ISO form at
the recorded precision for EVERY member. Residual R-P2-7 disclosed the
price: a month-first table yielded ISO twin dates, so a person's own
parsing call needed a different format argument on the twin than on
their table. Measured: `strptime('%m/%d/%Y')` parsed 400 of 400 real
cells and none of the twin's; a compact `YYYYMMDD` column's ISO twin
FAILED this tool's own validation, because the real cells are also
numbers and the ISO cells are not.

**So a twin datetime cell is written in the MEMBER that read the real
column — the document's `format` — at the precision the profile records,
and an offset is written only where the profile records a real one.**
The date half is written by the member; the clock half, the mark before
it and the offset after it are unchanged by the reversal. The member
fixes the field order, the delimiter and the year's width; what it does
not fix is carried by four censuses the description publishes, each
allocated to the ranks that can show it by the same smooth weighted
rotation the marks use, which draws no word:

| written by | census | the words |
|---|---|---|
| how wide the month and day fields were | `date_field_widths` | `padded`, `unpadded`, `first-padded`, `second-padded` for a cell whose two fields are both below ten; `first-field-padded`, `first-field-unpadded`, `second-field-padded`, `second-field-unpadded` for a cell where one alone is — ONE word per CELL |
| how a month NAME was written | `month_name_styles` | one joint `<case>-<length>-<mark>-<comma>` word, the length `either` on a cell of May |
| the case of a quarter's marker | `quarter_marker_case` | `upper`, `lower` |
| the case of a zulu offset marker | `zulu_case` | `upper`, `lower` |

**A SLASHED STAMP'S CLOCK HALF IS WRITTEN IN ITS STYLE** (landing T1, plan
P4-D370). Its one `datetime_separators` word names it (contract C6-10a,
D12a): `space` is the two-figure 24-hour clock every stamp wrote before,
and `space h AM-PM` and the rest a width and a face. Every rank writes
it, the hour at its width, on its face -- midnight `12:00 AM`, noon
`12:00 PM`, on the declared 12-hour face `12:00` and the hour past noon
less twelve -- at the precision the profile records. A pooled word names
none, and the 24-hour clock is written. The end of such a column is its
own instant written whole: a stamp holds no sixtieth second.

**STEP 5: THE WIDTH CENSUS'S UNNAMED REMAINDER** (landing T1; carried at
plan l.17955 as case (a)). Where the named counts of `date_field_widths`
come to less than the parsed cells -- a width each below the line was
left out -- the named words keep exactly their published counts and the
other `parsed - named` ranks wear joint words the census does not name,
in the order `padded`, `unpadded`, `first-padded`, `second-padded`:
WHOLE DAYS AT A TIME, from the ranks that show both fields; each word
on at most the line less one ranks and on fewer than the largest named
count. The days that can be taken hold no more of those ranks than a
word may or the remainder does, and of the days holding one number of
ranks only the first `remainder // size` are walked, fewest ranks first
and the earlier day first among equals. FIRST THE WALK THAT NEVER STEPS
BACK, as landing T1 built it: each of those days, in that order, taken
while the remainder still holds it and put in the first word with room,
or left out where none has room, until the days taken hold exactly the
remainder. WHERE IT FALLS SHORT, THE SEARCH (the T1 review's item 6: on
days of 4, 6 and 7 ranks under a remainder of 13 the walk took 4 and 6,
could not take 7, and gave up, though 6 and 7 hold 13): the same days
MOST RANKS FIRST, the earlier day first among equals, depth first, each
put in the first word, then the next, then left out, and the first way
whose days hold exactly the remainder is taken. Most ranks first because
it fills the words with the days that fit them least and leaves the
small days to make up what is left: walked fewest ranks first, as the
fix stream's first round walked it, a census of one day each of 1 to 99
ranks under 297 looked at 2.8 million states, where most ranks first
takes 99. The search does not walk a remainder past what the words hold
together, a day from which the days left cannot make up what is left of
the remainder, their words aside, or a day reached with the loads of
one that failed before, in some order -- none of those can hold an
assignment -- and it ENTERS AT MOST 100,000 STATES, a state being a day
reached that none of those turned back; past that it places nothing.
Only a census built to defeat it reaches the bound: unbounded, days of
even sizes under an odd remainder at a floor of 100 walked every state
there is for 99 seconds, and on 3,000 twin-like censuses at floors 11
to 200 the search decided every one the first walk left to it within
1,190 states. Where the search finds no set of days -- none exists, or
the bound was reached -- no rank moves and the report says synthtwin
found none (`date_field_widths`): case (b), a remainder outnumbering
the named word's visible cells, stays carried.

**The joint words are joint on purpose, and that is a rule and not a
convenience.** On a column half written `%m/%d/%Y` and half `m/d/yyyy`
not one real cell mixes the two, so two independent censuses would have
written about half the eligible cells `03/5/2024` — a style no row of
that table uses. The same holds of a hand-entered column mixing
`17-MAR-2024` with `17 Mar 2024`, which carries its case and its mark
together. A rank that cannot show a convention — a day above the ninth,
a cell carrying no zulu marker — takes the column's commonest form and
is counted against no census.

**Each census is spent over its own classes of rank, and a named form
keeps its least (plans P4-D131 to P4-D133).** No census of written forms
carries a pool (contract D17 to D20), so what each owes is its named
counts and nothing else.

1. WIDTHS. A rank whose two numeric fields are both below ten takes a
   joint word; one whose FIRST field alone is, a first-field word,
   written with that field padded or not; one whose SECOND alone is, a
   second-field word likewise -- first and second in the member's own
   field order, and on a textual member the day is its one field. A
   class the census counts no word for takes the joint words' padding of
   that field, summed (`padded` and `first-padded` pad the first field),
   and one with none of those either takes that field padded. A rank
   whose two fields both show, where the census counts no joint word,
   takes the joint word built field by field from the convention the
   commonest named one-field word of that field does NOT wear, a field
   the census names no one-field word for being padded: a census naming a
   one-field word says that no cell of its table showing both fields
   wore that word's convention in that field, because
   `folded_width_tally` would have joined the named count to such a
   cell's joint word and the census would name the joint word instead
   (plan P4-D294, amended by the repair pass of the carried date items of
   2026-09-18). A rank that shows no width takes the commonest joint
   word, or the joint word the commonest first-field and second-field
   words make.
2. NAMES. A rank whose month is May takes the census's `either` words; a
   rank of any other month the words that name a length. A class the
   census counts no word for takes the other class's words with the
   length set aside: `either` read as `abbreviated`, a named length read
   as `either`.
3. MARKERS AND ZULU CASES are spent over every quarter rank and over the
   ranks carrying `Z`.
4. THE RESERVATION. Every class is spent by the smooth rotation; where
   that leaves a named form fewer places than the smaller of its count
   and the floor (never below two), and those leasts come to no more
   than the class's places, the leasts are reserved first, the places
   left are shared by the rotation over what each form is owed beyond
   its least (over the leasts where nobody is owed more), and the
   finished counts are spread by the rotation once more. A twin's column
   has its own number of cells in each class, and a proportional share
   of a smaller class fell under the floor: at a smallest group size of
   fifty, `second-padded: 97` came back under it and the twin missed an
   obligation the real table met.

*Amended by the review of 158c811.* This section spent a withheld pool
evenly over the forms a census left unnamed, spent the joint width words
over every rank showing a width and `padded`/`unpadded` over every rank
showing one field, gave a rank of May the commonest style, and reserved
nothing.

**The date half, per member:**

| `format` | the cell's date half | example |
|---|---|---|
| `iso-date`, `iso-datetime`, `iso-mixed` | `YYYY-MM-DD` | `2024-03-17` |
| `slashed-iso-date`, `slashed-iso-datetime` | `YYYY/MM/DD`, both fields padded | `2024/03/17` |
| `compact-date` | `YYYYMMDD` | `20240317` |
| `month-first-date`, `month-first-datetime` | month, day, four-figure year, slashed, each field at its allocated width | `03/17/2024`, `3/17/2024` |
| `day-first-date`, `day-first-datetime` | day, month, four-figure year, slashed, at its allocated width | `17/03/2024` |
| `two-digit-month-first-date` | month, day, `YY`, slashed, at its allocated width | `03/17/24` |
| `two-digit-day-first-date` | day, month, `YY`, slashed, at its allocated width | `17/03/24` |
| `dotted-month-first-date`, `dotted-day-first-date` | dotted, both fields PADDED (contract C6-22) | `17.03.2024` |
| `dotted-two-digit-month-first-date`, `dotted-two-digit-day-first-date` | dotted, both fields padded, `YY` | `17.03.24` |
| `textual-day-first-date` | day at its allocated width, the month NAME in its allocated case and length, four-figure year, on the allocated mark | `17-MAR-2024`, `7 September 2024` |
| `textual-month-first-date` | the month NAME, the day at its allocated width with the allocated comma, four-figure year, on the allocated mark | `Mar 17, 2024`, `Mar 17 2024` |
| `iso-month` | `YYYY-MM` | `2024-03` |
| `year-quarter` | `YYYY-` then `Q` or `q` as allocated, then the quarter | `2024-Q1`, `2024-q1` |

**A LAYOUT IS WRITTEN WHOLE, FIELD BY FIELD** (landing R2a, plan
P4-D383). A column read under a layout (contract LY1) has every cell
written through that layout by `parsing.written_layout_date`, the one
inverse of the layout reader, and nothing is appended after it: the
year in four figures, or in two where the field is `{YY}` or one of
the windows of G7.3e; `{MM}`, `{DD}`, `{HH}`, `{MI}` and `{SS}` in two
figures and `{_D}` padded with a space; a flexible `{M}` or `{D}`
padded or not as the width word its rank was allocated says, the
census of contract LY5 spent over the layout's flexible fields in
their own order -- one field takes `padded` or `unpadded`, two the
slashed pair's joint words; a month or weekday name in its field's
own set and case, the weekday the date's own; `{F}` as zeros at
`subsecond_digits`; and the offset the rank wears in its field's own
spelling, at the place the layout puts it -- `+0100` under `{+HHMM}`,
`-05` under `{+HH}`, the word itself under `{Z}`, `{UTC}` or `{GMT}`.
THE CLOCK HALF (landing R2b): `{H}` writes the hour in one figure below
ten and `{_H}` pads it with a space; `{hh}`, `{h}` and `{_h}` write the
same three widths on the 12-hour dial, the hour less twelve after noon
and 12 at the top of the dial, never 0; a marker field -- `{AM}`, `{am}`,
`{A.M.}`, `{a.m.}` -- writes its morning word before noon and its
afternoon word from noon on, after the gap the layout writes: none, a
space, or the narrow no-break space U+202F. A dial field with no marker
is T1's declared face (`--twelve-hour`), written on the dial it shows as
the stamps are.
A rank allocated `(none)` under an offset some cells omit
(`{+HHMM?}`) writes no offset and none of the marks before it; a field
that must write one and is handed none writes the shared clock's,
`+00:00` in its spelling. The ranks, the tails, the precision and the
allocation of the offsets are every member's.

**THE DAY OF THE YEAR AND THE PARTIAL FORMS** (landing R2c, plan
P4-D383). `{DDD}`, the ask-first field of a column the person said holds
dates (contract S8f), is the day of the year in three figures, `001` to
`366`. A column some of whose cells were read only in part publishes each
PARTIAL FORM it wore in `resolution_mix` beside the layout's own count
(contract LY6, LY7): the layout cut after a field -- `{YYYY}-{MM}`,
`{YYYY}`, HL7's twelve figures under its fourteen -- or its day, or its
day and month, written as an unknown marker (`{UN} {MON} {YYYY}`,
`{UN} {UNK} {YYYY}`). Those cells stand inside `n_unparsed` and reach no
other fact, so the full ranks are drawn as every member's are, and the
partial cells are written after them and before the stand-ins, each a
FULL RANK WRITTEN SHORT: the forms are taken in the order of their names,
and the k-th of the n partial cells takes the full rank at k times the
count of full ranks over n, rounded down, reads that rank's written cell
back under the layout -- the next rank that reads where one does not --
and writes its instant under the form furthest behind its share (its
count times k + 1, less the cells it has taken times n), the first form
on a tie: the fields the form keeps from the instant, a flexible field in
as few figures as it takes, and each marker as itself. Where no full rank
reads back there are no partial cells, and the stand-ins take every
unread cell. No word is drawn. A form written as figures alone is a
number, so G7.9b's debt counts only the stand-ins that are not.

*Amended by the Codex review of landing R2c (items 3 and 4).* A partial
cell that is one of the column's absent spellings -- `2024-03` declared
missing beside published partial months -- and, where G11's
all-different obligation binds the column (G7.3's amendment of that
review), one the column already holds, a full rank's cell or an earlier
partial cell, is not written there: the units of its form's precision --
years, months, days, hours, minutes or seconds -- are walked outward from
its own, the earlier first at each distance, inside the layout's year
band of 1800 to 2299, and the first unit that is neither is written. So
each form keeps its published count. Where no unit is left there are no
partial cells, and the stand-ins take every unread cell. Measured on the
reviewed head: the absent month came back on 74, 65 and 63 present cells
at three seeds, and 80 different years as one, `2024`, written 80 times.
The walk says which unit is written, not how it is found: a unit found
taken or absent stays so for the rest of the column, so it may be
crossed in one hop (the verification of that repair, open item 2; one
unit at a time asked 500,359 times for 1,000 partial days of a
20,000-row column of different HL7 stamps).

*Amended by the fifth push's critic (MAJOR 4).* The walk keeps first
inside the span of the full ranks that read back, from the unit of the
first instant they write to the unit of the last -- the span the
published tails set, the cell's own unit always inside it. Where no unit there is free, the nearest free
unit below the span is written, the walk going down toward 1800, and
only where none is, the nearest above it. Measured on 45191fa: 120 ISO
dates from 2024-01-01 beside 80 different years 1900 to 1979 came back
with years 1984 to 2063, 39 of them after the column's last date, and
validate raised nothing; they are now 1945 to 2024. The source's own
partial years are published nowhere, so the twin cannot put them where
the source had them.

A month NAME is built by `month_spelling`, the one inverse of the
reader's own `month_of_name`, so a producer counting names and a
generator writing them cannot spell one month two ways — as
`clock_spelling` is the one inverse of `clock_ordinal`. The whole date
half is `written_date`, the one inverse of `parse_datetime`, and the
generator reaches it through `_cell_of_ordinal` and nowhere else.

**What the reversal does NOT change.** The figures after a second are
still zeros: the description says how MANY the finest cell carried and
nothing about their values, so any other figure would be a made-up fact.
The precision, the mark and the offset state are decision 5's own gains
and are untouched. And the spellings no member reads still fall to free
text, `08APR2024` among them; the reversal is about writing what was
read, not about reading more. Two this paragraph once named beside it
are read since landing T1, on a slashed stamp: a 12-hour clock
(`3/17/2023 9:30 PM`) and Excel's unpadded hour (`3/17/2023 9:30`),
whose clock half the stamp members read in the forty forms of the
`time_of_day` role (contract C6-10a, D12a) and the twin writes in its
style (the T1 paragraph above). The `iso-datetime` member still reads
its clock with two figures a field on the 24-hour clock (the contract's
`iso-datetime` row), so that MEMBER reads no 12-hour clock and no
one-figure hour after an ISO date (the T1 review's item 11). Such a
column falls to the layout member of G7.5 (landing R2b, plan P4-D383),
which reads `2024-03-17 9:30` under `{YYYY}-{MM}-{DD} {H}:{MI}` and
`2024-03-17 09:30 PM` under `{YYYY}-{MM}-{DD} {hh}:{MI} {AM}`, and writes
each cell back in that layout (the Codex review of landing R2b, item 3).

Then the clock half, exactly:

| `resolution` | `time_precision` | cell text |
|---|---|---|
| `quarter` | `quarter` | `YYYY-Qn` |
| `month` | `month` | `YYYY-MM` |
| `date` | `date` | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `datetime` | `minute` | `YYYY-MM-DD` + mark + `HH:MM` |
| `datetime` | `second` | `YYYY-MM-DD` + mark + `HH:MM:SS` |
| `datetime` | `subsecond` | `YYYY-MM-DD` + mark + `HH:MM:SS.` + `subsecond_digits` digits |

then the offset suffix, when one was allocated: `Z`, or `+HH:MM`, or
`-HH:MM`, exactly as the offset key spells it.

**Read the table through the member.** Its texts are the ISO
spellings: on every other member `YYYY-MM-DD` stands for the member's
own date half (the table above), and on a slashed stamp `HH:MM` and
`HH:MM:SS` stand for the clock its one `datetime_separators` word
names (the T1 paragraph above): the two-figure 24-hour clock where
that word is `space` or pooled, and otherwise the hour at its width
and on its face (landing T1, contract C6-10a, D12a; the T1 review's
item 11).

**The table is COMPLETE, and that is now true of the contract as well**
(P2-C1-F6). Revision 1 of the profile contract permitted a sixth pair —
`resolution: datetime` with `time_precision: date` — for which no cell
text exists: written `YYYY-MM-DD` the column re-profiles with
`resolution: date`, and written with seconds it re-profiles with
`time_precision: second`, and both fields are EXACT-OBSERVABLE. The
producer cannot make that pair, because a value carrying no time of day
does not read as a date AND time at all, so the contract's invariant D6
now refuses it and its loader enforces that. Every pair a description
can carry has a row above.

**An offset is written only where `resolution` is `datetime`** (contract
invariant D9). A whole date, a month and a quarter have no time of day
for an offset to move, and a cell written `2024-03-15+02:00` reads back
as no date at all.

**THE TWO ENDPOINT CELLS ARE BUILT FROM THE PUBLISHED ENDPOINT'S OWN
FIELDS, NOT FROM ITS ORDINAL** (review item P2-C2-F5). G7.3 pins ranks
`0` and `P - 1` to `earliest` and `latest` "used exactly as published",
and this paragraph is what makes that sentence literal. For the two
SPAN resolutions the two routes cannot differ at all: a month and a
quarter ARE their canonical text, so the fields route and the ordinal
route write the same characters, and the pin is literal either way. The ordinal
space of G7.1 round-trips every instant a whole-second count can hold,
and there is one a real reader can still hand a description that it
cannot: the last second of a leap minute, `SS` of `60`, which the
profile contract's canonical form admits at 6.6.2 because the shipped
reader accepts one. *Stage 3 (plan P4-D328): the values this rule is stated over are the two
TAIL BOUNDARIES and the values a few-valued tail lists, which are the
published values of a date column now; no end is published.* Read the
published moment as its four fields —
the date, `HH`, `MM` and `SS` — and build the cell as:

1. `resolution` `date`, `month` or `quarter`: the published text itself, which is
   already the cell text the table above asks for.
2. `resolution` `datetime`: take the published date with `HH:MM` and
   `SS` of `00`, move THAT to the clock G7.4 allocates for this cell —
   unchanged where `datetimes_read_at` is `local`, shifted by
   `offset_in_seconds` where it is `utc` — and then write the published
   `SS` back into the seconds field unchanged. Every offset is a whole
   number of minutes (contract 6.6.2 bounds the minute field), so the
   move never touches the seconds field and a `60` survives it.

The result is then cut to the recorded `time_precision` by the table
above, and the offset suffix follows as usual. The cut can drop no
published detail: `minute` is the only precision with no seconds field,
and the contract's D10 admits it only where every published moment's
`SS` is `00`. For every instant whose `SS` is `00` through `59` this produces
exactly the same bytes the ordinal route produces, which is why it moved
no case of G14.3's first nine when it was written; for `SS` of `60` it
produces the endpoint the description published, and G14.3's
`leap_second_endpoint` case freezes those bytes beside a committed
mutant that puts the ordinal route back.

**Both tail boundaries are therefore EXACT-OBSERVABLE, with no
leap-second exception**, which is what the ratified plan requires in its
own words —
both tail boundaries EXACT-OBSERVABLE in the representation owner
decision 5 fixes (`docs/plans/phase-2-generator.md` revision 5, P2-D6,
the datetime paragraph), the obligation stage 3 moved from the two ends
to the two boundaries without lowering it — and what the profile
contract's 9.6 now states in the same words. An earlier
revision of this section instead declared the endpoint REPORT-ONLY
because the ordinal space has no room for the value. That was a true
statement about the ordinal space used to lower a bar the owner set;
the bar is restored and the ordinal space is no longer the endpoints'
route.

**The rule above has no case that declines** (review items P2-C3-F2 and
P2-C4-F1). Step 2 writes the published `SS` back on BOTH clocks, at
every instant the canonical form can spell. An earlier revision of this
paragraph named two descriptions on which the endpoint would instead be
met as far as it could be, recounted and named — a `time_precision` of
`minute` whose endpoint carries seconds, and an `SS` of `60` while
`datetimes_read_at` is `utc` — and an implementation followed it,
sending the second of those back through the ordinal space. The revision
that withdrew those two named a third in the paragraph below: a
shared-clock endpoint whose own offset moves its cell off the end of the
calendar. Each was an exception written beside a sentence that says
there is none, and the previous paragraph's own words apply to all
three: a true statement about what a cell can show, used to lower a bar
the owner set. The first two pairs are refused by the profile contract's
**D10**, on the same terms as its D6 refusal of the
`date`-beside-`datetime` pair, and its **D11** ties
`date_percentiles.min` and `.max` to the tail rule -- both are `null`,
and every published rung stands between the two boundaries. The third
pair no longer exists to refuse: stage 3 publishes no end and no end's
offset, and the calendar's edge is G7.3e's obligation on every rank of a
tail, which is where the cell it was about is now derived. No pair
reaches a generator, so this method needs no rule for them, and it
states none.

**The tails are still checked on the written cells, not assumed from
the rule.** After the cells are built, each is
read back with the shipped date reader, put on the clock
`datetimes_read_at` names and counted in the published `tail_unit`: a
cell must stand on each published boundary, and exactly `rows` cells
must lie strictly beyond it. Silence there was the defect: a fact the loader accepted
was quietly changed on output. The check is not a formality now that D10
and D11 stand, and it is not vacuous either: it fails on any
implementation that stops writing the ends from their own fields, which
is the regression this whole section exists to prevent, and a conforming
repository owes a case that puts that regression in and watches the
check catch it. What it is NOT is a route by which a
description gets a lesser tail. Every description this contract's loader
accepts has tails this method writes exactly; a disagreement here is a
defect in the implementation, and the run says so in as many words
rather than passing it off as an outcome the description asked for.

- **The mark between the day and the clock is the one allocated from
  `datetime_separators`** (stage 2, 2026-09-14, plan P4-D39). The ruling
  that stood here — `T` on every `datetime` cell, because the parser
  accepts `T`, `t` and a space and one choice had to be made for the
  bytes to be fixed — fixed the bytes at the cost of the source's own
  spelling: a stamp written with a space came back with a `T`, so code
  splitting on the space worked on every twin row and failed on every
  row of the real table. The bytes stay a fixed function of the
  description:

  1. Take the names of `datetime_separators` other than `(withheld)`,
     sorted: `lower_t`, `space`, `upper_t`, each weighted by its count.
     Where none is named and nothing is pooled, every cell is written
     with `T` and the steps below do not run.
  2. A `(withheld)` pool is split EVENLY over the PERMITTED marks the
     census leaves unnamed (landing 2b.3) — the three names, or `space`
     alone on a `month-first-datetime`, `day-first-datetime` or
     `slashed-iso-datetime` column — each taking the pool divided by
     their number, and the remainder one each in the order `upper_t`,
     `space`, `lower_t`; a mark given nothing is left out. Where no
     permitted mark is unnamed, the pool is not split. **Amended by plan
     P4-D220 and restored by plan P4-D222 (stage 2 closed by the owner
     rulings of 2026-09-17).** Contract D12 admits a pool only as the
     whole census and only over values a pool names no one in -- fewer
     than the line, or no more than two marks hold below it -- so each
     third of it is below the line and the twin described again pools the
     same count. Plan P4-D220 gave each rarer mark one value and the
     commonest the rest, which on a pool of thirty at a floor of twenty
     wrote twenty-eight `T` and the twin described again named them;
     writing the whole pool with one mark, the rule landing 2b.3 replaced,
     erased the spellings the pool stood for.
  3. The ranks this allocation covers are the ones that write a clock:
     on an `iso-mixed` column whose `all_at_midnight` is `true`, the
     ranks the form census gives `iso-date` write none and take no mark.
     Those ranks less the weights so far — the whole-date cells of any
     other `iso-mixed` column — are added to the commonest named count,
     the first name in sorted order winning a tie, or where nothing is
     named to `upper_t`, or to `space` on a slashed stamp.
  4. Every mark starts with a credit of zero. For the covered ranks in
     order, every mark's credit grows by its weight, the rank takes the
     mark with the most credit, the first in sorted order winning a tie,
     and that mark's credit falls by the weights' total. `upper_t`
     writes `T`, `space` a space, `lower_t` a `t`.

  The walk draws no word, and it spreads each mark across the date
  range, so the twin invents no link between a moment's date and its
  spelling. The published instants stay in the contract's canonical
  form, space-separated, whatever mark the cells carry.

  A `(withheld)` pool is not a deviation: described again at the same
  floor the twin pools the same count (landing 2b.3).

- **A column read jointly whose every value stands at midnight writes
  its whole dates as whole dates** (landing 2b.3, narrowing owner
  decision 4 and residual R-P4-12). Such a column is generated in whole
  days, so a bare date spells every rank exactly. Its `resolution_mix`
  is spent over the ranks by the smooth rotation of step 4 over the two
  forms, `iso-date` before `iso-datetime` on a tie, after the ranks whose
  instant the published tail fixes are settled in rank order: rank `0`
  and rank `P - 1` with their published offsets and, on a column the
  move onto a midnight below reaches, each rung rank and each rank
  standing between two pinned ranks of one instant, with every offset
  that instant stands at midnight under. A settled rank none of whose
  offsets is `(none)` or `(withheld)` is a moment; on the `utc` clock a
  settled rank that may carry no offset is a bare date while `iso-date`
  has a count left; each takes one from its form's count (repair pass
  of landing 2b.3: bare dates beside `T00:00:00+02:00` moments publish
  rungs at 22:00, rung ranks the rotation made bare dates were written
  22 hours early, and every twin of that shape missed). A rank given
  `iso-date` is written `YYYY-MM-DD`, with no mark, clock or offset. No
  other column writes a bare date.

- **A column counted in seconds that publishes `n_at_midnight` above
  nought has that many values moved onto a midnight** (landing 2b.3):
  one partly at midnight on either clock, or one wholly at local
  values at midnight on the `utc` clock. After G7.3's instants exist:

  1. The ranks the published tail pins never move: rank `0`, rank
     `P - 1`, and each interior rung's rank `floor((P - 1) * c / 100)`,
     which takes its published rung (the first rung wins a shared rank).
     Every other rank interpolated past a pinned value below or above it
     is brought back to that value.
