  2. A pinned rank, or one standing between two pinned ranks of one
     value, whose cell is written at midnight counts toward
     `n_at_midnight`; midnight is asked of the WRITTEN cell, on the
     rank's own wall clock and cut to the column's precision.
  3. What is still owed is spread over the other ranks: each adds the
     count owed to a credit, and a rank is chosen where the credit
     reaches the number of those ranks, which is then taken back. On the
     dial's half day (G7.3b step 10) the other ranks are the body's
     alone: a tail rank stands there from one unit past midnight, never
     at a written midnight, so one chosen was taken back off midnight by
     G7.3g step 5 and the count left a cell short (landing 3b.2-H, plan
     P4-D371: a weekday clinic written `h:mm` on the dial, its noon slots
     reading 12:00, published 21 cells at midnight and its twins wrote 20
     at a floor of 11, every seed).
  4. A chosen rank moves to the local midnight nearest its instant, the
     earlier on a tie, brought inside the pinned values either side; a
     rank with no local midnight inside them is left. An unchosen rank
     written at midnight moves one precision step later, or earlier where
     later would pass its upper bound.
  5. A second pass over the unchosen ranks, in rank order, moves as many
     more as are still owed, by step 4.

  The set of step 1 is stated once in the implementation, so a change to
  what the tail publishes changes that set and not the construction. A
  count the two passes cannot reach is a deviation of `n_at_midnight`.

- **A column publishing no count of values at midnight is moved
  nowhere** (landing 2b.6). The repair pass of landing 2b.3 moved an
  accidental value at midnight off a column publishing `n_at_midnight`
  of nought, and the integration repair moved each dense run of such
  ranks out together; both are WITHDRAWN, because the nought they served
  is withdrawn. A nought a reader can tell from a suppressed count of
  one is that count: 400 moments a day apart at noon, and the same 400
  with a single row moved to midnight, published `0` and `1` and were
  otherwise identical documents. So the field is absent on both, the
  construction owes such a column nothing, and its twin may hold a value
  at midnight that the real column did not — a fidelity cost named here
  rather than paid in silence, and the one clause 3 of the owner's twin
  definition requires.

  The two endpoint cells carry the marks of ranks `0` and `P - 1`, like
  any other rank.

  **WITH ONE EXCEPTION, AND IT KEEPS AN EXACT FACT RATHER THAN
  RELAXING ONE** (review item P4-DATE-F2). Where the cell this rule
  produces is one of the spellings the column publishes among its
  absent cells — the keys of any column's `missing_by_source`, since a
  declaration reaches the whole table — another mark is offered, in
  order: each mark the census names, in sorted order, then the other
  common form, a space for `T` or `t` and `T` for a space; since
  landing 2b.3 the marks offered first are every mark step 2 writes,
  the pooled ones included. The first whose spelling is not absent is
  written (the stage 2 audit, 2026-09-14). A spelling a column's own
  calendar placeholder or stand-in pass judged absent is not a
  declaration and is not offered to other columns (landing 2b.3).
  **WHICH SPELLINGS THOSE ARE IS READ OUT OF THE DESCRIPTION** (repair
  pass of landing 2b.6): each decision published in `sentinel_verdicts`
  names the spellings its own pass took out (contract V5), and a key no
  decision names was made absent by something that reaches the whole
  table. The version this replaces counted — the keys denoting the
  judged candidate, with the column's pooled hole spellings added,
  against the verdict's `n_occurrences` — and a count cannot separate
  two keys writing ONE candidate day: twenty judged
  `1900-01-01 00:00:00` beside thirty `1900-01-01T00:00:00` a person
  declared put 50 cells against a verdict of 20, so the judged key was
  offered to every column and a second column's ordinary values were
  read as absent, which made the REAL table miss thirteen obligations
  of its own description. Any two of them spell the same instant at the same
  precision on the same clock, so nothing published moves; what moves is whether
  the twin's OWN description still counts the cell. A real column can
  hold a present cell at midnight written `2024-01-01` and, beside it,
  cells a declaration made absent as `2024-01-01T00:00:00`; the twin
  writes every parsed cell at the finest precision, reaches the second
  spelling, and hands back a cell its own reader calls absent — so
  `n_present` falls and, where the cell was an endpoint, an
  EXACT-OBSERVABLE end walks out of the twin over a separator nobody
  chose. The exception is asked ONLY at that collision, so no other
  cell and no frozen vector moves. Where EVERY offer is absent too, an
  interior rank of a column counted in whole units -- dates, months,
  quarters, and a column whose every moment stands at midnight -- is
  stepped to the nearest unit whose spelling is not absent, earlier
  before later, first inside its own G12.4 window and then inside
  `[earliest, latest]` (stage 2 confirmation review, 2026-09-15: a day
  declared absent in all three of its spellings otherwise received eight
  values, which read back as absent cells). On an eligible column
  (layer L0) both ranges are cut to the rank's L0 piece, and where no
  unit of the piece qualifies the allocated form stands, so the step
  never carries a cell across a band edge (G7.3l). A rank inside its window
  stays inside every rung's bound, because the window never falls below
  the unit before the rank's own. Only where no unit qualifies, or on a
  column written to the second, does the allocated form stand, G12's
  endpoint entry name a lost end, and the report name every value left
  in an absent spelling as a deviation of `n_present`: this rule
  declines to invent a spelling the description does not make possible.

  **And the census is given back** (stage 2 review, 2026-09-14; the
  stage 2 audit, 2026-09-14). Each cell whose mark that exception
  changed hands the mark it owed to the first other rank, in rank
  order, that was allocated the mark the changed cell now wears, still
  wears it, was neither changed nor given a mark before, and whose new
  spelling is not absent. A repeated spelling is allowed, but no change
  may leave the column one spelling fewer, nor one value fewer once
  upper and lower case are ignored: a rank whose spelling is the last
  copy of its kind, literally or folded, is passed over while the
  spelling it would take is already written (stage 2 closure review:
  five cells of three spellings came back as two values; stage 2
  confirmation review: a `t` given to the last copy of a day beside that
  day's `T` folded ten cells of three values into two, which is binary). The walk is linear: each
  pair of marks keeps its own place in its list of ranks.
  The finished marks are then counted against the allocation, and a
  shortfall no rank could take is a deviation of `datetime_separators`.
  A spelling is matched as absent whatever the case of its letters, as
  the reader matches it.

  **A column of moments whose absent cells were pooled** below the
  group size (`missing_by_class` `(withheld)` above zero), in a table
  that declared missing values, carries a REMARK in the report (the
  stage 2 audit, 2026-09-14; a remark since the closure review, which
  measured it filed as a failed fact beside an ordinary pooled blank):
  those spellings are not published, so the twin cannot avoid one, and
  a value written in it reads back as absent.
- **The fractional digits are zeros.** The profile publishes how MANY
  subsecond digits the finest cell carried and nothing about their
  values — the parser reads and discards the fraction — so any other
  digits would be an invented fact, and drawing them would cost words
  for a quantity no published fact constrains.
- **Every parsed cell is written at the same precision**, which is the
  finest the column recorded. That is what makes `time_precision`
  EXACT-OBSERVABLE: it is the finest precision any value writes, so at
  least one value must write it, and writing them all at that precision
  is the rule that needs no further fact. On an `all_at_midnight` column
  every cell is its day with a midnight clock at that precision —
  `00:00`, `00:00:00`, or `00:00:00.` and `subsecond_digits` zeros —
  carrying its allocated mark (stage 2, 2026-09-14), and the report
  recounts the midnight cells it wrote and names any that are not.
- `format` is EXACT-OBSERVABLE and IS reproduced (landing 2b.6, plan
  P4-D61): the cell is written through the member that read the real
  column, so a month-first source column yields month-first twin dates
  and re-profiles as `month-first-date`. It was not reproduced at all
  under owner decision 5 (P2-R4-F3), when such a column yielded ISO
  twin dates and
  a person's own parsing call needed a different format argument on the
  twin than on their table, so the field could not be reproduced at
  all; the owner reversed that decision and residual R-P2-7 is retired
  with it. The one column whose member its
  own twin cannot show is an `iso-mixed` column not wholly at midnight,
  which is written wholly as moments (R-P4-12).

### G7.9 Reaching a distinct count a mark census absorbed out of reach

**The defect this closes** (plan P4-D245, ledger K-2B-51; the owner on
2026-09-21, 'I think we need to fix'). Ruling 6 of the owner's rulings
of 2026-09-17 counts a written spelling below the census line into the
COMMONEST spelling, and that ruling stands: it is what keeps a census
from naming a handful of rows. So a column of 125 moments at midnight
on two days, 120 of them written with a space between day and clock and
5 with a `T`, publishes `datetime_separators` of `{"space": 125}` at a
floor of eleven — beside `n_distinct_folded` of THREE, because the
column really did hold three different spellings.

A construction that reads that census as an instruction about the CELLS
writes 125 spaces over two days. That is two different values where the
description publishes three, and a column of two values is read back as
BINARY (the taxonomy decides the kind on the count of values before it
asks whether they are dates). `synthtwin validate` then reported the
twin missing `axes.role`, `axes.statistical_type` and `midnight.count`
while the REAL table missed none — the tool telling the person their
twin was wrong for doing exactly what the description said.

**The rule.** After the marks are allocated (G7.5 step 2) and the
absent-spelling repair has run, the parsed cells are counted by folded
spelling. Where a column of dates holds FEWER folded spellings than
`n_distinct_folded` publishes, the construction may spend ranks on the
permitted marks (contract D12) the census leaves UNNAMED, in the order
`upper_t`, `space`, `lower_t`:

1. The number of ranks spent is bounded by the SHORTFALL the
   description itself publishes — `n_distinct_folded` less the folded
   spellings the cells hold AND less the `n_unparsed` stand-ins still
   to be written — and by a budget of `census_floor(floor)` less one
   ranks in all, whichever binds first. The stand-ins are counted
   though this pass never sees them: the datetime content builder
   appends exactly `n_unparsed` of them (G7.2, G10.4) after this pass
   runs, each a spelling no other cell of the
   column holds, so the finished column holds that many folded
   spellings more than the cells in hand. Counting only the cells in
   hand made the shortfall too large by exactly that many and the pass
   OVERSHOT — measured on 303 midnight moments over two days beside two
   cells no date reader accepts, where the twin wrote six different
   values against a published five, so `synthtwin validate` named
   `distinct.n_distinct` and `distinct.n_distinct_folded` on a column
   that had named nothing before this pass existed (the review of
   2026-09-21, item 1).
2. A rank is spent when its cell is at least eleven characters long, it
   wears the commonest NAMED mark, its respelling is not a spelling the
   table declares absent, its respelling is a folded spelling the cells
   do not already hold, its own folded spelling is still worn by
   another rank, and it is NEITHER OF THE TWO END RANKS, which are
   written as the description publishes `earliest` and `latest`. So no
   spend ever leaves the column one spelling fewer, none buys a
   spelling twice, and neither published end is respelled.

   **AND THE MARK IT IS TAKEN FROM IS LEFT AT OR ABOVE
   `census_floor(floor)`** (*added by the dates pass of the stage-3
   review, item 6*). The budget of item 1 keeps the mark this pass
   INVENTS below the census line, so that describing the twin counts it
   back into the commonest one and publishes the census exactly as it
   stands -- and that absorption only happens while the commonest one is
   itself still a count the census may print. On a SPARSE column it need
   not be: 22 dates in 2,000 rows, alternating a `T` separator and a
   bare date, publish `{"upper_t": 11}` at a floor of eleven, which is
   exactly the line. Seed 4 spent one of those eleven, leaving ten `T`
   beside one space; no count of that census then reached the line, so
   describing the twin pooled the whole census under `(withheld)` and
   `synthtwin validate` named `marks.upper_t` and `marks.unnamed` on a
   twin whose own generation reported nothing. The spend stops while the
   count it would take from is at the line.
3. The pass RUNS ON THE TWO ISO DATETIME MEMBERS ALONE — `iso-datetime`
   and `iso-mixed`, the members contract D12 permits all three marks —
   and is skipped on every other member, and on a census holding a
   withheld pool, which G7.5 already splits over every permitted mark.
   THE SKIP IS BY MEMBER AND NOT BY CHARACTER. A slashed stamp writes
   its date in fields of no fixed width, so its mark sits at no fixed
   index: `3/03/2020 13:37` carries it at index nine and
   `2024/06/20 13:37` — the frozen `slashed_pool` case — at index TEN,
   where it is the MARK and not a digit. The date members carry no mark
   at all. Until the independence repair of 2026-09-21 this item read
   'a member whose eleventh character is a digit of the date rather
   than the mark', which that frozen cell contradicts; a second
   implementer reading it literally would not skip
   `slashed-iso-datetime`. No byte moved when the reason was corrected,
   because D12 permits a slashed stamp the SPACE ALONE, so a census
   naming anything leaves it no mark unnamed to buy in any case —
   which is why the skip could be misstated for a landing without a
   committed file saying so.

**STATED IN FULL, because the three clauses above do not decide the
pass.** They say which ranks MAY be spent and how many; they leave four
things a second implementer has to invent, and two conforming programs
that invented them differently would write different bytes. The
independence repair of 2026-09-21 completed the statement rather than
letting the shipped code be the answer, for the reason G2.1's placement
is stated at that width:

4. **Where the mark sits, and what a respelling is.** On the members
   this pass runs on, the cell's eleventh character — index ten,
   counting from nought — is the mark between the day and the clock.
   A rank's respelling is that cell with that ONE character replaced by
   the spare mark and every other character of it untouched, which is
   why a cell shorter than eleven characters is passed over: it carries
   no mark to replace.
5. **Which rank takes a spare mark.** Each spare mark in turn, in the
   order `upper_t`, `space`, `lower_t` stated above, is offered the
   ranks between the two end ranks in rank order, lowest first, and
   each rank that meets every clause of item 2 takes it as offered. When a mark's offer reaches the last of
   those ranks, the next spare mark is offered the same ranks again
   from the lowest. The pass stops the moment the ranks spent reach the
   SMALLER of item 1's two bounds — the published shortfall and the
   budget of `census_floor(floor)` less one — and no further rank is
   offered anything.
6. **The clauses of item 2 are asked of the column as it now stands.**
   A spend changes which folded spellings the cells hold, so the rank
   offered a mark after it is judged against the column that spend
   left: a folded spelling one rank has just bought is a spelling the
   cells already hold, and a rank whose own folded spelling another
   rank has just left is no longer worn by another rank.
7. **The commonest NAMED mark on a tie, and a census that names
   nothing.** Where two names of the census carry the same count, the
   commonest is the first of them in sorted order — the same tie G7.5
   steps 3 and 4 settle the same way, on the same census. Where the
   census names no mark at all, no cell wears the commonest named mark
   and no rank is ever spent, so the pass leaves such a column exactly
   as it found it without being told to skip it.

**Why the budget is one below the line.** The twin is held to its
description by being DESCRIBED AGAIN, and the description of a column
wearing fewer than `census_floor` cells of a mark counts that mark back
into the commonest name by ruling 6 — the same absorption that created
the shortfall. So the published census is met exactly. A spend that
REACHED the line would publish a count the real column's census
withheld, and the twin would miss its own mark census instead: measured
on the shape above, eleven ranks and twelve alike miss `marks.space`
and `marks.unnamed`, while one through ten miss nothing at all.

**Where the spent ranks come from, and why they name no row.** The
count spent is a function of the PUBLISHED numbers alone. The count the
real column held — five, in the shape above — is not published, is not
read and is not reproduced: the twin writes ONE. So the twin carries no
number the description does not already carry, and a reader of the
twin's own description cannot see the mark at all.

**What it does not do.** It buys values; it does not excuse their loss.
A shortfall the budget cannot close leaves the column exactly where
G12.5's published envelope and `_kind_notes`' deviation already put it,
and a twin that holds fewer values than the census can supply is
reported missing its role as before.

**The stand-in term is witnessed one call at a time**, in
`tests/test_oracle_rule_witnesses.py`. The one frozen case that reaches
this rule (`date_absorbed_mark`) publishes `n_unparsed` of nought, so no
committed vectors file parts the stand-in road from the fallback, and
plan P4-D295 routes a new case into an existing file, where it would
move bytes. TWELVE columns with the answers worked by hand instead —
eleven midnight moments over two days, every one written with a space,
asked at shortfalls of nought and one, at budgets of one and two ranks,
on a slashed stamp, on a date member, on a census holding a withheld
pool, on a census naming nothing but the mark the cells do NOT wear, on
a census whose two names tie, and on a table declaring the respelling
of the first day absent — asked of the oracle's
`marks_bought_for_the_shortfall` and of the shipped
`_spellings_short_of_the_count` alike, with seven mutants (the stand-ins
left uncounted, the budget raised to the census line, both END ranks
opened, item 7's tie stated backwards, item 2's commonest NAMED mark
dropped, item 2's declared-absent spelling dropped, item 3's member skip
dropped) each turning that witness red. THE LAST FOUR ARE THIS
DOCUMENT'S OWN DEBT: the repair's skeptic measured sixteen one-clause
mutants of the rewritten function against every frozen case and the
eight rows then standing, and those four moved cells while moving
nothing any file or row could see — item 7's tie worst of all, since
nothing but the shipped code had ever pinned it, which is the one source
an oracle may not be written from. A clause this document states in full
and no row parts is a clause the oracle and the generator may both have
wrong. THE TWO NAMES DIFFER ON PURPOSE:
the oracle's is what it hands back and the shipped one's is the
shortfall it closes, so the pairing a reader checks is not asserted by a
shared name (the independence repair of 2026-09-21, ledger K-2B-42).

**It reasons about the FOLDED count alone**, and on one shape that
leaves the unfolded count further from its published value than it
found it. A census naming both `upper_t` and `lower_t` writes two
spellings of every instant that fold to one, so a column of 125
midnight moments over two days beside five spaces publishes
`n_distinct` and `n_distinct_folded` of three while the construction
already writes four different texts for two folded ones. This pass
sees the folded shortfall of one, spends a rank, and reaches the
published folded count exactly — taking the unfolded count from four to
five. Measured on that column: the twin missed `axes.role`,
`axes.statistical_type` and `midnight.count` before this pass and
misses `distinct.n_distinct` alone after it, three checks traded for
one. Holding the unfolded count instead was measured too — a guard that
spends only where the unfolded count is short as well returns that
column to its three misses and moves no other shape — so the trade is
recorded here rather than taken back. The entry K-2B-51 carries the
same measurement, so its rule is not read as a claim about every column
of dates.

### G7.9b The offsets a column of figure runs owes its count of cells that are not numbers

**The defect this closes** (landing R2a's repair round, item 2; plan
P4-D383). A layout whose cells with no offset are figures -- HL7's
`{YYYY}{MM}{DD}{HH}{MI}{SS}`, with at most a point and a fraction after
the run -- and whose last field is an offset some cells omit
(`{+HHMM?}`) writes a NUMBER on every rank G7.4 gives no offset, and a
cell WEARING an offset is text to every reader of numbers. Where each
offset the real column wore stood on fewer cells than the census line,
contract D3 counts them all into `(none)` (plan P4-D222), every rank is
allocated no offset, and the twin was all numbers -- while the universal
count `n_not_numeric` still published the cells that were not, so it
missed `counts.n_numeric` and `counts.n_not_numeric`, and code that read
the twin's column as numbers stopped on the real table's offsets.

**The pass**, after G7.9 and before the stand-ins are written, on a
column of that layout whose census of offsets pools nothing and names
`(none)` as its commonest count (ties to `(none)`):

1. The DEBT is `n_not_numeric`, less the cells in hand that are not
   numbers, less the `n_unparsed` stand-ins written after the pass,
   each a text. Nothing the real column held and the description does
   not publish is read.
2. The OPEN ranks are those between the two ends -- the ends are
   spellings the description prints -- whose cell is a number that no
   other rank's cell repeats, so a respelled cell replaces one value
   with one and the published counts of different values stand.
3. The OFFSETS on offer are `+00:00`, `+01:00`, ... `+14:00`, in that
   order, each written in the field's own spelling (`+0000` under
   `{+HHMM?}`, `+00` under `{+HH?}`), or the zulu field's own word, the
   one offset it has -- LESS EVERY OFFSET THE CENSUS NAMES (skeptic 2
   of landing R2a, item 1). A cell written at a named offset is counted
   into that offset and read at it, not into `(none)`: 1,000 HL7 stamps,
   300 at `+0000` and 5 at `-0500`, were paid at `+0000`, and the twin
   missed the census on `(none)` and on `+00:00` at every seed, where
   the column had validated as free text before the landing; with
   `+01:00` named, the payments past the first `census_floor - 1`
   landed on it, and one moved a tail's instant. Where nothing is left
   on offer, or the debt is nought or less, nothing is paid and
   nothing past the class of each cell is read.
4. The payments are the fewest of: the debt, the open ranks, the
   number cells less `census_floor`, and `census_floor - 1` times the
   offsets on offer. Payment `k` of `n` goes to the open rank at
   position `k * open // n`, and writes that cell again with the marks
   before the offset field and offset number `k // (census_floor - 1)`
   after them; a payment whose cell would be a spelling the column
   holds absent, or that its field cannot write, is not made.
5. **WHOLE TEXTS, WHERE THE OPEN RANKS FALL SHORT** (the Codex review
   of landing R2a, item 4, and the verification of its repair). The REST
   is the fewest of the debt, the number cells less `census_floor` and
   `census_floor - 1` times the offsets on offer, less the payments step
   4 made. Where it is two or more it is paid with whole texts: a number
   worn by at least two ranks and by fewer than `census_floor`, none of
   them an end, every rank wearing it written again at ONE offset, so
   the column holds as many different texts as before and no text wears
   two spellings. Each offset's ROOM is `census_floor - 1` cells less the
   payments step 4 wrote at it, and the texts on offer are those whose
   ranks number at most the largest room and at most the rest. The step
   AIMS at the largest total of ranks, at most the rest and at most the
   rooms together, that the texts on offer reach, and walks the offsets
   in step 3's order. At each, the texts it MAY TAKE are those not yet
   taken and not barred from it (below); it takes the largest amount, at
   most its room and at most what is left of the aim, that those texts
   reach and that leaves what is then left of the aim both a total the
   texts not yet taken after it still reach -- those barred from it
   among them -- and no more than the rooms of the offsets after it
   hold; it takes none where only none does that, and where not even
   none does, the largest amount at most its room and what is left of
   the aim that the texts it may take reach. An amount's texts are
   counted from the most ranks down, at each size as many as there are,
   at most what is left of the amount, while what is then left stays a
   total the texts of fewer ranks reach; of the `n` texts of one size it
   may take, in the order of their first rank, choice `j` of `k` is the
   text at position `j * n // k`. The walk stops where what is left of
   the aim is under two or the offsets run out. A text taken whose
   respelling at its offset is a spelling the column holds absent, or
   one its field cannot write -- the first such in the walk's order, by
   offset and then from the most ranks down -- is BARRED FROM THAT
   OFFSET alone, and the walk is made again; every other offset may
   still take it. 1,000 cells, 100 stamps ten times each and
   seven of them ending `-0500`, publish 107 different texts and seven
   cells that are not numbers: the twin's texts all repeated, step 4
   found no rank to pay, and seeds 1 and 2 held no offset at all and
   missed both class counts. And with eleven of them wearing an offset,
   step 5 chose offset by offset, each offset taking the most it held,
   and every seed from 0 to 5 wrote ten and missed both class counts: at
   seed 0 step 4 wrote the one text standing alone at `+0000`, a text of
   nine copies filled the nine cells left there, and the one cell over
   fitted no text. The aim and the look ahead write a text of six copies
   at `+0000` and one of four at `+0100` there, and the eleven at every
   seed.
6. **FEWER TEXTS STANDING ALONE, WHERE WHOLE TEXTS THEN WRITE MORE**
   (the verification of the Codex review's repair). Step 4 writes every
   text standing alone it may before step 5 sees the rest, and a rest no
   whole text reaches -- one cell, beside texts of two copies and more --
   was left owed where one text standing alone fewer and a text of two
   would have written it: 5 of 180 twins of repeated stamps. Where steps
   4 and 5 write fewer cells than step 5's bound and step 4 had payments
   to make, the pass is made a second time from the cells as they were
   handed, step 4 making only the largest count of payments, below its
   own, whose sum with the largest total -- at most the bound less that
   count -- that the texts step 5 may take reach is the greatest of any
   such count, and only where that sum passes the cells written; the
   texts step 5 may take are the numbers worn by at least two ranks, by
   fewer than `census_floor` and by no more than the bound, none of them
   an end. Step 5 then writes the rest as above. The second pass is kept
   only where it writes more cells; otherwise the first pass's cells
   stand.

**Why it moves no published fact.** Each offset stands on one cell
fewer than the line and is one the census does not name, so the twin
described again counts each into the commonest named count, `(none)`,
and reads that cell at no offset
(`taxonomy._offsets_as_published`): the census, the clock the column is
read on, every instant and every count of different values come back as
published, and the class count comes back exact. Each offset written is
worked out from the census and the field alone and is not read from the
real column, nor published; it may still be one some real cells wore,
since the census counted those into `(none)` and does not say which they
were -- seven real `+0000` among 1,000 stamps came back as seven made-up
`+0000` at seeds 0 to 2 (the Codex review of landing R2a, item 8).
Measured: HL7 stamps with 1, 7, 10, 11, 12 and 25 of 1,000 cells
wearing an offset, at floors 11 and 36 and seeds 0 to 2, all exit 0 in
`validate`, where 11 and 12 missed both counts before and 1 to 10 read
as stand-ins; and stamps to the minute, whose texts repeat, keep their
count of different values only because a repeated text is never paid
on in part (paid on in part, five and fifteen offsets missed
`distinct.n_distinct`); beside a named offset, `+00:00` with 5 and with
40 rare ones and `+01:00` with 30, every seed at floors 11 and 36 exits
0 since the named offsets left the offer; and by steps 5 and 6, thirty
shapes of repeated stamps -- two to twelve copies of each, one to
fifteen offsets owed, floors 11 and 36, seeds 0 to 2 -- hold both class
counts and the count of different values and exit 0 in `validate` on
168 of 180 twins, where 163 did with step 5 alone and 129 before it.
Codex's column of 100 stamps ten times each, with 11, 13, 14, 17, 20 or
24 of its cells wearing an offset, validates at every seed from 0 to 5,
where nine of those twins fell short while each offset took the most it
held; and on the verification's random shapes in rank order, no text
standing alone, step 5 writes all that any choice of whole texts over
the offsets writes on 1,112 of 1,112, where 232 fell short so. The pass
alone costs 1.1 CPU seconds at 300,000 rows and 3.5 at a million
whether 7 or 140 cells are owed, and a second pass of step 6 0.2 and 0.7
more; respelling every text on offer at every offset step 5 wrote at
cost 20.6 and 68.0 owing 140. Frozen cases `layout_offsets_owed`,
`layout_offsets_owed_repeats` beside repeated texts,
`layout_offsets_owed_beside_named` beside a named `+00:00`,
`layout_offsets_owed_whole_texts`, step 5's, and
`layout_offsets_owed_across_offsets`, its aim and look ahead, the
oracle's `offsets_paid_to_the_classes` against the shipped
`_offsets_owed_by_the_classes`.

**What it leaves.** A run of figures whose every offset falls in one pool
(`{"(withheld)": n}`) is not paid: G7.4 writes the pooled ranks with no
offset at all, and the twin misses its count of cells that are not
numbers, as before this pass. Nor is a debt past `census_floor - 1`
times the offsets on offer -- 150 cells at a floor of 11 where the
census names none of the fifteen -- paid past that bound: 1,000 HL7
stamps, 180 of them in twenty offsets of nine, are paid 150 and miss
both counts (validate exits 3), as they did before this pass. Nor is a
rest that no choice of whole texts reaches beside any count of the texts
standing alone -- one cell owed where no number stands alone -- paid
past what they reach: those twins miss both class counts, 12 of the 180
above, each owing one to three cells beside texts of ten or twelve
copies. And step 5 places whole texts by its aim and its look ahead, not
by a search of every packing, so where the rest nears what the rooms on
offer hold together it can write a few cells fewer than some packing of
the same texts would: against an exact search over random shapes in
rank order with two or three offsets on offer, 7 of 2,724 fell short, by
11 cells in all, and with fifteen on offer owing 120 to 150, 2 of 300
fell short of the largest total their texts reach, by 3.

### G7.10 Dates written as counts: read exactly, written back as counts

Landing R4 (plan P4-D384; contract 6.6.2, dates written as counts). A
column named under `settings.forced_date_counts` was described as the
dates its counts name, so the twin draws it as dates by every rule of
G7 above, in the ISO text the description was made from; this section
says how that text is written back as the system's counts, and how a
count is read, which the validator's re-description repeats.

**Reading a count.** A cell the grammar of contract 6.6.2 takes as a
count -- with as many whole figures before an exponent as it writes,
`17e+8` and `1704067200e+0` among them (the Codex review of landing R4,
item 8) -- is its exact value: the whole figures and the figures after
the mark as one integer over a power of ten, times ten to the exponent
R's form writes, in lowest terms over ten. The redundant zeros go first
and the magnitude is asked before any number is built: a number past
ten to the thirtieth names no date in any system and is held there, one
nearer nought than ten to minus thirty, which reads its system's first
day at every unit, is held at ten to minus thirty-one, and every other
count is read to its last significant figure, in pieces past Python's
limit on integer text -- so `1e+9999` builds no number of its own
length, `45042.` with 4,301 zeros reads as 45042, and a serial written
forty places past the point just above a half-millisecond boundary
reads the later millisecond, each reading deciding as the exact number
would (item 7 and its verification; keeping thirty figures and one for
the rest read 355 of 385 such serials a millisecond early). Its moment is the system's first day plus that many units,
in whole nanoseconds; Excel's 1900 system counts serial 60 as no day,
reads 1 to 59 from 31 December 1899 and 61 onward from 30 December
1899, and reads no serial below 1. A `days-since-1840` count reads its
whole part alone, its figures after the point being a contact number,
and a cell of that system writing an exponent or more than nine figures
after the point is no count. The moment is settled to the unit U -- the
finest of the nanosecond, microsecond, millisecond, second, minute and
day that is at least the system's unit over ten to the most figures
after the mark any count read as a date writes (a count naming no date
or a moment of a placeholder day tells nothing of the form, nor of the
magnitude below: a lone `0` beside serials written `%.6f` made a trimmed
form before, which their own six places missed, and a lone `1e+15` a
binary64 step no unit kept; the verification of item 4), and NO FINER THAN
THE WRITER KEEPS -- by
rounding half to even. The writer spells a count that is not whole
through the binary64 nearest it, within two to the `b - 54` of the
system's unit of the exact count where every count stands below two to
the `b`, so U is at least the finest unit above two to the `b - 52` of
it, a bit spare for a tail (`date_counts.writer_keeps`): Excel serials
written to fourteen figures were settled to the nanosecond, and 999 of
1,000 moments handed to the writer read back as another; they settle to
the millisecond, Unix seconds to the microsecond at most, SPSS seconds
to the millisecond (the Codex review of landing R4, item 2). Only where
no unit holds every figure so (below) are the counts written with more
figures than the rest, at most one in a hundred of them and one at
least, the rest nine tenths, set aside as strays: U is then the usual
cells', each stray is held to its own last figure, and its moment is
written back in the usual form (the second review of landing R4, item
5; its verification: Excel date-times mostly at six-hour steps or at
midnight, written trimmed, whose few longer cells carry the time of
day, were refused while the strays were set aside first). So Excel's
`%.15g` serials, ten figures after the point and a step of 8.64
microseconds, settle to the millisecond, and `45386.3541666667` reads
as 08:30 exactly. A column of `%.15g` or `repr` figures settles from
the least precise cell, which writes the fewest figures after the point
past serial 10,000; `repr`'s seventeen figures, whose last two are the
double's tail, are tried first at fifteen figures' step and then at
each finer unit down to U. A unit at least the step is what lets the
twin's own cells read back as the moments it drew. Every count must
then be its column's own writing of the moment it was read as -- within
half the form's last figure and four binary64 steps of that moment's
exact count -- or the column is not read as counted dates at all
(contract NF115): one to three figures of a day, tenths of a second and
four figures of a day of moments off the whole minute keep a figure no
unit holds, and the first build, which settled them to the minute or
the second, lost those figures or wrote a twin that missed its own
description (the review of landing R4, item 2). A count naming 1
January 1900 or 31 December 9999, or its system's plain count for
either, is no value; so the days a count of the column holds no date on
-- both placeholder days, and on a column of Excel 1900 DATES 2 January
1900, the day pandas' count for 1 January, serial 2, names; on a column
of moments that serial names one instant, midnight of 2 January, and
every other moment of the day is a date (`date_counts.hole_words`) --
are holes of the column, which the description and the checker hold as
its absent spellings. On a column of dates the count pass offers none
of them and a cell written on one moves to a neighbouring day, and the
weekday pass holds each a hole, as it holds both placeholder days on a
column of moments (at this landing's integration beside landing 3b.D2:
1,000 SAS seconds across 1 January 1900, a Monday, came out of the
last pass below with seven Monday ranks on Sunday and missed the weekday
census at seed 0), and so do the hour pass, whose escape paid back
(G7.3g step 3) moves ranks by whole days, and G7.3i's joint day plan
(at batch 3's integration beside lanes J and D3; the reference's hour
and day passes always held them). NO TAIL
REACHES A WALL OF THEM: the
stretches beyond a tail's boundary the column's counts cannot hold --
either placeholder day, the day or the instant serial 2 names (on a
column of moments, the written unit's span of it), and on Excel's two
systems every moment before the system's first count -- are joined
where they touch (`date_counts.blocked_units`), and one running on to
the furthest unit the member's spelling writes, or to the calendar's
first or last day, is a WALL: the tail's reach is cut to one unit short
of the nearest (`date_counts.tail_reach`) -- Excel's days before its
first count with 1 January 1900 and serial 2 beside them, and 31
December 9999 -- so its end, its group and every rank drawn between
them stand inside it, and no source value stands beyond one. Any other
such stretch inside the reach is an ISLAND -- 1 January 1900, in a
system that writes the days either side of it -- and cuts nothing, for
a source's tail runs past it as often as not (`date_counts.tail_islands`):
the tail's end and its group, each one distance, step off it, inward
to the unit just inside it where that is a distance of one or more and
otherwise outward to the unit just beyond it (`off_the_islands`); a
rank whose stratum lies wholly on it, with m such ranks, is given a
stratum from m units inside it to m beyond it, and every stratum
is then kept no nearer than the one inside it and no further than the
one outside it (`stratum_off_the_islands`); step 9 offers no unit on
it. The validator draws its windows to the same reach and the same
strata. A last pass, after every other, moves any rank left on a hole
day to the nearest instant inside its own gap whose day is none of them
and that no rank holds -- a whole number of days away, its clock kept,
and where no whole day's move fits its gap, a whole number of the units
the column is written at away (a minute, or a second) -- and where every
such instant is held, the nearest one, in the same order. (The second
review of landing R4, item 2: a twin of Excel birth dates from 1900 drew
serial 1 on three seeds of three, read it back as no value and missed
its own count of present cells. Its verification: a tail of Excel
date-times from 1900, its end and group stepped off midnight of 1
January alone, kept a rank on that day inside a stratum less than a day
wide, which no whole day's move fits, and wrote its end before serial 1
as ISO text, on six seeds of six. The repair of that verification: a
reach cut at 1 January 1900 in SAS days drew none of a tail's eight
values before 1900, and a dense tail of SAS seconds piled onto the last
second it allowed missed both counts of different values.)

**Writing a moment.** Each cell G7 wrote as a date or moment is
written as its system's count of that moment: a whole count exactly,
from its integer; a count that is not whole through the binary64 value
nearest the exact one, formatted as the exporter the form names writes
it -- `places` figures after the mark, rounded half to even and kept
(`%.Nf`, pandas' `45000.0`) or trimmed (`%g`, R), fifteen or seventeen
significant figures trimmed (`%.15g`, `repr`, a whole count at
seventeen written as `repr` writes a whole double, `45123.0`), and R's
exponent form where it is shorter -- with the column's mark, a point or
a comma. R's rule writes an exponent only where it is the shorter, so a
column of whole counts written with a needless one, `1704067200e+0` or
`1704067200000e-3`, is held by its form and written back in full,
`1704067200`: the one spelling of such a column the twin does not keep
(the verification of the Codex review of landing R4, item 8), against
the owner's rule that every spelling comes back as written: owned by
lane L1, its item 2 (the orchestrator, 2026-10-13). A `days-since-1840` column writes its day count alone where
no census of contact numbers is published -- none reaching the line
(the second review of landing R4, item 1) -- and otherwise its day count
and, after the point, the contact number the census gives the cell,
EVENLY SPACED:
each word the census counts c times stands at the c keys (2j + 1) / (2c)
for j from nought -- the middles of c equal shares of the cells -- and
the dated cells, in the order they stand, take the words in the order
of their keys, compared exactly, a tie to the word ranked first (the
commonest, ties in sorted order), a cell past the census's last word
writing none. Each word is written exactly as often as the census
counts it, every stretch of the rows holds it within about one cell of
its share, and it is independent of the dates, which the arrangement
put in an order drawn at random; dealt in rank order down the rows, as
the first build did, the first half of a twin of 100,000 rows held no
contact number (the review of landing R4, item 8). A cell written in a
spelling the column publishes as absent -- a count that names no date,
a placeholder day -- and an unparsed stand-in are left as they are.

**What is frozen.** Generation reference vectors file 26 holds both
halves on cells either side of Excel's leap day, SAS and Stata days,
seconds and milliseconds before and after 1960, R's exponent form,
nanoseconds past 2**53, an Epic day with its contact number, a comma for
the point, SPSS seconds, Arrow's microseconds and R's days from 1970
each at a count worked out from the calendar, which the oracle asserts
before it writes (the Codex review of landing R4, item 9), fifteen
significant figures either side of serial 10,000, one
figure rounded half to even, six figures fixed and trimmed, R's shorter
form, a contact number, a comma, `repr`'s shortest figures and its
`45123.0`, four censuses of contact numbers dealt over the dated
cells, each system's holes and seven cases of the last pass off them;
`tests/test_stage3b_counted.py` holds the product to every answer and
turns each case red on its mutant (float arithmetic, a 1970 epoch for
1960, halves rounded up, untrimmed figures, no leap day, the exact value
where binary64 is written, the contact numbers dealt down the rows,
`%.17g` where `repr` is written, the last pass taking a day a rank
holds, and Excel's serial 2 no hole).

**Stated limits.** A date kept at local midnight is read as the instant
its count names, not as the day; contact numbers are not kept with
their dates; a column whose figures no unit keeps is not read as dates;
an unparsed cell of a column of counted dates is a text stand-in, as on
every column of dates, so a twin whose source holds numbers the date
role could not read misses `n_numeric`; and a workbook's clock cells
keep their binary64 reading, which moves 94 of them by a millisecond,
rather than this one.

### G7.13 Dates and times pooled in people: drawn inside their grain, and the G1 floor

Lane PS (plan P4-D417; contract NF128, NF129 and TG1). A column of dates,
stamps, clock times or counted dates beside a person column that the
count in people (plan P4-D406) would hold is either DESCRIBED AT A GRAIN
-- its cells written as the starts of their buckets, the tails pooled
into the first and the last bucket the floor's number of people hold, and
that column described by its role's own rules -- or HELD, as a record
number, with the record its twin writes valid values from. Either way its
block carries `time_grain` (contract NF128, NF129): `rung` (a rung or
`held`), `finest` (the column's own precision), `kind` (`date`, `stamp`,
`clock`, `counted`), `reading` (the date member, clock form or counting
member its cells read under), `mark`, `rows`, `people` and `spans`.

The twin is built from the block by every rule of its role -- G7 to G7.10
for dates, G7A for clocks, G8 where the coarse cells took one or two
values and the constant or binary role, G9 for a held record number --
and MEASURED as built, against the description it was built from. Then,
as the decimal comma of G6 is applied, only the cells that LEAVE move,
with the third stage's words (G4.2), word `r` for row `r`:

**A pooled column (a rung).** A cell that is absent -- empty, or a
spelling the column publishes among its holes -- leaves as written. Every
other cell is read under the record's reading; one that does not read
leaves as written. Its moment `t` names a bucket `[s, e)` at the rung:
`s` the start of `t`'s year (1 January), quarter (its first month's
first day), month (its first day), day (midnight), block of four hours
(00, 04, 08, 12, 16 or 20 hours), hour, minute or second, and `e` the
next bucket's start, a clock's never past the end of its day. The cell's
own precision gives the step `u`: a day for a date, a month for
`iso-month`, a quarter for `year-quarter`; for a stamp its finest field
-- the hour, the minute, the second, or ten to the minus `k` seconds for
`k` figures of a fraction; a clock form's own step; for a counted date
its member's unit over ten to the figures after its mark. With `c` the
steps in `[s, e)` (the months or quarters in it, for those two), a cell
with `c` at most one leaves as written; otherwise the target is `s` plus
`bounded(word_r, c)` steps (G3.4b), and the cell is written AGAIN IN ITS
OWN FORM naming it: a clock by its form's one spelling (G7A.1), a
counted date by its member's count with the cell's own figures after the
mark (G7.10), and a date or stamp field by field over the cell's own runs
of figures and letters, assigned by the member's own order (a layout's by
its items; a layout holding a field no run rule writes -- a weekday, a
month's name, a spaced field -- is written by the layout's own writer of
G7.5 at the first width word that writes the cell's form and reads back)
-- each field at the width its run shows (one figure stays
one, an opening zero stays padded; a run of two figures that shows
neither is padded unless the cell writes some field with one figure), a
month's name at its own length and case, the marker of the half of the
day by the new hour, and every other character, the offset's included,
as written. Where the cell so written does not read back under the
member as the target at the cell's precision, with the same offset, the
cell leaves as written. A STAMP LEAVES WITH ITS COLUMN'S ONE JOINT: where
the block's `datetime_separators` names one mark and no withheld pool, a
drawn stamp whose eleventh character is another joint (`T`, `t` or a
space) -- one the build took to reach the column's count of different
values (G7.9), which a value drawn inside its bucket no longer needs --
leaves wearing the named mark, where it still reads. The bucket the twin's
cell falls in is the one its built cell named, so the twin, read at the grain, is the twin as
built and meets the description as the build was measured -- but for the
count of different values, which G7.9 builds at the column's own
precision, so two built values may share one bucket.

**The count at the rung** (`grains.count_filled`; `generation._filled_to_the_count`).
Before the draw, where the built cells fall in fewer buckets than the
block's `n_distinct`, rows move to EMPTY buckets, each written as its new
bucket's start in the cell's own form. A row moves only between the same
two published points -- the buckets the ladder's rungs, the tails'
boundaries and values and the heavy dates name, and the span's ends --
and only to a bucket whose census key is its donor's: none on a clock; any
on a column written to the month or coarser; the weekday at a rung of the
month or coarser; the weekday, the day of the month and the time of day at
the day or finer. Donors, stretch by stretch from the earliest: buckets no
point names holding two rows or more, fullest first (ties earlier), each
giving its last rows first; then the rung just below the stretch, giving
its last rows while every rank it is published at (taxonomy's rank
`((n - 1) * num) // den` over the present rows) stays inside it; then the
rung just above, giving its first rows on the same terms. A bucket a heavy
date, a tail (its boundary or one of its values) or a span's end names
gives none, and no stretch at or below the low tail's boundary, or at or
above the high tail's, moves a row (repair round 2 of lane PS, Codex's
item 2: a boundary the p05 rank also held once gave a row of 1982 to
1981, a tail of 31 rows against 30). Each row goes to the
earliest empty bucket of its key, until the count is met or no move is
left. So every published point keeps its rank, every tail and heavy date
its rows and every census at the rung its counts; no word is drawn. The
oracle's `pooled_count_filled` holds the product to it.

**A held column (rung `held`): the G1 floor.** The spans are the
record's, deepest first, each from its first bucket's start to the start
after its last bucket (a clock's never past its day), and then the
method's FIXED SPAN, 1 January 2000 to 31 December 2029 (a clock: its
whole day) -- never the table -- WIDENED BY WHOLE DECADES (repair round
3 of lane PS, the second verify's item 2), its last year 2039, 2049 and
so on, never past 9999, until its buckets at the column's finest written
detail (the record's `finest`: a month for `%Y-%m`) number at least
twice the column's published count of different values (`n_distinct`;
the made-up cells' own count where the block names none) -- room for the
walk of at most 4,000 steps below to find a value no earlier made-up
value took (a span exactly as wide left 600 birth months 582 and 583
different at seeds 0 and 1). THE CAPACITY IS RESOLVED FIRST (repair
round 2 of lane PS, Codex's item 1; measured at the finest written
detail since repair round 3, where it was days): the walk below starts
in the first of them whose buckets at the record's `finest` number at
least that count, and a made-up cell that span cannot take walks the
next, and so on; where none can take it unrepeated it takes a value an
earlier made-up cell took in the last (a valid value, the count of
different values then named short: reached by no description the
profiler writes once the fixed span is widened, and kept as the floor's
last guard), and only a member this
step does not write leaves a made-up cell as made up, named in the
twin's report (eight different values against a deepest span of one day
had left 875 of 1,000 cells as stand-ins). The DIFFERENT made-up cells of
the column (G9), in the order of the rows each first stands on, each take
one value, and every row holding that made-up cell writes it. A made-up
cell's runs are read by the member's own order from its layout alone:
each run of figures is the field the member writes there, and a run of
letters by where it stands -- one letter between the date and the clock
a joint, written `T` in its case; two after the clock a marker of the
half of the day; one after the clock a zulu letter, `Z`; three, `UTC`.
The step `u` is a day, an hour where the layout writes an hour, a minute
where it writes minutes and a second where it writes seconds; with `c`
the steps in the span, the walk starts at the span's first moment plus
`bounded(word, c)` steps, with the word of the row the made-up cell first
stands on, and steps forward (from the span's end back to its start) --
to the next day where the month, the day or the month's name cannot fill
its run, to the next hour where the hour cannot -- to the first moment
every field of which fills its run at the run's width (one figure: below
ten; two: any value, or ten and more where some made-up cell of the
column writes that field with one figure), whose cell, written with its
offset's figures as noughts and its fraction as the moment's own
figures, reads under the member and is no value an earlier made-up cell
took; at most 4,000 steps. A counted member steps by days and writes its
member's count with the made-up cell's figures after the mark, taken
only where it is as long as the made-up cell; a layout no run rule
writes is filled by the layout's own writer, by days (by steps of 3,607
seconds where it has a clock), at most 64 steps, at the first moment it
writes in the made-up cell's very form. THE MEMBER'S OWN FORM (repair
round 1 of lane PS): a made-up cell none of these fills -- a stand-in of
a withheld layout (`A-------AZ`), which no date wears -- walks again
from the same start, by days (by steps of 3,607 seconds where the member
writes a clock, of 61 of its own steps for a clock time), to the first
moment no earlier made-up cell took, written in the member's own form
(`parsing.written_date`, alone or with ` HH:MM`, ` HH:MM:SS` or
`THH:MM:SS` after it, and the date with each two-figure field opening
with a nought written with one figure, alone and together -- repair
round 2; a layout's writer at each width; a clock's one
spelling; a count at no figures after the mark) that reads under the
member (an ISO date column may take an ISO stamp, as its source's
unread cells were): first one as long as the made-up cell and on its
side of the code alphabet (`parsing.is_code_text`), then one on its side
alone, 384 steps each, then any, 20,000 steps. Where the made-up values
then leave the column without its longest or its shortest made-up
length, the first made-up value of that length (in the order of the
rows) walks once more from its own start for one as long as it, whatever
its side, and takes it in place of its first value. So the held column
keeps every layout, every width and the census of repetition its block
publishes (two made-up values never take one) wherever a date can wear
them, and every value parses under its member. A PUBLISHED LAYOUT NO
DATE WEARS (repair round 2, the combined verify's item 2): a made-up
cell whose layout the held block names (not its withheld pool) and that
no value of the member can wear in that very form (`grains.wears_a_date`:
the field and layout walks over the fixed span find none) -- twelve
people's `pending` beside ISO dates -- stands for real cells that do not
read either, and leaves as made up, so the layout census and its lengths
hold. A length the block withholds the form of and no valid value of the
member wears (three people's `pending`, seven characters; one cell `x`)
is the G1 floor's price: the twin misses that `min_length` or
`max_length` and its report says why.

**What is measured.** The twin's report and its approximations are
measured on the cells AS THEY LEAVE, read as the validator reads them
(validation V14; repair round 2 of lane PS, Codex's item 4): a pooled
column's at its rung (`grains.coarse_cells`), so a row the count at the
rung moved is counted where it went, and a held column's as written, so
a length its valid dates do not keep is named (before, the report read
the made-up cells and named none). The oracle (`tools/reference/
make_generation_reference_vectors.py`, `pooled_drawn_inside`) writes the
pooled draw from these words for ISO dates and stamps, padded US and
day-first dates, padded 24-hour clocks and Excel's whole serials, and
`tests/test_dates_pooled_in_people.py` holds the product to it word for
word. No frozen vector moves: no description of the vectors carries the
key.

**Stated limits.** A stamp's offset is written as it was, so a value
drawn across a change of daylight saving can wear an offset not in force
on its new date (lane DST's limit, as before); a member whose cells this
method cannot write again -- `days-since-1840` with its contact numbers,
a layout the day of the year rules -- is held whole, and a made-up cell of
such a member leaves as written; a column whose two-figure
fields mix padded and unpadded cells writes a field that showed neither
as padded.

## G7A. Clock columns (`time_of_day`)

This role was added by Phase 4 and this section was written after its
implementation shipped, which is the wrong order and is recorded as
such in G13. It is written from the behaviour the shipped tool has, so
that an independent implementer can reproduce it; it is not evidence
that the behaviour was reviewed before it existed.

### G7A.1 The ordinal space

A clock column holds TIMES OF DAY and nothing else: no date, no zone,
no offset. Each cell is a place in one day, and the role counts in
**integer ordinals** of the form's own unit. No float is formed
anywhere in G7A.

| form | unit | capacity | spelling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hh-mm` | minutes of day | 1,440 | `HH:MM` |
| `hh-mm-ss` | seconds of day | 86,400 | `HH:MM:SS` |

**SINCE LANDING T1 THOSE ARE TWO OF FORTY** (plan P4-D370, contract
C6-10a): a width `hh` or `h` (one figure below ten), `-mm` or `-mm-ss`,
and a face -- the 24-hour clock, the declared 12-hour face (` twelve-hour`,
whose `12` is the first hour and whose capacity is half a day), or a
marker pair after one space or none. The ordinal is the minute or second
of the day on that face; the spelling writes the hour at the form's
width, `hours % 12` with 12 in place of 0 on a 12-hour face, the marker's
morning word below noon and its evening word from noon on. Every ordinal
in `[0, capacity)` still has exactly one spelling, and ranks are ordered
by ordinal, never by text. The reader below admits these forms; what it
refuses beyond the shapes refused below is `24:00`, a marked hour of 0 or past 12,
`Am`, a one-letter marker, and a marker after two spaces or a no-break
space.

The ordinal of a cell is `hours * 60 + minutes` for `hh-mm` and
`hours * 3600 + minutes * 60 + seconds` for `hh-mm-ss`, the hour read on
the form's face for the other thirty-eight. The spelling of an ordinal
is that map inverted, the minutes and seconds in two digits and the
hour at the form's width as the paragraph above writes it. Because the unit is the form's own, every ordinal in
`[0, capacity)` has exactly one spelling in that form, and no value the
generator interpolates is ever truncated or widened to fit a cell.

**What the reader accepts is EXACTLY the forty forms**, and the word
exactly is the rule rather than a summary of it: two ASCII digits in
the minute and second fields, the hour in two figures or, below ten,
one, at most 23 unmarked and 1 to 12 marked, minutes and seconds at
most 59, the marker as the paragraph above admits it, and nothing
before the digits and nothing after. Before landing T1 it was exactly
the two shapes of the table, and an hour written with one digit such as
`9:30` was refused; it is read since, the column keeping one width
(contract C6-10a), and a consumer that refuses `9:30` or orders
`9:30 AM` after `1:00 PM` by its text is not following this method
(the T1 review's item 11). Three shapes a reader might expect are
refused on purpose — a fractional part (a reading that dropped it
would describe such a cell approximately while publishing an exact
ladder), the leap second `23:59:60` (the ordinal space has no faithful
point for it, and making one up would write into the twin a time that
no clock face reaches), and anything else — a date, an offset, a
name.

**Nothing is trimmed before the reader looks**, and that is a fourth
refusal rather than an oversight. What this role publishes are the
CELLS THEMSELVES: the two endpoints and the eleven ladder rungs are
values some row held, written in the column's form -- character for
character as the row wore it, but for a cell whose hour shows the other
width, which is written in the column's (contract C6-10a, NF109). A
cell of another precision, or on another face, is counted unparsed
rather than silently re-read, so a column of `hh-mm` cells with one
`hh-mm-ss` cell among them publishes `n_unparsed` of 1.

### G7A.2 What the profile supplies

Published: `clock_form`; the 11-rung `clock_percentiles` ladder;
`earliest`; `latest`; `n_unparsed`; together with the universal class
counts and `n_distinct` / `n_distinct_folded`. **This role publishes no
sixth key.** It has NO OFFSET MACHINERY AND MAY NOT INVENT ANY: the
datetime role's ten offset and resolution keys are absent here, so
there is no zone to carry, no reading to convert and no endpoint field
surgery. A clock time is a place in the day and nothing else.

The loader holds the published values to four rules before the
generator sees them: every published time wears the column's own form
(T1); the ladder begins at `earliest` and ends at `latest` (T2); the
ladder never goes backwards (T3); and at least one cell parsed (T4). A
fifth (T5) is the detection line — enough of the column's cells are
clock times for it to be read this way.

Fixed quantity used below:

```
P = n_present - n_unparsed        cells that parsed as clock times
```

### G7A.3 The one refusal this role adds

A day holds 1,440 different minutes and 86,400 different seconds -- the
declared 12-hour face half of each (G7A.1) -- and nothing else can be
written in the column's form. So where

```
n_distinct - n_unparsed  >  capacity(clock_form)
```

the description asks for more different times than its form has, and
generation REFUSES before a single cell exists, naming the description
valid and the table impossible. The test is the FORM'S CAPACITY and not
the span between the two endpoints: a description whose own source met
every count is never refused here, which is the difference between a
description nothing can satisfy and one this method finds hard.

**The span is a separate matter and is not a refusal.** Where the
endpoints are close together and the column asks for many different
values, the form has room but the RANGE does not, and G7A.4's repair
runs out of places. Nothing is silently dropped: the twin holds fewer
different times than published and the generation report names the
shortfall as a deviation of `n_distinct`, alongside every ladder rung
the clamp moved. Measured on a forged 100-cell `hh-mm` column whose
ends were `08:00` and `08:10` -- eleven minutes for a hundred different
values -- the twin held 11 different times, reported a deviation of
`n_distinct` reading 11, and reported 8 of the 11 rungs moved.

**A description the PROFILER wrote can never have that shape**, and the
reason is worth stating because it tells an implementer exactly when
the clamp can bite. Write `lo` and `hi` for the ordinals of `earliest`
and `latest`. Every parsed cell is a clock time between those two
endpoints, so the number of DIFFERENT parsed cells is at most
`hi - lo + 1`. And `n_unparsed` counts unparsed CELLS while `n_distinct`
counts each unparsed spelling once, so `n_unparsed` is at least the
number of different unparsed spellings, and therefore

```
n_distinct - n_unparsed  <=  (different parsed cells)  <=  hi - lo + 1
```

on every description measured from a real column. The repair always has
a place to step into there.

The inequality is necessary and, on its own, not quite sufficient: it
bounds how many different times are wanted, and the repair also needs
the interpolation not to jump past them. That second half comes from
the ladder being a SELECTION ladder over the column's own values
(G7A.2, invariants T2 and T3), so its rungs are real cells in order and
the interpolation between two rungs stays between two values the column
held. With both halves the conclusion holds, and no profiler path was
found that breaks either. The clamp is reachable only from a
HAND-WRITTEN description, which this method accepts and must therefore
say what it does with -- and what it does is degrade and report, never
refuse and never quietly hold fewer. Sixty profiler-built clock columns
were checked against the inequality and none came within reach of it;
the inequality is the reason, and the check is only corroboration.

This is why G7A.3's first paragraph does not say the capacity test
guarantees a place for every value. It does not: it guarantees the FORM
has room, not that the RANGE does. Only the report closes that gap.

### G7A.4 Values: the tails, and the body between their boundaries

*Amended at stage 3 (plan P4-D328): a column of clock times publishes no
earliest and no latest value either, so its two ends belong to its two
tails and its body runs between the two published boundaries.*

The cells are ranks `r = 0 .. P - 1`, one cell per rank; clock columns
are not stratified by value, because no clock multiplicity map is
published. With `m_lo = low_tail.rows` and `m_hi = P - 1 -
high_tail.rows`, in the form's own unit -- minutes of the day for a
`-mm` form, seconds for a `-mm-ss` form, on the form's face:

- `r < m_lo` or `r > m_hi`: a TAIL rank, placed by G7.3b in this unit
  (or by G7.3c where the tail publishes its values), against the day's
  own ends: nothing beyond `00:00` below and nothing beyond the last
  minute or second above (G7.3e in this space).
- `r == m_lo`: the cell is `low_tail.boundary`; `r == m_hi`:
  `high_tail.boundary`, each the published TEXT, not a re-spelling of
  its ordinal -- unless that text is a spelling the table calls absent,
  when the cell is written as a present time on an absent place is
  (below).
- otherwise: the body, interpolated between the KNOTS -- the low
  boundary at position `m_lo`, each PUBLISHED rung `j` at position
  `P * PCT[j] / 100`, and the high boundary at position `m_hi + 1`,
  every position counted in hundredths of a rank times `2**64` so that a
  rank reading one word `w` stands at `100 * (r * 2**64 + w)`. A rung
  the tail rule withholds is not a knot. Let `(p0, v0)` and `(p1, v1)`
  be the two knots the rank's own position falls between, the last pair
  where it passes the end:

  ```
  share   = min(max(position - p0, 0), p1 - p0)
  ordinal = v0 + (share * (v1 - v0)) // (p1 - p0)        (v1 where p1 <= p0)
  ```

  identical in shape to G7.3's segment reading. The floor division
  rounds toward the EARLIER time, and `ordinal` lies between the two
  boundaries by construction, so no body cell falls into either tail.

**EVERY INTERIOR RANK READS ONE WORD, AS IT ALWAYS HAS.** A clock
column is handed `P - 2` content words and spends them in rank order;
rank `0` and rank `P - 1` draw none. A boundary rank and a tail's group
READ their word and set it aside, so every body rank keeps the word it
read before stage 3 and no column generated after this one moves
(G3, G4). A column with no tails at all spreads its ranks evenly over
its count of different values from `00:00` (the ramp of G7.3d), each
interior rank still reading and discarding its word.

**The all-different obligation is EXACT for this role**, and it is the
one shape where it is. Everywhere else a column's count of different
values falls to an envelope; here a closed finite space of times has a
place for each of them and the construction can take the next one. The
obligation applies where

```
n_distinct - n_unparsed  >=  P
```

and the repair is: in the BODY, keep the ordinal of the previous rank;
if this rank's ordinal is not above it, step to the previous ordinal
plus one; then clamp to one unit below the high boundary. In a TAIL it
is the two-pass step of G7.3b step 5: from the innermost rank outward,
a distance not above the one inside it is raised to that distance plus
one and then kept at the edge; then, from the outermost rank inward,
a distance not below the one outside it is lowered to that distance less
one, never below one unit. **The clamp runs inside BOTH passes**: with
the clamp applied only after the first, the ranks piled up at `00:00`
and `23:59` and 7 of 20 twins of an all-different column repeated a
value its description publishes as different (the skeptic of the tail
design, B5). The real column fits, because its own `m` values stood
between the day's edge and the boundary.

**AND NO PARSED CELL WEARS A SPELLING THE TABLE CALLS ABSENT.** The
ranks come out of the layout, which knows nothing about the spellings
this document's columns publish among their absent cells, so a rank can
land on one -- and the twin then writes a cell its own reader counts as
no value at all, one more absent cell and one fewer present one. After
the ranks are placed and before any cell is spelled, each BODY rank --
one strictly between the two tail boundaries -- whose spelling is one of
those is moved to the NEAREST unit of the window it was built in
(G12.10 above) that is not one of them, earlier before later at one
distance, and -- on a column whose values were all different -- one no
other rank stands on, so G11 survives the step. A boundary rank and a
tail rank do not move: the first stands at a value the description
prints and the second at a distance the published shape fixes, and a
twin that moved either would miss a published fact to keep a count. Nor
does a body rank whose window is one unit, which is a body with no slack
left in it. On an eligible column (layer L0, G7A.4d) the window is cut
to the rank's piece, and a rank that finds no unit there stays where it
stands, as a rank whose window is one unit stays. The search passes at most one unit per absent spelling and,
where the ranks must differ, one per rank. *On a column laid by G7A.4b
(the round-2 fix of landing 3b.5)* no rank of a run or of a drawn tail
is left on a place a spelling the table calls absent names: a run whose
every step is one takes no cell (G7A.4b step 2), a rank of another run
moves off it (step 4), and a tail drawn through its shape skips their
distances (step 1), so a tail rank still never moves and none lands
there -- save the places the hour's other width spells another way
that a group or a drawn tail has nothing but absent places beside,
whose cells are written in that width (below; G7A.4b steps 1 and 2).

*Added by the dates pass of the stage-3 review, item 5.* The stand-ins
of G7A.5 were stepped past the absent spellings from the day the role
landed and the clock VALUES were checked against nothing. Measured at a
floor of eleven: 99 minutes two apart from `07:00` with `08:00` declared
missing and held by eleven cells wrote TWELVE `08:00` cells at seed 0,
leaving 98 present against a published 99 and 12 absent against 11, at
seeds 0, 3 and 7. There are enough free minutes to keep both the
absent count and the uniqueness, and the step above takes one.

**AND A PRESENT TIME PUBLISHED ON AN ABSENT PLACE IS WRITTEN AS ITS
SOURCE WROTE IT.** Where a place a spelling the table calls absent names
(G7A.4b step 1) is one the description stands present cells on -- a
heap's value, a tail's boundary or listed value, a published rung, such
a place in a census group whose every step is an absent place (G7A.4b
step 2), or such a place beyond a drawn tail's boundary whose every
step on no heap is an absent place (step 1) -- the table held present
cells there, and the form's own
spelling of that
place is one the column's reader counts as no value. So those cells can
only have shown the hour's OTHER width, the one other spelling that
reader reads at that place -- `0:00` in a column of `hh:mm` beside
`00:00` declared missing -- and every rank standing there is written in
it (`calendar_clock.present_spellings`), as its source wrote it. Where
the hour shows no width (`10` to `23`, and `12` on a marked face) the
two spellings are one, and the form's own is written. A place the
description stands nothing present on keeps the form's own spelling
too: the construction keeps its ranks off such a place where it can
(the step above; G7A.4b steps 1, 2 and 4), and a cell it could not move
is not given a spelling the table may never have held. Every other cell
is the form's own spelling of its ordinal, and NF109's remark says both:
a cell of the other width is written in the column's, save these, which
keep their own.

*Added by the verification of the round-2 fix of landing 3b.5.* A
ten-minute grid in `hh:mm` holding 15 real times at midnight written
`0:00` beside 20 cells of `00:00` declared missing publishes a heap of
15 and a listed low tail on `00:00`, the form's spelling of that place,
and every twin wrote all 35 cells `00:00` and MISSED eleven checks at
seeds 0 to 2, at d4f5ee4 and at baaf9de alike, where the table
validates; laid by G7A.4 its twins MISSED twelve or thirteen, and a
second column holding those times beside another column's `00:00`
nine, or eleven laid by G7A.4. Laid either way the column now writes 15
`0:00` and 20 `00:00`, the second column 15 `0:00` and no `00:00`, and
no twin misses anything. So do a heap of 30 `8:00` beside `08:00`
declared missing (55 `08:00` before, eight MISSED), a low boundary on
`7:00` beside `07:00` (one `07:00` too many, six MISSED) and a fifth
percentile on `5:00`, pinned in its run, beside `05:00` (one too many,
five MISSED). And a quarter-hour grid writing 20 `1:15` beside 15
`01:15` declared missing, the only step of its census group, had its
producer's own description refused under CC5 at baaf9de -- "this file
has been changed since it was written" -- where at d4f5ee4 it loaded
and every twin wrote 35 `01:15` and MISSED eleven checks; it now loads
and its twins write 20 `1:15` and 15 `01:15`. Of this repair's own 80
such columns (seed 71), 40 MISSED at every seed at baaf9de and two had
their description refused; none now.

### G7A.4b The rank rule: a census, heaps, a step and codes (landing 3b.5)

*Added by landing 3b.5 (lane C1, plan P4-D373).* A block publishing a
`clock_step` is laid by this section; a block publishing none -- every
description written before it -- by G7A.4, byte for byte as before.
With `k` the step in the form's own unit and every distance and place
below on that step:

1. **The tails.** An ABSENT PLACE is a time a spelling the table calls
   absent names in the column's form -- a key of its own
   `missing_by_source` or of any other column's, since a declaration
   reaches the whole table and the checker reads it so: one that reads
   as a time there and is, trimmed and case-folded, the form's own
   spelling of that time (`calendar_clock.absent_places`). A tail listing its values
   and holding no heap, or holding no heap on a step of one unit with no
   absent place beyond its boundary, is placed as G7A.4 places it (G7.3b,
   G7.3c). A
   tail LISTING its values gives each heap's value its count and the rows
   left to the other values by G7.3c, against the sum its mean fixes less
   the heaps'. A tail drawn through its shape keeps its heaps' cells on
   their values and draws the rest by G7.3b IN STEPS: its rows, mean and
   root-mean-square less the heaps' (`calendar_clock.tail_less_heaps`),
   each distance divided by `k`, its edge in steps less the heaps'
   distances and the absent places' on the step inside it
   (`calendar_clock.absent_beyond`); each drawn distance `d` is read back
   past both (`calendar_clock.off_the_heaps`: one step further for each
   at or before it) and times `k`. So no drawn cell stands off the step,
   on a heap or on a spelling the column calls absent, and every heap
   keeps its count -- save where EVERY step beyond the boundary on no
   heap is an absent place. The rows the heaps leave stood in the table,
   present, on those the hour's other width spells another way
   (`calendar_clock.absent_with_another_width`), in that width -- as a
   census group's cells do on such places alone (step 2) -- and never
   on one whose hour shows no width; so those are then the draw's room
   (`calendar_clock.absent_room_beyond`) -- its edge less the heaps'
   distances and the other absent places', each drawn distance read
   back past those alone -- and each cell drawn there is written in
   that width (G7A.4). The tail's cells, heaps and drawn ones together,
   stand at its ranks in order.

   *Amended by the third verification of the round-2 fix of landing
   3b.5.* Skipped as every absent place is, those steps left a drawn
   tail no room, and CC5 refused the producer's own description: 70
   `00:30` and one `0:00` beyond a low boundary at `01:00`, beside 40
   `00:00` declared missing, left its one drawn row no step inside the
   dial, so generate and the checker of the real table exited 1 at every
   seed and the table had no twin; 12 of this repair's 1,500 random tables of clock
   columns were refused so at 05eeeb9, every one on a low tail. Its
   twins now write 40 `00:00` and the one `0:00` and miss nothing; and
   so do the twins of one `01:00 AM` beyond a heap on `2:00 AM`, beside
   `1:00 AM` and `12:00 AM` declared missing, where the draw stands on
   `1:00 AM` alone, `12`'s hour showing no width.
2. **The body's stretches** (`calendar_clock.clock_body_blocks`). From
   rank `m_lo` (nought with no tails), in ordinal order: each heap
   between the boundaries is a stretch of its count on its value; each
   census group counting `n` cells takes its steps inside the body and
   on no heap, cut by the heaps inside it into RUNS, and run `j` takes

   ```
   f_j + floor(r * U<=j / U) - floor(r * U<j / U)
   ```

   of them (`calendar_clock.run_shares`), `U` the group's steps on no
   absent place, `U<=j` and `U<j` those through and before run `j` -- so
   a run whose every step is an absent place takes no cell, save in a
   group whose every step on no heap is an absent place: the table held
   that group's cells, present, on those the hour's other width spells
   another way (`calendar_clock.absent_with_another_width`), in that
